## 2026-10-09 — Coconut Llama-3.2-1B: reproduction gate + E3 twin transplant (coconut, run_id: 20261009-094526_coconut_llama1b-minimal-pair-patch)

**Goal:** Same as the paired CODI run (`20261009-102724_codi_llama1b-minimal-pair-patch`): (1) reproduction gate
for the released Llama-3.2-1B Coconut checkpoint; (2) does the GPT-2 E3 twin transplant
(`20260927-003331_coconut_minimal-pair-patch-full`: all-slot 0.827, value in passes 1 and 4) hold on Llama?
Same script, same caps.
**Mechanism / model:** `coconut`, backbone `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct@5a8abab` (tokenizer patched to Meta's
defaults) + `connordilgren/llama32-1b-gsm8k-coconut@49dc864/checkpoint_10`, 6 latent passes.
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test, gold-trace set n=1194 (same filter as the GPT-2 run).
**Hyperparams:** Coconut env pins (torch 2.5.1, transformers 4.46.2), greedy; pair caps 1000 / 300; deltas ±1..3.
**Command:** `eval_command.txt`. Code change: `coconut_common.finish_and_decode` also stops on `<|eot_id|>`,
as the reference `Coconut.generate` does for Llama (GPT-2 behaviour unchanged).
**Headline results:**
- **Gate passes:** base accuracy **0.364** vs 0.357 in Dilgren & Wiegreffe Table 1 (Coconut paper 0.453 used
  a different setup). Loaded with missing=0 unexpected=0.
- Twin transplant, n=232 qualified pairs:

| pass | single | leave-one-out | prefix 0..p | GPT-2 single / LOO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **0.190** | **0.159** | 0.190 | 0.013 / 0.818 |
| 1 | 0.147 | 0.211 | 0.194 | 0.558 / 0.398 |
| 2 | 0.091 | 0.211 | 0.203 | 0.000 / 0.827 |
| 3 | 0.056 | 0.211 | 0.207 | 0.026 / 0.818 |
| 4 | 0.017 | 0.211 | 0.211 | 0.338 / 0.628 |
| 5 | 0.009 | 0.211 | 0.216 | 0.004 / 0.784 |
| **ALL-SLOT** | **0.216** [0.167, 0.273] (changed 0.293) | | | 0.827 [0.773, 0.870] |

- Non-responsive pairs (n=215): all-slot moves the recipient to the twin's wrong answer 0.102 [0.069, 0.150]
  (GPT-2 0.489).
- CFR: 232/447 = 0.519 [0.473, 0.565] (GPT-2 0.559); P(twin correct | original wrong) = 0.082.

**Interpretation:** **The Coconut transplant result does not port.** Replacing all six continuous thoughts with
the twin's changes the answer in only 29% of pairs and steers it to the twin's answer in 22% (GPT-2: 83%).
Whatever steering there is comes almost entirely from pass 0. Passes 1–5 add ~2.5 pp in the prefix curve, and
leaving any of passes 1–5 out costs nothing. The answer is mostly determined by the question tokens, which the
answer positions can still attend to. That fits two readings, which this run cannot yet separate:
(a) Llama-1B Coconut does most of its computation outside the latents (latents mostly unused, a known worry
for Coconut at scale), or (b) the value is in the latents but redundantly re-derivable from the question, so
overwriting them is "corrected". The decisive control is ablation: zero or mean-replace all latents and check
whether accuracy drops. If it barely moves, (a) holds.
This makes the Q1/Q3 picture method-dependent across families: CODI's finding ports (0.84 → 0.69), Coconut's does not (0.83 → 0.22).
**Gotchas hit:** without the `<|eot_id|>` stop, generation runs past the answer turn. The smoke test caught it
only indirectly; checking `finish_and_decode` against the reference generate did.
**Caveats:** single seed, greedy. Different pair sets per model. Before trusting the null, confirm with the ablation
control above. A pass-indexing bug is unlikely, since it is the same code that gives the GPT-2 table and the
checkpoint loads cleanly with gate accuracy matching the paper, but the ablation would also expose one.
**Next:** latent-ablation control on Llama Coconut (cheap: one decode pass, ~6 min); then the Q2 decode control.

## 2026-10-09 — CODI Llama-3.2-1B: reproduction gate + E3 twin transplant (codi, run_id: 20261009-102724_codi_llama1b-minimal-pair-patch)

**Goal:** First cross-family check. (1) Reproduction gate: does the released Llama-3.2-1B CODI checkpoint
reproduce the paper's GSM8K-Aug accuracy under our eval code? (2) Does the GPT-2 E3 minimal-pair (twin)
transplant result (aligned all-slot 0.839, value on z0/z2/z4; `20260927-004340_codi_minimal-pair-patch-aligned`)
hold on a different, 8x larger model family? The design is identical to the GPT-2 run: same script, same caps
and same aligned site convention (patch site s as `{s+1: twin z_s}`).
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, backbone `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct@5a8abab` (ungated mirror of
`meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`; tokenizer/config patched to Meta's defaults: no pad token,
PreTrainedTokenizerFast, no pad_token_id) + `connordilgren/llama32-1b-gsm8k-codi@5f670c7` (Dilgren & Wiegreffe
release), compute_steps=6.
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test, full n=1319; run seed=11.
**Hyperparams:** bf16, LoRA r=128 alpha=32 on q/k/v/o/up/down/gate_proj, prj_dim=2048, num_latent=6, greedy;
pair caps 1000 / non-responsive cap 300; deltas ±1..3.
**Command:** see `eval_command.txt` (run from `/workspace/codi` with the CODI env; `--model_name_or_path
/workspace/llama32-1b-instruct --ckpt_dir /workspace/codi_llama --prj_dim 2048 --eval_n 0 --n_pairs 1000
--n_nonresponsive 300`). Code changes needed: `eval_codi.build_model` picks LoRA targets by family;
`patch_minimal_pair_codi.py` records the real backbone.
**Headline results:**
- **Gate passes:** base accuracy **0.566** (746/1319) vs 0.560 in Dilgren & Wiegreffe Table 1 (CODI paper 0.556).
  Checkpoint loaded with missing=0 unexpected=0.
- Twin transplant, n=471 qualified pairs:

| condition | Llama-1B matches_twin | changed | GPT-2 (n=317) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ALL-SLOT aligned** | **0.692** [0.649, 0.732] | 0.828 | 0.839 [0.795, 0.875] |
| ALL-SLOT legacy | 0.594 | 0.773 | 0.713 |

| site | single | leave-one-out | prefix z0..s | GPT-2 single / LOO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| z0 | 0.000 | 0.699 | 0.000 | 0.199 / 0.729 |
| z1 | **0.384** | **0.251** | 0.384 | 0.003 / 0.839 |
| z2 | 0.028 | 0.686 | 0.467 | 0.202 / 0.659 |
| z3 | 0.000 | 0.696 | 0.469 | 0.000 / 0.836 |
| z4 | **0.217** | **0.482** | 0.667 | 0.360 / 0.546 |
| z5 | 0.004 | 0.667 | 0.692 | 0.000 / 0.842 |

- Non-responsive pairs (n=272, twin answered wrong): all-slot moves the recipient to the twin's wrong answer
  0.474 [0.416, 0.534] (GPT-2 0.533).
- CFR: P(twin correct | original correct) = 471/743 = 0.634 [0.599, 0.668] (GPT-2 0.581);
  P(twin correct | original wrong) = 0.085.

**Interpretation:** The core Q1 finding replicates across families: transplanting the twin's latents moves
the answer to the twin's answer in most pairs (0.69), and also carries the twin's wrong answers. That means the
latents carry the problem-specific value, not just a "be correct" signal. The effect is weaker than on GPT-2
(0.69 vs 0.84, non-overlapping CIs). Localization is sparse in both models: a few slots carry the value and
the rest are inert (single ≈ 0, LOO ≈ all-slot). **The slots differ, though.** GPT-2 uses z0/z2/z4 (even
slots), while Llama uses z1 (strongest) and z4, and z0 is inert. So the qualitative claim ports ("value lives
in a sparse subset of slots"), but a slot-index-level claim does not. Any cross-model mapping needs to be
learned per model, not assumed by position.
**Gotchas hit:** the gated meta-llama repo needs a token, so we used the unsloth mirror with the tokenizer
config patched to Meta's. LoRA target modules had been hard-coded to GPT-2 names (c_attn etc.), which would
have silently loaded nothing for Llama. Fixed, and the load is confirmed by missing=0 unexpected=0.
**Caveats:** single seed, greedy. Qualified pairs differ between models (each model's own correct originals),
so the GPT-2 vs Llama comparison is on different pair sets. The legacy row is kept only for continuity.
**Next:** Q2 decode control on Llama (does a probe read the value at z1/z4 where the transplant says it lives?);
a within-method baseline (CODI GPT-2 seed vs seed) to answer the advisor's pretraining-artifact concern.

## 2026-10-09 — CODI Llama-3.2-1B: necessity of the latents under every replacement (codi, run_id: 20261009-231032_codi_llama1b-necessity-all-replacements)

**Goal:** CODI counterpart to `20261009-231035_coconut_llama1b-necessity-all-replacements`. Same design as GPT-2
`20260927-005051_codi_necessity-all-replacements`. How much does Llama-1B CODI need its latents, and do the
necessary slots match the transplant carriers z1/z4 (`20261009-102724_codi_llama1b-minimal-pair-patch`)?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct@5a8abab` + `connordilgren/llama32-1b-gsm8k-codi@5f670c7`,
bf16, LoRA r=128 on q/k/v/o/up/down/gate, prj_dim 2048, 6 latents.
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test, all 1319; run seed 11.
**Hyperparams:** greedy; mean over 300 test examples; pass@10 at T=0.7; max_new_tokens 64.
**Command:** `eval_command.txt`; 3 shards + merge. Code change: `necessity_codi.py` records the real backbone.
**Headline results:** baseline 0.566 (746/1319; paper 0.560). `early_termination_necessity=0.090`.

| condition | Llama acc (PWC) | GPT-2 acc (PWC) | Llama pass@10 | GPT-2 pass@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 0.566 (1) | 0.419 (1) | 0.639 | 0.519 |
| trunc_0 | 0.475 (0.73) | 0.238 (0.45) | **0.711** | 0.509 |
| ablate_all_zero | 0.444 (0.69) | 0.231 (0.44) | 0.622 | 0.494 |
| ablate_all_mean | **0.315 (0.52)** | 0.105 (0.20) | 0.456 | 0.307 |
| ablate_all_noise | 0.478 (0.74) | 0.141 (0.26) | 0.656 | 0.397 |

Truncation curve k=0..6: 0.475, 0.428, 0.500, 0.493, 0.475, 0.566, 0.566. It is not monotone: one latent is
worse than none, and the jump comes at k=5.
Single-site PWC (zero / mean / noise): z0 0.91/0.90/0.86, **z1 0.82/0.76/0.83**, z2 0.85/0.96/0.83,
z3 0.87/0.93/0.85, **z4 0.88/0.83/0.87**, z5 0.98/0.98/0.98 (n.s. under all three).

**Interpretation:**
- **Necessary, but less than on GPT-2.** Every ablate-all condition is significant (McNemar p ≤ 4e-12), and mean
  is again the most damaging replacement (PWC 0.52, worse than no latents, the same pattern as GPT-2). But
  no latents still keeps 73% of correct answers (GPT-2 45%). Without latents, pass@10 is *higher* than with them (0.711 vs
  0.639): as on GPT-2, the latents concentrate probability on one answer rather than being the only route to it.
- **Necessity matches the transplant carriers.** Under mean replacement, the two most necessary sites are z1 (0.76) and
  z4 (0.83), exactly the slots that carry transplantable value (single-slot steering 0.38 / 0.22). z5 is
  unnecessary, as on GPT-2. Two independent tests (necessity, sufficiency for steering) pick the same
  slots on Llama, and on GPT-2 they picked different ones (z0/z2/z4 for steering, with z0/z4 most necessary).
- Across both methods, the 1B model leans on its latents less than GPT-2 small does. CODI keeps most of its
  latent-content story (transplantable, necessary at the carrier slots), and Coconut keeps almost none of it beyond pass 0.
**Gotchas hit:** a second, byte-identical merge of the same shards (`20261009-220539_codi_llama1b-necessity-all-replacements`)
appeared on the pod at 22:05 UTC, probably from a parallel session. Not copied back; this run is the scripted merge.
**Caveats:** single seed. The non-monotone truncation curve suggests that truncated CODI is off-distribution (it was
trained with exactly 6 latents), so truncation is a weaker probe of CODI than ablation.
**Next:** large-delta twin rerun with the hidden-operand filter; within-method baseline.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (6 latents) | 0.359 (1) | 0.331 (1) | 0.491 | 0.415 |

| ablate_all_zero | 0.272 (0.67) | 0.033 (0.08) | 0.431 | 0.091 |
| ablate_all_mean | 0.297 (0.75) | 0.090 (0.22) | 0.440 | 0.222 |
| ablate_all_noise | 0.259 (0.64) | 0.066 (0.15) | 0.415 | 0.152 |

Truncation curve k=0..6: 0.208, **0.320**, 0.330, 0.344, 0.352, 0.356, 0.359. On GPT-2 it is graded:
0.081, 0.083, 0.152, 0.190, 0.234, 0.272, 0.331.
Single-pass PWC (zero / mean / noise): p0 0.74/0.77/0.64, p1 0.84/0.83/0.76, p2 0.87/0.85/0.80,
p3 0.91/0.89/0.87, p4 0.94/0.92/0.91 (n.s. under zero), p5 0.97/0.94/0.95 (n.s.).

**Interpretation:**
- **Neither pure reading holds; the latents are needed but shallow.** Removing all latents loses 63% of
  correct answers (PWC 0.37, McNemar p=2e-24), so the latent block is needed. But a single latent recovers
  almost everything (0.208 → 0.320 of 0.359), and passes 2–5 add 4 pp in total. With all six present,
  content-free replacements (zero/mean/noise) keep 64–75% of correct answers; on GPT-2 they keep 8–22%.
  So most of Llama Coconut's work is the latent block existing, plus pass 0's content. Passes 1–5 contribute little.
- **This matches the transplant exactly.** There, pass 0 alone steered 0.19 of the 0.216 all-slot rate, and passes 1–5
  added ~2.5 pp. Necessity falls monotonically with pass index here (p0 most necessary, p4/p5 n.s.), the
  same ordering as transplant steering. On GPT-2 the carrier was pass 1 (PWC ~0.3, steering 0.56).
  Pass 0 is the hidden state at `<|start-latent|>`, computed from the question alone, so on Llama Coconut the
  "reasoning" that can be moved or removed is mostly a re-encoding of the question, not multi-step latent computation.
- **Scale shifts reliance off the latents.** Ablating all latents costs 33–36 pp on GPT-2 but only 6–10 pp on
  Llama, and Llama without latents (0.208) is 2.6× GPT-2 without latents (0.081). The 1B model answers more
  from the question directly. For the "do findings port" question this means the Coconut transplant null on
  Llama is real, but it is about where the computation lives, not a broken pipeline.
**Gotchas hit:** with 6 shards sharing one A40, Coconut ran at ~38 s/question per shard. The answer decode
recomputes the whole sequence per token (no KV cache, as in the reference generate), so the run took 4.7 h.
A KV-cached batched decode is worth adding for future Llama Coconut runs (validate against the gate first).
**Caveats:** single seed; greedy except the pass@10 columns. GPT-2 numbers come from `20260927-005834`
(same script and data).
**Next:** large-delta twin rerun with the hidden-operand filter (see the twin notes); within-method baseline.

## 2026-10-11 — Zhang-style random swap + twin swap, coconut on gsm8k (coconut, run_id: 20261011-050903_coconut_zhang-swap-gsm8k)

**Goal:** Pilot from PILOT_ZHANG_SWAP.md: replicate Zhang et al. 2025's random-permutation latent/CoT swap (arXiv 2512.21711, Table 3) on the Dilgren & Wiegreffe GPT-2 grid, next to our E3 twin swap on the same recipients (GSM8K only). Does the 'latents are placeholders' verdict depend on the intervention, the task, or the method?
**Mechanism / model:** `coconut`, openai-community/gpt2 / hf:connordilgren/gpt2-gsm8k-coconut/checkpoint_33, compute_steps=6.
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test n=1194 seed=0; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'method': 'coconut', 'num_latents': 6, 'perm_seed': 0, 'n_twin_cap': 400, 'max_new_tokens': 48, 'deltas': [1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3]}
**Command:** `scripts/swap_random_coconut.py --method coconut --dataset gsm8k --checkpoint_path <grid>/gpt2-gsm8k-coconut/checkpoint_33 --checkpoint_label hf:connordilgren/gpt2-gsm8k-coconut/checkpoint_33 --data_dir ~/Projects/are-lrms-easily-interpretable/data --device cpu --slug zhang-swap-gsm8k --stage pilot --hardware 'local Apple Silicon CPU'  (venv pinned to Coconut's requirements: torch 2.5.1, transformers 4.46.2)`
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.336`, `compute_steps=6`
**Results:** Random swap: accuracy 0.336 -> 0.040, IR 92.5% [90.8, 93.8], steer-to-donor 7.8% (n=1194; 1186 with a differing donor). Twin swap on base-correct recipients with a responsive twin (n=179, CFR 0.61): IR 92.2%, steer 87.1%. Same 178 recipients, paired: twin steer 87.1% vs random steer 14.0%, McNemar b=132 c=2, p=8e-37. IR does not separate them (b=10, c=12, p=0.83).
**Interpretation:** On GSM8K, Zhang's random swap does NOT give a placeholder verdict: the latents are load-bearing (accuracy collapses, 92% of answers change). But the random swap only shows *that* the latents are used, not *what* they carry. Random donors almost never transfer their answer (8-14%), while same-problem twins do (87%, consistent with E3's 83%). IR is identical for both donors, so the content signal is visible only to a twin donor plus a steering metric.
**Gotchas hit:** The local transformers 5.x breaks coconut_common's legacy KV-cache slicing, so I used a scratch venv pinned to Coconut's requirements. Grid CoT/no-CoT checkpoints keep the base vocab (50257), while the Coconut ones have +3 latent tokens; the loader now resizes to the checkpoint's vocab.
**Caveats:** Single seed and permutation. GPT-2 only. CODI is not in this pilot (its scripts hard-code CUDA): CODI GSM8K/ProntoQA/ProsQA is the next step. Steer is defined as P(swapped answer == donor's own base answer AND != recipient's base answer | donor answer differs). On ProntoQA, binary answers make ~50% steer the chance level. Swaps are full-chain (all 6 latent passes / the whole reasoning text). The CoT splice re-tokenizes the donor's decoded text.
**Next:** CODI rows (GSM8K zen-E + grid ProntoQA/ProsQA, on RunPod); Llama-1B grid; no-CoT parity check on our own pool; decide the paper angle (PILOT_ZHANG_SWAP.md).

## 2026-10-11 — Zhang-style random swap + twin swap, codi on gsm8k (codi, run_id: 20261011-061437_codi_zhang-swap-gsm8k)

**Goal:** CODI rows of the Zhang-swap pilot (PILOT_ZHANG_SWAP.md): does the pattern from Coconut (random swap = placeholder on logic tasks, load-bearing but content-blind on GSM8K; twin swap reads the content) hold for CODI?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2 / hf:zen-E/CODI-gpt2, compute_steps=6.
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test n=1194 seed=0; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'method': 'codi', 'num_latents': 6, 'perm_seed': 0, 'n_twin_cap': 400, 'max_new_tokens': 64, 'deltas': [1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3], 'dtype': 'float32', 'greedy': True}
**Command:** `scripts/swap_random_codi.py --dataset gsm8k --checkpoint_path zen-E/CODI-gpt2 --grid_repo ~/Projects/are-lrms-easily-interpretable --data_dir ~/Projects/are-lrms-easily-interpretable/data --device cpu --fp32 True --slug zhang-swap-gsm8k --stage pilot --hardware 'local Apple Silicon CPU'  (venv: torch 2.5.1, transformers 4.46.2, peft 0.15.2)`
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.441`, `compute_steps=6`
**Results:** Base accuracy 0.441 (fp32, gold-trace test set, n=1194; reference bf16 protocol 0.437 on the full test set). Random swap: accuracy 0.441 -> 0.043 [0.033, 0.056], IR 93.0% [91.4, 94.3], steer-to-donor 1.6%. Twin swap on base-correct recipients with a responsive twin (n=235, CFR 0.625): IR 94.5%, steer 86.7%. Same 228 recipients, paired: twin steer 86.4% vs random 1.8%, McNemar b=193 c=0, p=1.6e-58.
**Interpretation:** Same pattern as Coconut on GSM8K (`20261011-050903_coconut_zhang-swap-gsm8k`): a random swap breaks the model (latents are used), but a random donor's answer almost never transfers, while a twin's does (86-87%, matching the aligned E3 84%). The answer-change rate can't separate the two donors. So the use-vs-content split holds across both latent methods. Note: CODI's latents 'sharpen' rather than 'compute' in the sampling-recovery test, yet foreign latents still collapse accuracy. Removing latents and replacing them with wrong content are different interventions.
**Gotchas hit:** `eval_codi.build_model` hard-codes CUDA, so this loads with the grid repo's device-agnostic `CODIInference` and reimplements its latent loop with an override hook. bf16 on CPU took ~3.6 s/example, so it is cast to fp32 (~35x faster). On the n=30 smoke test, 1/30 base answers differed from bf16; full-set base accuracy matches the references.
**Caveats:** fp32, not the reference bf16 protocol. Single permutation seed. GPT-2 only. Full-chain swap (z_0..z_5, aligned). On ProntoQA, binary answers put chance-level steer at ~50%.
**Next:** Llama-1B grid; write up the use-vs-content table across methods and tasks. Multi-dataset direction: see MULTI_DATASET.md.

## 2026-10-11 — Zhang-style random swap, codi on prosqa (codi, run_id: 20261011-062104_codi_zhang-swap-prosqa)

**Goal:** CODI rows of the Zhang-swap pilot (PILOT_ZHANG_SWAP.md): does the pattern from Coconut (random swap = placeholder on logic tasks, load-bearing but content-blind on GSM8K; twin swap reads the content) hold for CODI?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2 / hf:connordilgren/gpt2-prosqa-codi/pytorch_model.bin, compute_steps=6.
**Data:** prosqa test n=500 seed=0; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'method': 'codi', 'num_latents': 6, 'perm_seed': 0, 'n_twin_cap': 400, 'max_new_tokens': 64, 'deltas': [1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3], 'dtype': 'float32', 'greedy': True}
**Command:** `scripts/swap_random_codi.py --dataset prosqa --checkpoint_path <grid>/gpt2-prosqa-codi/pytorch_model.bin --grid_repo ~/Projects/are-lrms-easily-interpretable --data_dir ~/Projects/are-lrms-easily-interpretable/data --device cpu --fp32 True --slug zhang-swap-prosqa --stage pilot --hardware 'local Apple Silicon CPU'  (venv: torch 2.5.1, transformers 4.46.2, peft 0.15.2)`
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.816`, `compute_steps=6`
**Results:** Base accuracy 0.816 (Dilgren & Wiegreffe report 80.0). Random swap: accuracy 0.816 -> 0.816, IR 0.0% [0, 0.76], steer 0 (n=500).
**Interpretation:** Placeholder verdict, same as Coconut on ProsQA.
**Gotchas hit:** `eval_codi.build_model` hard-codes CUDA, so this loads with the grid repo's device-agnostic `CODIInference` and reimplements its latent loop with an override hook. bf16 on CPU took ~3.6 s/example, so it is cast to fp32 (~35x faster). On the n=30 smoke test, 1/30 base answers differed from bf16; full-set base accuracy matches the references.
**Caveats:** fp32, not the reference bf16 protocol. Single permutation seed. GPT-2 only. Full-chain swap (z_0..z_5, aligned). On ProntoQA, binary answers put chance-level steer at ~50%.
**Next:** Llama-1B grid; write up the use-vs-content table across methods and tasks. Multi-dataset direction: see MULTI_DATASET.md.

## 2026-10-11 — Twin magnitude, Coconut GPT-2: steering drops only when the answer changes by <=5%; flat above (coconut, run_id: 20261011-090628_coconut_twin-magnitude-gsm8k)

**Goal:** Phase A step 1 (MULTI_DATASET.md §4). Every earlier twin changed one operand by 1-3; an offline reanalysis of the logged twin runs found steering drops when the answer changes by <=5% of its value. Does it, with changes up to +-20 and x0.5..x3, and is the drop about relative change, absolute change, or answer size?
**Mechanism / model:** `coconut`, gpt2 / `hf:connordilgren/gpt2-gsm8k-coconut@checkpoint_33`, 6 latent passes, fp32, greedy.
**Data:** gold-trace test file, all 1194 (seed-0 order); 10,951 twin candidates (4,374 pass the hidden-operand filter);
2,072 qualified pairs, 300 non-responsive pairs.
**Design:** same script, sites and qualification as E3, plus `--change_set 1,-1,2,-2,3,-3,5,-5,10,-10,20,-20,x0.5,x1.25,x1.5,x2,x3 --conditions all_slot`: one twin per (example, propagation-qualified step, change), deduplicated by twin text; multiplicative changes round half up. Only the aligned all-slot transplant is run. Per pair: absolute and relative answer change and fraction moved = (patched - original)/(twin - original). The hidden-operand filter (`minimal_pairs.passes_hidden_operand_filter`: no chain operand that is neither a question number nor an earlier result, and the perturbed number not equal to any step result) is recorded per pair, not applied at patch time; the analysis reports filtered (primary) and all pairs. **Definition is mine**: the Llama twin notes name the filter but don't define it. Analysis: `uv run python scripts/analyze_twin_magnitude.py results/<this run>`, which also excludes pairs whose twin answer equals the original (the changed step doesn't reach the answer; steering is undefined and `matches_twin` is False by construction). The `magnitude_bins` in the manifest INCLUDE those pairs; quote the analysis-script numbers below.
**Command:** `eval_command.txt`; wrapper `scripts/pod/phase_a_step1.sh run`. Pod `ymuz0w5buqfe26` (RTX A40 secure, CA-MTL-1,
$0.59/hr), in parallel with the CODI run; decode 70 s, whole run ~20 min.
**Headline results:** base accuracy 0.336 (identical to E3). CFR 0.587. All-slot steer 0.845 over all qualified pairs
(manifest); non-responsive pairs follow the twin's wrong answer 0.473.

Steer rate by relative answer change (19 of 2,072 pairs excluded: twin answer = original):

| rel. answer change | filtered n | filtered steer [95% CI] | all n | all steer [95% CI] | median frac. moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <=5% | 72 | 0.708 [0.595, 0.801] | 116 | 0.595 [0.504, 0.680] | 1.00 |
| 5-15% | 200 | 0.880 [0.828, 0.918] | 345 | 0.870 [0.830, 0.901] | 1.00 |
| 15-40% | 318 | 0.909 [0.872, 0.936] | 588 | 0.881 [0.852, 0.905] | 1.00 |
| 40-100% | 333 | 0.898 [0.861, 0.926] | 660 | 0.871 [0.843, 0.895] | 1.00 |
| >100% | 173 | 0.838 [0.776, 0.886] | 344 | 0.840 [0.798, 0.875] | 1.00 |

Logistic steer ~ log rel change + log |answer|: filtered +0.084 (p=0.27) and -0.225 (p=6e-5); all +0.154 (p=0.003) and
-0.185 (p=4e-7).
**Interpretation:** Confirms the offline reanalysis for Coconut, and sharpens it: steering is flat at ~0.84-0.91 from 5% to
>100% answer change and drops only in the <=5% bin (0.60 all, 0.71 filtered; CIs clear of the 5-15% bin in both pools).
So the drop is a threshold at small relative changes, not a trend, and large changes don't hurt. Coconut's dip is deeper
than CODI's (`20261011-092740_codi_twin-magnitude-gsm8k`: 0.84 filtered). Larger answers steer less independently of the
relative change. Median fraction moved = 1.0 everywhere; mean fraction moved in the <=5% bin is >1 because the failures
there overshoot by many multiples of the tiny twin-original gap.
**Gotchas hit:** as in the CODI run (excluded twin = original pairs).
**Caveats:** single seed, greedy, gold-trace subset. Bins share recipients. Filtered <=5% n=72, below the 150 target: the
dip is significant in the unfiltered pool, suggestive in the filtered one.
**Next:** step 3 ladder on the synthetic depth task.

## 2026-10-11 — Twin magnitude, CODI GPT-2: steering is flat over 5% to >100% answer changes; a small dip at <=5% (codi, run_id: 20261011-092740_codi_twin-magnitude-gsm8k)

**Goal:** Phase A step 1 (MULTI_DATASET.md §4). Every earlier twin changed one operand by 1-3; an offline reanalysis of the logged twin runs found steering drops when the answer changes by <=5% of its value. Does it, with changes up to +-20 and x0.5..x3, and is the drop about relative change, absolute change, or answer size?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2 / `hf:zen-E/CODI-gpt2@fd641b3`, 6 latents, eval mode, bf16, greedy.
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test, all 1319; 11,514 twin candidates (4,540 pass the hidden-operand filter); 2,917 qualified pairs
(original and twin correct), 300 non-responsive pairs.
**Design:** same script, sites and qualification as E3, plus `--change_set 1,-1,2,-2,3,-3,5,-5,10,-10,20,-20,x0.5,x1.25,x1.5,x2,x3 --conditions all_slot`: one twin per (example, propagation-qualified step, change), deduplicated by twin text; multiplicative changes round half up. Only the aligned all-slot transplant is run. Per pair: absolute and relative answer change and fraction moved = (patched - original)/(twin - original). The hidden-operand filter (`minimal_pairs.passes_hidden_operand_filter`: no chain operand that is neither a question number nor an earlier result, and the perturbed number not equal to any step result) is recorded per pair, not applied at patch time; the analysis reports filtered (primary) and all pairs. **Definition is mine**: the Llama twin notes name the filter but don't define it. Analysis: `uv run python scripts/analyze_twin_magnitude.py results/<this run>`, which also excludes pairs whose twin answer equals the original (the changed step doesn't reach the answer; steering is undefined and `matches_twin` is False by construction). The `magnitude_bins` in the manifest INCLUDE those pairs; quote the analysis-script numbers below.
**Command:** `eval_command.txt`; wrapper `scripts/pod/phase_a_step1.sh run`. Pod `ymuz0w5buqfe26` (RTX A40 secure, CA-MTL-1,
$0.59/hr), run in parallel with the Coconut run; decode 177 s, twins ~25 min, patch 409 s.
**Headline results:** base accuracy 0.415 (E3 on A5000: 0.419, same invocation; 5/1319 examples, bf16 on a different GPU).
CFR 0.636. All-slot steer 0.812 over all qualified pairs (manifest), non-responsive pairs follow the twin's wrong answer 0.493.

Steer rate by relative answer change (27 of 2,917 pairs excluded: twin answer = original):

| rel. answer change | filtered n | filtered steer [95% CI] | all n | all steer [95% CI] | median frac. moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <=5% | 119 | 0.840 [0.764, 0.895] | 223 | 0.753 [0.693, 0.805] | 1.00 |
| 5-15% | 273 | 0.919 [0.881, 0.946] | 472 | 0.847 [0.812, 0.877] | 1.00 |
| 15-40% | 439 | 0.891 [0.858, 0.917] | 781 | 0.837 [0.810, 0.862] | 1.00 |
| 40-100% | 461 | 0.852 [0.817, 0.882] | 928 | 0.809 [0.783, 0.833] | 1.00 |
| >100% | 249 | 0.823 [0.771, 0.866] | 486 | 0.813 [0.776, 0.845] | 1.00 |

Logistic steer ~ log rel change + log |answer|: filtered -0.141 (p=0.018) and -0.144 (p=0.001); all +0.002 (p=0.96) and
-0.070 (p=0.010).
**Interpretation:** Large changes transplant as well as small ones: steering stays at 0.81-0.92 from 5% to >100% answer
change, so the 83-84% E3 number was not an artefact of +-1..3 twins. The <=5% dip is real in the unfiltered pool (0.75 vs
0.85) but mostly disappears under the hidden-operand filter (0.84 vs 0.92, CIs touch), so part of the earlier "small changes
steer less" signal came from twins whose re-executed gold is unreliable. Larger original answers steer a little less in
both pools. The log-linear logistic is the wrong shape for a threshold; read the bins. Median fraction moved is 1.0 in
every bin: failures are mostly all-or-nothing, not partial moves.
**Gotchas hit:** pairs with twin answer = original answer had to be excluded from the analysis (see Design).
**Caveats:** single seed, greedy. Bins share recipients (several twins per problem), so the CIs are somewhat optimistic.
The filtered <=5% bin has n=119, below the 150 target.
**Next:** the same ladder on the synthetic depth task (step 3), where the change size is controlled by construction.

## 2026-10-11 — Synthetic depth task, explicit CoT GPT-2: 0.999 at every depth 1-12 (explicit_cot, run_id: 20261011-105901_explicit_cot_synthetic-depth-cot)

**Goal:** Phase A step 2: the CoT upper bound on the depth task (one chain of 1-12 dependent +,-,* steps, values 0..99),
and the init checkpoint for step-3 Coconut.
**Mechanism / model:** `explicit_cot`, gpt2 (openai-community/gpt2), full fine-tune.
**Data:** synthetic depth v1.2.0 (`latentreasoning/tasks`, seed 5980): train 100k (balanced, L1/L2 oversampled), test 5,576
(500/level, L1 = 76).
**Training:** Coconut repo `run.py` @27273cb, `cot: True`, config `configs/synthetic/gpt2_depth_cot.yaml` (adapted from
Dilgren & Wiegreffe `gpt2_prosqa_cot.yaml`: 1 GPU, batch 32 x grad-accum 4 = effective 128 as their 4 x 32; lr 1e-4
constant, wd 0.01, fp32, seed 0, `save_only_improve: True`, monitor set = `valid_monitor.json`). Launched with
`WANDB_MODE=disabled torchrun --nproc_per_node 1` via `scripts/pod/phase_a_step2.sh`, sharing one A40 with 2 other
training jobs, so seconds/epoch is a 3-way-shared number, not solo throughput.
**Deviation: stopped by hand after epoch 1.** The planned rule was early stop after 2 epochs without a >= 0.5 pt monitor
gain. Monitor accuracy after epoch 1 was 349/349 = 1.0, which is at the ceiling, so two more ~1 h epochs could not
improve it and would have blocked the job queue. The epoch-1 checkpoint is the one evaluated (and the best on monitor).
**Checkpoint:** `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/synthetic_checkpoints/gpt2_depth_cot/checkpoint_1` (Coconut state dict, 652 MB;
the step-3 Coconut init); training log next to it (`gpt2_depth_cot.log`). Pod path in `metrics.extra.checkpoint_pod_path`.
**Eval:** `scripts/eval_synthetic_coconut.py` (`eval_command.txt`): greedy, prompt = question + "\n" exactly as run.py,
answer after "###", batched decode verified identical to batch-1 on 32 examples, full test.json.
The manifest's curve fields were recomputed with the flat-curve rule (`depth_curve.py`, commit e130331) before commit:
the first eval reported a fit-noise "midpoint" at level 7.9 for depth.
**Headline results:** test accuracy **0.999**; per level 1.000 for L1-L7 and 0.996-0.998 for L8-L12. Flat, so no midpoint
(beyond range). AUC 0.999. Mean CoT length 57 tokens. Train time 3,584 s for the epoch (shared GPU).
**Interpretation:** Writing the intermediate values makes the depth task trivial for GPT-2 small at every depth, as
intended for the upper bound: whatever no-CoT loses with depth is attributable to doing the steps without a scratchpad.
**Caveats:** one epoch, one seed. **Next:** no-CoT and filler on the same task; Coconut from this checkpoint in step 3.

**Goal:** Phase A step 2 width pilot: CoT upper bound on the width task (2-16 independent single-digit products, answer =
the unique largest; max sampled uniformly over achievable products, chance ~3.4%).
**Mechanism / model:** `explicit_cot`, gpt2 (openai-community/gpt2), full fine-tune.

Dilgren & Wiegreffe `gpt2_prosqa_cot.yaml`: 1 GPU, batch 32 x grad-accum 4 = effective 128 as their 4 x 32; lr 1e-4
constant, wd 0.01, fp32, seed 0, `save_only_improve: True`, monitor set = `valid_monitor.json`). Launched with
`WANDB_MODE=disabled torchrun --nproc_per_node 1` via `scripts/pod/phase_a_step2.sh`, sharing one A40 with 2 other
training jobs, so seconds/epoch is a 3-way-shared number, not solo throughput.
**Deviation: stopped by hand after epoch 1.** The planned rule was early stop after 2 epochs without a >= 0.5 pt monitor
gain. Monitor accuracy after epoch 1 was 418/450 = 0.929, which is at the ceiling: the 30 width-16 monitor items always score 0 inside run.py, whose generation cap is 128 tokens while a width-16 CoT needs ~130, so the reachable maximum is 420/450, so two more ~1 h epochs could not

The manifest's curve fields were recomputed with the flat-curve rule (`depth_curve.py`, commit e130331) before commit:
the first eval reported a fit-noise "midpoint" at level 7.9 for depth.
**Headline results:** test accuracy **0.996** (our eval sizes its token budget from the data, 146 tokens, so width 16 is
scored: 0.998). Per level 0.986-1.000; flat, no midpoint. AUC 0.996. Mean CoT length 74 tokens. Train 3,994 s for the epoch (shared GPU).
**Interpretation:** CoT solves the width task at every width; the upper bound for the H2 pilot.
**Caveats:** one epoch, one seed. The Coconut run.py monitor metric under-counts width 16 (see above); test numbers don't.
**Next:** no-CoT, filler-6 and filler-24 on the same task; McNemar filler vs no-CoT pooled over widths >= 6.

## 2026-10-11 — Synthetic width task, filler tokens (24 positions, faithful) GPT-2: 0.997, no room left for filler to help (filler_tokens, run_id: 20261011-105612_filler_tokens_synthetic-width-filler24-faithful)

**Goal:** Phase A step 2, H2 width pilot (MULTI_DATASET.md §2): does filler beat no-CoT on a task that needs width, not
depth? 24 filler positions (4x the latent count, to give filler its best chance).
**Mechanism / model:** `filler_tokens`, gpt2, full fine-tune, compute_steps=24, filler token ".".
**Data:** synthetic width v1.2.0 (2-16 single-digit products, answer = unique largest, max sampled uniformly, chance ~3.4%):
train 100k, monitor 450, test 7,500 (500/level).
**Training:** `scripts/train_synthetic.py --method filler_tokens --compute-steps 24 --faithful` (Pfau et al. paper-faithful
mode: 50/50 CoT/filler training mixture, unmasked filler-span loss; same datasets and builders as the GSM8K filler runs).
lr 1e-4, batch 32 x grad-accum 4 = 128 (matched to the Coconut-repo no-CoT/CoT runs), linear decay over max 10 epochs,
early stop after 2 epochs without a >= 0.5 pt monitor gain, best-on-monitor checkpoint evaluated. Seed 42. Pod
`ymuz0w5buqfe26` (A40 secure), sharing the GPU with 2-3 other jobs, so seconds/epoch (2219 s mean) is a shared number.
Command: `eval_command.txt`; wrapper `scripts/pod/phase_a_step2.sh`.
**Checkpoint:** `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/synthetic_checkpoints/synthetic-width-filler24-faithful/best` (HF format); training log next to it. Pod path in `metrics.extra.checkpoint_pod_path`.
**Headline results:** test accuracy **0.997**; widths >= 6: 1.000; per level 0.986-1.000
(lowest at widths 2-5). Monitor by epoch: 0.987, 0.998, 0.993, 0.993; best epoch 2, early-stopped after 4. CoT leak rate 0 (the model never
writes steps at test time despite the CoT half of its training mix). Curve flat: no midpoint.
**Interpretation:** The width task is solved without written steps: 0.997 at every width up to 16, about as high as
CoT (`20261011-110121_explicit_cot_synthetic-width-cot`, 0.996). So the H2 width pilot has no headroom: whether filler
beats no-CoT is decided by the no-CoT run on the same task (McNemar, widths >= 6) in the step-2 report, but with
accuracy at ceiling a 5-point gain is impossible. Finding the largest of 16 single-digit products is evidently within
one GPT-2 forward pass, which is itself consistent with the plan's premise that width does not need serial steps.
**Caveats:** one seed; GPU shared. Small dips at widths 2-5 (0.99) are where the L2 space is enumerated and train is
oversampled.
**Next:** no-CoT (Coconut repo and same-stack) on width for the paired test; a harder width task (more chains, larger
operands, or a different aggregate) if H2 is to be tested at all.

## 2026-10-11 — Synthetic depth task, filler tokens (6 positions, faithful) GPT-2: accuracy falls from 0.99 at depth 1 to ~0.15 at depth 12, midpoint 3.5 (filler_tokens, run_id: 20261011-093413_filler_tokens_synthetic-depth-filler6-faithful)

**Goal:** Phase A step 2, H2 core control (MULTI_DATASET.md §2): filler tokens with as many positions as CODI/Coconut have
latents (6), trained on the depth task. If filler matched the latent models here, their gain would be about extra
positions, not feeding results forward. Also gives the filler depth curve against no-CoT.
**Mechanism / model:** `filler_tokens`, gpt2, full fine-tune, compute_steps=6, filler token ".".
**Data:** synthetic depth v1.2.0 (one chain of 1-12 dependent +,-,* steps, values 0..99, single tokens): train 100k
(balanced; L1/L2 enumerated and oversampled), monitor 349, test 5,576 (500/level, L1 = 76).
**Training:** `scripts/train_synthetic.py --method filler_tokens --compute-steps 6 --faithful` (Pfau et al. mode: 50/50
CoT/filler training mix, unmasked filler loss). lr 1e-4, batch 32 x grad-accum 4 = 128 (as the Coconut-repo runs), linear
decay over max 10 epochs, early stop after 2 epochs without a >= 0.5 pt monitor gain. Seed 42. Pod `ymuz0w5buqfe26` (A40
secure), GPU shared with 2-3 other jobs, so seconds/epoch (1962 s mean; 1,391-2,568 s) is a shared number.
Command: `eval_command.txt`; wrapper `scripts/pod/phase_a_step2.sh`.
**Checkpoint:** `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/synthetic_checkpoints/synthetic-depth-filler6-faithful/best` (HF format, epoch 6); training log next to it.
**Headline results:** test accuracy **0.338**, AUC 0.368, midpoint (halfway
between fitted floor 0.150 and best 0.987) at depth **3.46**. CoT leak
rate 0. Monitor by epoch: 0.129, 0.186, 0.206, 0.218, 0.301, 0.332, 0.332, 0.272; best epoch 6, stopped after 8.

| depth | n | accuracy [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 76 | 0.987 [0.929, 0.998] |
| 2 | 500 | 0.780 [0.742, 0.814] |
| 3 | 500 | 0.600 [0.556, 0.642] |
| 4 | 500 | 0.476 [0.433, 0.520] |
| 5 | 500 | 0.370 [0.329, 0.413] |
| 6 | 500 | 0.300 [0.261, 0.342] |
| 7 | 500 | 0.250 [0.214, 0.290] |
| 8 | 500 | 0.238 [0.203, 0.277] |
| 9 | 500 | 0.202 [0.169, 0.239] |
| 10 | 500 | 0.150 [0.121, 0.184] |
| 11 | 500 | 0.112 [0.087, 0.143] |
| 12 | 500 | 0.146 [0.118, 0.180] |

**Interpretation:** Without written steps the model handles one step (0.99) and then loses accuracy with every added step;
by depth 10-12 it is near 0.11-0.15 (chance for a uniformly guessed 0..99 answer is ~0.01, but answers are not uniform).
This is the shape H1 needs: a depth range where a single forward pass with 6 extra positions is not enough while CoT stays
at 0.999 (`20261011-105901_explicit_cot_synthetic-depth-cot`). Whether the 6 filler positions help at all is the
comparison with the no-CoT runs (Coconut-repo and same-stack), done in the step-2 report with a paired test.
**Caveats:** the monitor curve was still noisy (0.30 -> 0.33 -> 0.33 -> 0.27) when early stopping fired at the 0.5-pt
rule; the no-CoT runs on the same task were still improving at that point, so "filler vs no-CoT" must be read with each

is evidence against Coconut A-lite helping, not against Coconut: the final stage got 1 epoch (reference: 3 x 3
plus long final training), and accuracy at stage boundaries typically recovers over several epochs.
**Gotchas hit:** (1) Sharing one GPU with two other trainers made Coconut ~7x slower (many small sequential passes);
moved to its own pod. (2) Option A drops all written steps after stage 3, so levels > 3 jump straight from "3 steps latent,
rest written" to "all latent" (dataset.py skip-all), and 6 latents must cover up to 12 steps. (3) Checkpoint lost (above).
**Caveats:** Under-trained final stage; one seed; different training stack from no-CoT; depth level overstates serial
depth (~3x, `depth_curve.py --by collapsed`).
**Next:** A fair Coconut test needs several final-stage epochs (and ideally option B's 1 latent per step reaching 6 stages)
on a depth task that resists collapsing (v2).

The 4PL `midpoint` in the manifest is halfway between the fitted floor and best accuracy; it is not meaningful when a curve sits on its floor.
**Next:** Options (not run): (a) more epochs (v1 no-CoT needed 25) to see whether the midpoint moves right; (b) restrict to levels 1-6 or 1-8 with more test items per level; (c) easier rule constants/ranges. Decide before spending on CODI/Coconut.

## 2026-10-14 — Ouro-1.4B step-0 gate: few-shot no-CoT GSM8K by loop count (recurrent_depth, run_id: 20261014-100712_recurrent_depth_gate-ouro-1.4b)

**Goal:** Step 0 of extending Q4 (CODI <-> Coconut linear-map transplant) to a looped model.
No GSM8K-trained Ouro exists, so: can the released base `ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B` answer the
xmech eval questions (GSM8K test, 1319) *without* CoT, at which loop count, and on enough of
the questions CODI and Coconut also get right to build ladder pairs?
**Mechanism / model:** `recurrent_depth`, released Ouro-1.4B (whole 24-layer stack looped,
trained at 4 loops), no fine-tuning. compute_steps = 4 = trained loop count; loops 1-6 swept.
**Data:** xmech eval split (= GSM8K test, 1319), shots from the xmech fit split; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** 8-shot `Question: ...\nAnswer: <number>`, greedy, stop at newline, max 8 new
tokens. CoT reference: same shots with the `<<..>>` rationale written out, "The answer is N",
first 200 eval questions, 4 loops, max 160 tokens. Batch size 1, eager attention, bf16.
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/ouro_gate.sh` (transformers 4.56.2 venv); see `eval_command.txt`.

**Headline results:**

| loops | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no-CoT acc | 0.068 | 0.152 | 0.174 | **0.183** | 0.180 | 0.180 |
| correct in Ouro & CODI & Coconut (of 363) | 42 | 113 | 132 | **139** | 137 | 137 |

CoT reference at 4 loops: 0.665 (first 200; no-CoT on the same 200: 0.24). Unparseable: 0.
**Gate (fixed before running: some loops <= 4 with acc >= 0.15 and >= 100 three-way-correct): PASS**
(loops 2, 3, 4).

**Interpretation:** The base model does the task format fine (66.5% with CoT) and gets ~18%
without it. Loops buy no-CoT accuracy steeply up to 2 and saturate at the trained count (4);
5-6 neither help nor hurt. 192 questions flip wrong->right from 1 to 4 loops, 40 right->wrong.
So there is serial computation across loops worth localizing, and enough shared-correct items
(139 three-way, 175 Ouro&CODI, 157 Ouro&Coconut) for Q4-style ladder pairs.

**Gotchas hit:**
- Ouro remote code needs transformers 4.56.x: 4.54.1 / 4.55.0 fail with
  `property 'key_cache' of 'UniversalTransformerCache' object has no setter`; 4.53.3 lacks
  `GenericForQuestionAnswering`.
- **Batched left-padded generation is broken**: only the longest (unpadded) row decodes
  correctly, padded rows produce garbage (" 1. total. total"). SDPA additionally crashes on
  padded batches at loops > 1 (`(*bias): last dimension must be contiguous`). Hence bs=1 + eager.
  An earlier batched smoke run read ~0% for this reason -- any batched Ouro number is invalid.
- Default exit rule (`early_exit_threshold=1.0` on the cumulative exit-gate pdf) can exit before
  the last loop if the bf16 cumsum rounds to 1.0; the script pins `early_exit_step = k-1`.

**Caveats:**
- Guessing: Ouro's most common no-CoT outputs are round numbers (10 x130, 100 x65, 12 x63);
  79 of the 242 loop-4 correct answers are one of its 10 most frequent outputs. Some
  "base-correct" items are lucky guesses with no computed intermediate -- step 1 should prefer
  recipients that are correct at loops 3-4 and whose answer is not a frequent guess, or at least
  report results split that way.
- One prompt, one shot seed; no prompt search. A better prompt might raise no-CoT accuracy.
- Not comparable to the CODI/Coconut accuracies (different size, pretraining, and no
  task fine-tuning); only within-Ouro curves are meaningful.

**Next:** Ouro-2.6B gate (same script, running). Then step 1: Q1-style same-problem twin
patching over (loop, layer, token position) at 4 loops to find where Ouro holds the
intermediate value, before any Q4 transplant.

## 2026-10-14 — Ouro-2.6B step-0 gate: few-shot no-CoT GSM8K by loop count (recurrent_depth, run_id: 20261014-124731_recurrent_depth_gate-ouro-2.6b)

**Goal:** Same as the Ouro-1.4B gate (`20261014-100712_recurrent_depth_gate-ouro-1.4b`), for the
larger released model: can base `ByteDance/Ouro-2.6B` answer the xmech eval questions without
CoT, at which loop count, and on enough CODI/Coconut-correct questions for Q4 ladder pairs?
**Mechanism / model:** `recurrent_depth`, released Ouro-2.6B (48-layer stack looped, trained at 4
loops), no fine-tuning. compute_steps = 4; loops 1-6 swept.
**Data:** xmech eval split (= GSM8K test, 1319); run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** identical to the 1.4B run (8-shot, greedy, newline stop, bs=1, eager, bf16;
CoT reference on the first 200 at 4 loops).
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/ouro_gate.sh` (second model in the loop); see `eval_command.txt`.

**Headline results:**

| loops | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no-CoT acc, 2.6B | 0.095 | 0.187 | 0.228 | **0.233** | 0.234 | 0.230 |
| no-CoT acc, 1.4B (for reference) | 0.068 | 0.152 | 0.174 | 0.183 | 0.180 | 0.180 |
| correct in Ouro-2.6B & CODI & Coconut (of 363) | 67 | 133 | 160 | **163** | 165 | 164 |

CoT reference at 4 loops: 0.715 (first 200; no-CoT on the same 200: 0.275). Unparseable: 0.
Ouro&CODI 206, Ouro&Coconut 183 at 4 loops. **Gate: PASS** (loops 2, 3, 4).

**Interpretation:** Same shape as 1.4B, shifted up ~5 points: steep gain from 1 to 2-3 loops,
flat from the trained count on (220 items gained, 38 lost from 1 to 4 loops). 2.6B saturates a
loop earlier than 1.4B in relative terms (loop 3 ≈ loop 4). 169 items are loop-4-correct in both
sizes. The larger model gives more three-way-correct items (163 vs 139), so it is the better
step-1 candidate if its 48 layers x loops patching grid is affordable; 1.4B is half the cost.

**Gotchas hit:** as in the 1.4B notes (transformers 4.56.2 only; batched left-padded generation
broken -> bs=1 + eager; exit step pinned to the last loop).

**Caveats:** Same guessing caveat: top outputs are round numbers (10 x130, 100 x62, 12 x57); 95 of
307 loop-4 correct answers are among its 10 most frequent outputs. One prompt / shot seed. Not
comparable to CODI/Coconut accuracies; within-Ouro curves only. Wall time ~2.5 h on an A40 at
bs=1 -- step 1 should batch by equal-length prompts (no padding) or cache the few-shot prefix.

**Next:** Step 1 localization (twin patching over loop x layer x position) on 1.4B first (cheaper),
2.6B if 1.4B localizes.

A 4th job (`modal_filler24`) OOMed at launch and was not rerun.
**Caveats:** **Confound:** "faithful" filler (cot_rate 0.5, unmasked filler loss) is trained with CoT supervision on half the examples and with the filler tokens positions in the loss, while the no-CoT baseline never sees a CoT. A plain (non-faithful) filler-6 run and a random-token filler control are needed to isolate the filler effect. ## 2026-10-14 — Ouro-1.4B step 1: twin patching over (loop, layer) at the answer suffix (recurrent_depth, run_id: 20261014-163349_recurrent_depth_twin-patch-ouro-1.4b)

**Goal:** Step 1 of extending Q4 to a looped model. Ouro has no latent slots, so before any
CODI/Coconut <-> Ouro transplant we need a site that carries the problem's computed value.
Candidate: the residual stream at the post-question answer prompt (`\nAnswer: `, 4 tokens),
per (loop, layer). Q1-style same-problem twins: does patching the twin's suffix states into
the recipient move the recipient's answer to the twin's?
**Mechanism / model:** `recurrent_depth`, released Ouro-1.4B, 4 loops (trained count), 24 layers.
**Data:** recipients = step-0 gate items correct at 4 loops (GSM8K test), shuffled; twin = one
chain operand perturbed (DELTAS ±1..3) and the chain re-executed. 157 candidates, 150 recipients
correct under this script's tokenization, 65 responsive pairs (twin also correct; CFR 0.43),
42 "clean" (neither answer one of the model's 10 most frequent outputs). Fewer than the 200-pair
cap: only 157 of the 242 gate-correct items admit a minimal pair.
**Method:** recipient's prefix + question cached and never patched; patch the decoder-layer
output at (loop u, layer l) at all 4 suffix positions (`twin_all`), the last one only
(`twin_last`), or with another recipient's states (`cross_all`, cross-problem control). Scoring
teacher-forced: ld = logp(twin answer digits + "\n") − logp(recipient answer); `restored` = (ld −
ld_recipient) / (ld_twin_own − ld_recipient); `flip` = ld > 0. Median ld_recipient = −5.3,
ld_twin_own = +4.6. Self-patch sanity passes.
**Command:** see `eval_command.txt` (pod, transformers 4.56.2 venv, A40).

**Headline results** (n=65; `restored`, twin_all; loops 1-indexed, layers 0-indexed (0–23);
manifest `grids` and prediction keys `u_l` are 0-indexed in both):

| loop | layers 0–12 | layer 14 | layer 16 | layer 17 | layer 18 | layers 19–23 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | -0.00 | 0.00 | 0.01 | 0.02 | 0.01 | 0.01 |
| 2 | 0.01 | 0.05 | 0.08 | 0.12 | 0.11 | 0.10–0.11 |
| 3 | 0.10–0.11 | 0.24 | 0.28 | 0.36 | 0.34 | 0.31–0.34 |
| 4 | 0.31–0.32 | 0.36 | 0.38 | 0.41 | 0.40 | 0.38–0.40 |

Flip rate tracks restored closely (max 0.45, loop 4 layer 17). `twin_last` ≈ `twin_all` everywhere: the
effect lives at the last suffix position (the " " that predicts the first digit). Exact 4×24
grids, all and clean subsets, in the manifest. Clean subset (n=42) slightly higher (max 0.45 at
loop 4, layer 17).

**The decisive split — first digit** (at loop 4, layer 18 = key `3_18`):

| subset | n | restored | flip |
|---|---|---|---|
| twin answer's first digit differs from recipient's | 34 | 0.74 | 0.74 |
| twin answer's first digit the same | 31 | 0.03 | 0.03 |
| cross donor, first digit differs | 44 | — | 0.59 |
| cross donor, first digit same | 21 | — | 0.00 |

**Interpretation:** The answer-prompt suffix carries the **next token — the answer's leading
digit — and nothing else causally**. Ouro's tokenizer emits numbers digit by digit after a
fixed " " token; every later digit is computed at its own position by re-reading the question,
so patching the suffix moves an answer only when the twin's first digit differs, and then
~75% of the way. The cross-problem control behaves identically (59% / 0%), so this is not a
problem-specific value either. Where it is computed: nothing at the suffix in loop 1; a first rise in the
upper-middle layers (~13–18) of loop 2 (to 0.12), the main jump in the same layers of loop 3
(0.10 → 0.36), a small gain in loop 4 (→ 0.41). Mirrors the gate's accuracy-by-loops curve
(6.8% → 15.2% → 17.4% → 18.3%) except that the big suffix gain comes one loop later.

**For Q4:** this site is not a scratchpad analogue of CODI's/Coconut's latents (which carried
intermediate step values the decoder then used). Transplanting mapped CODI/Coconut latents into
Ouro's suffix can at best set the leading digit. A Q4 into-Ouro transplant as designed would be
a null by construction — recorded here rather than run. Ouro → CODI/Coconut (Ouro suffix states
as map *source*, like the plain-GPT-2 control) remains possible but would be mapping a
next-digit state, not an intermediate value.

**Gotchas hit:**
- Greedy decoding under a suffix patch never changes (first version of this script: 0 changes
  at all 96 sites): the first generated token is always " ". Fixed by putting the space in the
  suffix and teacher-forced scoring.
- Ouro's `UniversalTransformerCache` breaks transformers' `create_causal_mask` with a prefilled
  cache (mask sized to the new tokens only). The script builds the 4-D mask, position ids and
  cache positions itself. Batched rows share the cached prefix via expanded views (no padding, so
  the left-padding bug from step 0 does not apply).

**Caveats:** n=65 (34 informative first-digit-differs pairs); one prompt; teacher-forced
log-probs rather than generated answers; sites only at the suffix — the question-token positions
(where the twin's number enters) are not tested, since patching them is input patching. The
intermediate value may well be computed at question or digit positions; this run shows only that
it is not handed to the answer through the suffix.

**Next:** if Q4 with Ouro is still wanted, the options are (a) a linear probe for the
intermediate step value at suffix and late-question positions per (loop, layer) — cheap, says
whether the value is *present* even though the suffix does not causally carry it; (b) patch at
the answer-digit positions (teacher-forced twin digits as context would leak the answer, so this
needs care); (c) drop the into-Ouro direction and report Ouro as the vertical mechanism that does
not externalise its intermediate state to a post-question site.

**Goal:** Control for `20261014-151324_filler_tokens_v2-modal-filler6-25ep` (0.858): is the gain over no-CoT (0.779) due to the filler positions alone, or to the CoT supervision that the faithful recipe mixes in (cot_rate 0.5, unmasked filler loss)? This run has 6 filler tokens but trains answer-only with the filler span masked out of the loss, i.e. no CoT supervision at all.
**Mechanism / model:** `filler_tokens`, gpt2 / /workspace/synthetic_runs/pilot-modal_nf6/best, compute_steps=6.

Per N (nf6 / no-CoT 0.779 / faithful-6 0.858): 6 -> 0.978 / 0.956 / 0.982, 8 -> 0.918 / 0.904 / 0.958, 10 -> 0.856 / 0.808 / 0.892, 12 -> 0.818 / 0.750 / 0.824, 14 -> 0.720 / 0.670 / 0.788, 16 -> 0.652 / 0.586 / 0.704. So about 4.5 of the 7.9 pt faithful-6 gain over no-CoT is already present with filler compute and no CoT supervision, and about 3.4 pt is extra from the faithful recipe. Monitor by epoch ended at 0.843 (best 0.845 at epoch 24; the evaluated checkpoint was the best-on-monitor one, `best_epoch` 24). The model never emits a CoT (0% emitted_cot). Note this is a different training signal from the no-CoT run only through the 6 extra positions (no CoT is shown, the filler loss is masked), so the 4.5 pt is attributable to extra forward positions at inference.

## 2026-10-15 — Ouro-1.4B step 2: linear probes for the intermediate value per (position, loop, layer) (recurrent_depth, run_id: 20261015-022002_recurrent_depth_probe-ouro-1.4b)

**Goal:** Step 2 of extending Q4 to a looped model. Step 1
(`20261014-163349_recurrent_depth_twin-patch-ouro-1.4b`) showed that the `\nAnswer: ` suffix
*causally* carries only the answer's leading digit. Is the intermediate step value at least
*present* (linearly decodable) at the end of the question or the suffix, and does it build up
over loops?
**Mechanism / model:** `recurrent_depth`, released Ouro-1.4B, 4 loops (trained count), 24 layers,
no fine-tuning. Same 8-shot no-CoT prompt as the gate.
**Data:** probes fit on 3200 xmech fit questions (GSM8K train, excluding the 8 shots), lambda on
another 800, reported on the 1144 xmech eval questions (GSM8K test) whose chain has >= 2 steps
and integer values. Subsets: Ouro correct at 4 loops in the gate (204) / wrong (940); step-1
value not literally in the question (1058).
**Method:** one forward pass per question; decoder-layer outputs at the last question token
(`q_last`) and the 4 suffix tokens (`sfx0`-`sfx3`, `'\n' 'Answer' ':' ' '`) for every (loop,
layer): 480 sites. Ridge on z-scored features, lambda in {1e-3..10} x n chosen per site and
target on the val split. Targets: `step1` (first intermediate), `penult` (last intermediate),
`answer`, `qlast_num` (last number in the question, a surface control), and `step1_resid` (slog
step1 with its linear dependence on slog answer and slog qlast_num removed). Regression on
signed-log1p (Pearson r; hit@5% relative error after inverting), ridge classifier on the ones
digit (accuracy vs. majority class). "Best site" = chosen on val, then reported on eval.
**Command:** see `eval_command.txt` (pod, transformers 4.56.2 venv, A40, ~20 min, ~$0.20).

**Headline results** (eval n=1144; loops 1-indexed, layers 0-indexed; sites `pos/u_l` are 0-indexed):

| target | best site | Pearson r (slog) | same pos, loop 1 layer 0 | hit@5% | ones-digit acc | majority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| step1 | sfx3/0_16 | 0.69 | 0.41 | 0.045 | 0.45 | 0.43 |
| penult | sfx3/1_17 | 0.76 | 0.48 | 0.038 | 0.44 | 0.43 |
| answer | sfx2/3_19 | 0.90 | 0.53 | 0.052 | 0.39 | 0.38 |
| qlast_num (surface) | sfx3/0_7 | 0.76 | 0.44 | 0.036 | **0.56** | 0.35 |
| step1_resid | sfx3/1_16 | 0.46 | 0.13 | — | — | — |

hit@5% and digit accuracy are each taken at their own val-chosen best site. Best r per loop (max
over layers, `sfx3`): step1 0.70 / 0.69 / 0.67 / 0.68; step1_resid 0.45 / 0.47 / 0.46 / 0.46;
answer 0.89 / 0.89 / 0.88 / 0.89. Same picture at `q_last` (step1 0.61 → 0.58, answer 0.80 →
0.78). Ouro-correct vs wrong items: no meaningful gap (step1 r 0.69 vs 0.70; answer digit 0.51
vs 0.37, but the correct subset's majority digit (0) is already 0.46). Full 4x24 grids per
position/target in the manifest (`grids_eval_all`); all subsets, val scores and lambdas in
`per_site.json` (gitignored, local).

**Interpretation:**
- **Magnitude yes, value no.** The order of magnitude of the intermediate and the answer is
  linearly readable (r 0.69–0.90 in log space), but the exact value is not: hit@5% <= 5% for
  every target, and the ones digit of step1, penult and answer sits at the majority-class floor
  at every one of the 480 sites. The probe *can* read an exact digit when one is in the text:
  the ones digit of the last question number decodes to 0.56 vs. a 0.35 floor. So the null on
  the computed values is not a probe-capacity artifact.
- **Loops add nothing to what is decodable.** Everything that is decodable is there by the
  upper-middle layers of loop 1 and stays flat (or falls slightly) through loops 2–4. Yet the
  gate's no-CoT accuracy goes 6.8% → 18.3% over the same loops, and step 1's causal effect at the
  suffix appears only in loops 2–4. The extra loops change something the linear probe does not
  see, or they change too few items to show up in a 1144-question correlation.
- **The magnitude signal is mostly a question-number readout.** At loop 1, layer 0 (barely past
  the embeddings) step1 r is already 0.41. `step1_resid` (beyond answer and the last question
  number) still reaches 0.46, but magnitude is also predictable from the *other* question numbers,
  which this residual does not remove. Nothing here shows a computed intermediate.

**For Q4:** this confirms step 1. There is no site at the end of the question or the suffix where
Ouro holds the intermediate value in a form a linear map could carry. A CODI/Coconut → Ouro
transplant at these sites would be null by construction. Ouro joins the program as the vertical
mechanism whose no-CoT computation, at this base-model accuracy (18%), does not leave a
decodable intermediate at a post-question site. Not comparable in number to the CODI/Coconut
probe runs (`20260920-042323_codi_probe-continuous-full`: ridge r 0.11–0.18 on latent slots);
those probed slots meant to hold a step, here positions that are not.

**Gotchas hit:**
- The prefix-cache path never fired: `tok(prefix + question)` never starts with `tok(prefix)` (the
  boundary tokenizes differently when joined; not investigated), so all 5144 questions ran the
  uncached full prompt, as in the gate. Correct, just slower (~0.14 s/question at 4 loops on an A40, 702 s total).
- Features for all 480 sites (5144 x 5 x 4 x 24 x 2048, bf16) are 10.1 GB, kept on the GPU; the
  probe fits take 35 s for all sites.

**Caveats:** Linear probes only, with single-digit and log-magnitude readouts. A
non-linear probe, or a probe for "value as a digit string at the answer positions", could still
find more. The question is only 1 of 5 positions; the value could sit at the operand tokens
inside the question (not probed). The base model is right on only 18% of these items, and the
correct subset is small (204) and contains frequent guesses, so "present when Ouro gets it
right" is weakly tested. One prompt; 1.4B only.

**Next:** Recommend stopping the into-Ouro transplant and reporting Ouro as above. If more Ouro
work is wanted: run the same probe on operand-token positions inside the question, or try an
MLP probe on the best sites. Both are cheap.

## 2026-10-15 — Ouro-1.4B step 2b: logit lens for the intermediate's leading digit per (loop, layer) (recurrent_depth, run_id: 20261015-024317_recurrent_depth_logit-lens-ouro-1.4b)

**Goal:** Follow-up to the linear probes (`20261015-022002_recurrent_depth_probe-ouro-1.4b`), which
tested log-magnitude and the *ones* digit. Ouro writes numbers one digit at a time after a `" "`,
so its unembedding at the suffix's last position can show a number's *leading* digit. Does the
first intermediate's leading digit appear there in early loops, before the answer's takes over
(a latent step-by-step signature)? The logit lens is also the readout the CODI runs here used.
**Mechanism / model:** `recurrent_depth`, released Ouro-1.4B, 4 loops, 24 layers, gate prompt.
**Data:** 1144 xmech eval questions (GSM8K test; chains >= 2 steps, integer values); 979 of them
"differ" (step1's leading digit != the answer's); 204 Ouro-correct at 4 loops. The leading-digit
probe is fit on 3200 xmech fit questions, with lambda chosen on 800.
**Method:** lens = `lm_head(model.norm(h))` on the output of layer l in loop u. Ouro applies
`model.norm` at the end of every loop, so at layer 23 this is exactly that loop's own exit
readout (sanity: it matches the model's own output digit on 100% of items). The lens is read at
the last question token (`q_last`) and the suffix's final `" "` (`sfx3`), restricted to the 10
digit tokens. **beats_donor** = P(target's leading digit) > P(donor digit), where the donor is
another item's step1 leading digit, different from this item's step1 and answer leading digits.
Chance is 0.5 regardless of how common each digit is (Benford). A ridge leading-digit probe on
the same features is also reported against the majority-class baseline.
**Command:** see `eval_command.txt` (pod, A40, ~20 min, ~$0.20). Post-hoc controls:
`python3 scripts/ouro_lens_controls.py results/<this run> xmech_questions.jsonl`.

**Headline results** (`sfx3`, differ items n=979; loops 1-indexed, layers 0-indexed):

| | loop 1 | loop 2 | loop 3 | loop 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| answer beats donor (end of loop) | 0.585 | 0.68 | 0.70 | 0.705 |
| step1 beats donor (end of loop) | 0.546 | 0.545 | 0.532 | 0.513 |
| step1 beats donor (best layer in loop: l 20) | 0.60 | 0.62 | 0.60 | 0.57 |
| — step1 digit also leads a question number (n=355) | 0.63 | 0.59 | 0.58 | 0.55 |
| — step1 digit novel (n=624) | 0.50 | 0.52 | 0.51 | 0.49 |
| — novel, donor not a question-number lead (n=362) | 0.57 | 0.57 | 0.56 | 0.56 |
| copy control: a question number's leading digit (n=551, same donor restriction) | 0.54 | 0.50 | 0.52 | 0.51 |
| Ouro-correct & step1 novel (n=116): step1 / answer | 0.52 / 0.76 | 0.56 / 0.97 | 0.57 / 1.00 | 0.60 / 1.00 |

Rows marked "end of loop" and the split rows use layer 23 (per-item values saved only there);
the "best layer" row is from the manifest grids. Top-1 over digits at layer 23: answer 0.32 → 0.42 over loops 1 → 4 (majority 0.29); step1
0.27 → 0.21. Supervised leading-digit probe at
`sfx3`: answer 0.32 → 0.41 by loop 4 (majority 0.29); step1 0.21–0.27 everywhere (majority on
differ 0.24). At `q_last` nothing: lens digit mass ~0, beats_donor 0.46–0.55, probes at majority.
Standard error at n≈1000 is ±0.016; at n≈360, ±0.026.

**Interpretation:**
- **The answer's leading digit is computed across loops**: weak after loop 1 (0.585), clearly
  present from loop 2 on (0.68 → 0.70). This matches the gate's accuracy curve and step 1's
  patching effect, and it holds for answer digits that occur nowhere in the question (0.52 →
  0.66).
- **No early-intermediate signature.** The step1 digit signal is weak and comes mostly from
  items where that digit already leads a number in the question (0.63 vs. 0.50 when it doesn't).
  With the donor restricted to digits not in the question, novel step1 digits reach 0.56–0.57.
  That is a little above the copy control at loops 2–4 (0.50–0.52), but flat across loops: it
  neither peaks early nor fades as the answer forms. Where Ouro is right, the step1 digit rises
  slowly alongside the answer's (0.52 → 0.60) rather than preceding it. This looks like
  correlation with the answer's digit, not an intermediate that is computed and then consumed.
- The mid-loop bump (layer 20 of loops 1–2, ~0.60–0.62) could not be split by the copy control
  (per-item values are saved only at end of loop). Its size matches the "copyable" row, so it
  most likely has the same source.

**For Q4:** consistent with step 1 and the linear probes. The `" "` position carries the answer's
leading digit, built up over loops 2–4, and no readable intermediate. A CODI/Coconut → Ouro
transplant here would be null.

**Gotchas hit:** none new. All prompts ran uncached (as in the probe run). bs=1, eager.

**Caveats:**
- Only the leading digit is testable this way; GSM8K's first intermediate often shares it with
  the answer (165 of 1144 items excluded as "same").
- The control analysis is post hoc and at layer 23 only.
- Only 116 items are both Ouro-correct and step1-novel.
- The base model is right on only 18% of items.
- Ouro-1.4B only.

**Next:** Ouro for Q4 is done unless someone wants Ouro-2.6B or a fine-tuned Ouro (not
budgeted). Report Ouro as the layer-wise mechanism whose no-CoT computation leaves the answer
digit, but no decodable intermediate, at the answer position.

## 2026-10-17 — Answer-phase KV eviction: CODI's answer reads slots 1 and 5 (and a little of 3), mostly at layers 8-11; partial eviction is worse than evicting everything; mean-merging the 6 slots is worth nothing (codi, run_id: 20261017-205418_codi_evict-kv)

**Goal:** Idea #4 of the KV/latent-efficiency brainstorm: use KV-cache eviction as a causal
test. The 6 continuous thoughts are computed honestly (no patching, no ablation of the latents
themselves); only the **answer phase** (eot + every generated answer token) is blocked from
attending to chosen thought positions at chosen layers. This isolates the answer → latent
attention read, which the necessity runs (`20260927-005051_codi_necessity-all-replacements`)
can't separate from the latents' effect on each other. Three questions: which slots does the
answer need, which slots suffice, and at which layers is the read? Also one compression
variant: can the 6 slots' K/V be mean-pooled into 1?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2 / `hf:zen-E/CODI-gpt2@fd641b3` (released checkpoint), 6
thoughts, paper inference protocol (LoRA r=128/α=32, projection 768+LN, greedy), **fp32 on
CPU** (the earlier CODI runs were bf16 on CUDA).
**Data:** gsm8k-aug test, all 1319 examples in file order; seed 11.
**Design:** A forward pre-hook on each of the 12 `GPT2Attention` modules adds `finfo.min` to the
chosen key columns while the answer phase runs. Slot i = the sequence position of iteration i's
input (absolute `L0 + i - 1`), the same convention as `override_input_at` and
`ablate_attention_codi.py`. So slot 1 holds the projected bot-position state (the "latent 0"),
and slot i holds iteration i−1's output. The 6th iteration's output is never written to the
cache. Checked on one example with `output_attentions`: masking slots {1,3} at layers 4-7 gives
exactly 0 mass there and leaves the other 8 layers untouched. Conditions: full;
evict_all; keep_only_i / evict_only_i; keep_135 (the slots the patching runs found carry the
value) vs keep_246; evict one layer band (0-3 / 4-7 / 8-11) for all slots, or keep only one band;
merge_mean (per layer, the 6 slots' K and V averaged into slot 1, slots 2-6 evicted). Paired
McNemar against full.
**Command:** (local CODI checkout at `codi@2c23146` + `codi_streaming.patch`, venv from its
`requirements.txt` minus the `nvidia-*`/`triton` lines)
```
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python <repo>/scripts/evict_kv_codi.py \
  --ckpt_dir ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--zen-E--CODI-gpt2/snapshots/fd641b3d3edc59e4f534b55588e906588c9e36bb/ \
  --checkpoint_label "hf:zen-E/CODI-gpt2@fd641b3" --model_name_or_path gpt2 --seed 11 --model_max_length 512 \
  --lora_r 128 --lora_alpha 32 --lora_init --greedy True --num_latent 6 --use_prj True --prj_dim 768 \
  --prj_no_ln False --prj_dropout 0.0 --inf_latent_iterations 6 --inf_num_iterations 1 --remove_eos True \
  --use_lora True --output_dir /tmp/x --device cpu --n 0
```
2916 s on an Apple Silicon CPU (2.2 s/example for all 23 conditions), $0.
**Headline results** (n=1319; "lost/gained" = flips vs full, paired):

| condition | acc | 95% CI | lost | gained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | 0.425 | [0.398, 0.451] | – | – |
| evict_all | 0.229 | [0.207, 0.252] | 316 | 58 |
| keep_only_1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 | 0.262 / 0.220 / 0.221 / 0.221 / 0.227 / 0.216 | | | |
| evict_only_1 | 0.362 | [0.336, 0.388] | 99 | 16 |
| evict_only_2 | 0.425 | | 8 | 9 |
| evict_only_3 | 0.407 | | 41 | 18 (p=0.004) |
| evict_only_4 | 0.422 | | 14 | 10 |
| evict_only_5 | 0.369 | [0.344, 0.396] | 103 | 30 |
| evict_only_6 | 0.418 | | 18 | 9 |
| keep_135 | 0.369 | [0.344, 0.396] | 95 | 22 |
| keep_246 | **0.109** | [0.093, 0.127] | 445 | 29 |
| evict_band L0-3 / L4-7 / L8-11 | 0.306 / 0.369 / **0.127** | | | |
| keep_band L0-3 / L4-7 / L8-11 | 0.113 / 0.181 / 0.262 | | | |
| merge_mean | 0.230 | [0.208, 0.253] | 309 | 52 |

**Interpretation:**
- **The attention read is worth ~20 points.** Evicting all 6 slots drops accuracy 42.5 → 22.9.
  The latents still exist, but the answer can't see them.
- **Necessity is concentrated in slots 1 and 5, with slot 3 a distant third.** Evicting any one
  of 2, 4 or 6 alone costs nothing. This is an independent confirmation of the patching result
  (value concentrated in slots 1, 3, 5). It uses a different intervention: eviction at read time,
  not content replacement at write time.
- **No single slot is sufficient.** keep_only_i ≈ evict_all for every i. Slot 1 is slightly
  above, at 26%.
- **Slots 1, 3 and 5 together recover ~71% of the latent contribution:** (36.9 − 22.9) /
  (42.5 − 22.9). Slots 2, 4 and 6 are each individually free to drop, but dropping them jointly
  costs 5.6 points, so they are partly redundant with one another.
- **Partial eviction can be worse than total eviction.** keep_246 (10.9%), evict L8-11 (12.7%),
  keep L0-3 (11.3%) and keep L4-7 (18.1%) are all *below* evict_all (22.9%). Reading some of
  the latent channel without the rest misleads the answer more than reading none of it. So the
  read is coordinated across slots and layers, not additive.
- **The read happens mostly late (layers 8-11), but no band is sufficient on its own.**
  keep_band L8-11 is only 26.2%.
- **Naive compression fails.** Mean-pooling the 6 slots' K/V into one entry is no better than
  evicting all of them. The slots are not interchangeable. For the efficiency framing: you can
  drop single slots 2/4/6 for free and half the latent KV (keep_135) at −5.6 points, but there
  is no free lunch here at 6 slots.

**Gotchas hit:** under transformers 4.52.4, CODI's GPT-2 returns the legacy tuple KV cache (not a
`DynamicCache`). Inside the attention call it *is* a `DynamicCache`, which is what the mask hook
uses for the key length. `eval_codi.build_model` hard-coded `cuda` + bf16; it now takes `device`
/ `dtype` kwargs, with defaults unchanged.
**Caveats:**
- fp32/CPU full accuracy is 42.5% on the full test set, vs 43.7% for bf16/CUDA in
  `20260918-021217_codi_released-weights-6lat`. Compare conditions only within this run.
- An additive mask renormalises the softmax: the evicted mass goes to the remaining keys (mostly
  question tokens and the attention sink). Some of the "worse than evict_all" effect may be this
  redistribution putting more weight on the surviving latent slots, rather than "misleading
  content". A value-zeroing variant (keep the key, zero V) would separate the two.
- The mask applies to every answer-phase token, so later answer tokens also lose access through
  earlier answer tokens' own reads.
- One checkpoint, one task, greedy decoding only.
**Next:** (1) a value-zero variant to separate renormalisation from content; (2) the same
harness on Coconut (slots 2 and 5 per patching) for the cross-method comparison; (3) Ouro
per-loop KV (idea #5) needs a pod.

## 2026-10-17 — Answer-phase KV eviction, Coconut: the answer reads the later slots (5, 6, then 2) almost only at layers 8-11, and no partial eviction is worse than evicting everything, unlike CODI (coconut, run_id: 20261017-212529_coconut_evict-kv)

**Goal:** The Coconut mirror of `20261017-205418_codi_evict-kv`. The 6 thoughts are computed
honestly; only the answer phase is blocked from attending to chosen thought slots at chosen
layers. Which slots does the answer read, at which layers, and does Coconut show CODI's
"partial eviction is worse than none" pattern?
**Mechanism / model:** `coconut`, gpt2 / `hf:connordilgren/gpt2-gsm8k-coconut@checkpoint_33`
(released, loaded into the vanilla module via `coconut_common.load_coconut`), 6 latents, greedy,
max_new_tokens 48, fp32 on CPU (transformers 4.52.4).
**Data:** `gsm_original_test.json` (Dilgren & Wiegreffe prep, the same 1319 GSM8K test questions
as CODI's split), all 1319 in file order; answer after `###`.
**Design:** Same mask and condition grid as the CODI run, from the new shared module
`scripts/evict_kv_common.py` (the CODI script was refactored onto it, and reproduces its
committed outputs on the first 8 examples). Coconut differences:
- The latent passes are `coconut_common.run_passes`, unmasked.
- The answer phase starts at `<|end-latent|>`. The last pass (slot 6 + `<|end-latent|>`) and the
  decode run with a KV cache, and the mask hits only queries at or after `<|end-latent|>`.
  `--check_reference` compared the unmasked cached decode with `finish_and_decode` (the reference
  no-cache `Coconut.generate` tail) on every example: **0 mismatches / 1319**.
- Slot i = the i-th `<|latent|>` = pass i−1. So the necessity/patching runs' passes 1 and 4 are
  slots 2 and 5. Extra conditions: keep_25 (the patching carriers), keep_1346 (their complement),
  and keep_135 / keep_246 for comparison with CODI.
**Command:**
```
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 <codi-venv>/bin/python scripts/evict_kv_coconut.py \
  --checkpoint_path ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--connordilgren--gpt2-gsm8k-coconut/snapshots/24f1422fcf6d557fd359fc818a4d1d0fde4aac7f/checkpoint_33 \
  --data_file ~/Projects/are-lrms-easily-interpretable/data/gsm_original_test.json --n 0 --check_reference True
```
1256 s on an Apple Silicon CPU (25 conditions + the reference decode), $0.
**Headline results** (n=1319, paired vs full):

| condition | acc | 95% CI | lost | gained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | 0.331 | [0.306, 0.357] | – | – |
| evict_all | 0.082 | [0.068, 0.098] | 356 | 27 |
| keep_only_1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 | 0.089 / 0.138 / 0.094 / 0.149 / 0.187 / 0.221 | | | |
| evict_only_1 / 3 / 4 | 0.327 / 0.328 / 0.324 | | ≤24 | (all p > 0.1) |
| evict_only_2 | 0.296 | | 64 | 18 |
| evict_only_5 | 0.272 | | 104 | 26 |
| evict_only_6 | 0.271 | | 101 | 21 |
| keep_25 / keep_1346 | 0.232 / 0.241 | | | |
| keep_135 / keep_246 | 0.196 / 0.262 | | | |
| evict_band L0-3 / L4-7 / L8-11 | 0.324 / 0.312 / **0.178** | | | |
| keep_band L0-3 / L4-7 / L8-11 | 0.081 / 0.149 / **0.310** | | | |
| merge_mean | 0.141 | [0.123, 0.161] | 276 | 25 |

Full accuracy 0.331 matches the earlier Coconut baseline (0.331 in
`20260927-005834_coconut_necessity-all-replacements`).

**Interpretation:**
- **The answer's attention read is worth ~25 points out of 33** (evict_all 0.082). That is
  proportionally much more than CODI (20 of 42.5). It is consistent with the necessity runs:
  Coconut depends on its latents more than CODI does.
- **Slots 2, 5 and 6 are read; slots 1, 3 and 4 are each free.** Single-slot sufficiency rises with
  position: slot 6 alone recovers 0.221, slot 1 alone nothing (0.089).
- **Read ≠ necessity.** Replacing pass 1 (slot 2) *content* was the most damaging intervention in
  the necessity run (~4× any other pass). Blocking the answer's direct *read* of slot 2 costs
  only 3.5 points. So slot 2 matters mostly by feeding the later thoughts, not by being read at
  answer time. Slot 6, the last thought, was outside the patching analysis and is read directly.
- **The read is almost entirely in layers 8-11.** Keeping only the top band recovers 0.310 of
  0.331, and evicting layers 0-3 or 4-7 is nearly free. Efficiency-wise, about 2/3 of the latent
  KV (layers 0-7) can be dropped for −2 points. CODI can't do this (keep_band L8-11 = 0.262 vs
  0.425).
- **No partial condition is worse than evict_all**, unlike CODI (where keep_246, evict L8-11,
  keep L0-3 and keep L4-7 all fell below evict_all). Coconut's read degrades gracefully and
  roughly additively; CODI's is coordinated.
- **Mean-merging keeps a little** (0.141 vs 0.082). Unlike CODI, the averaged entry isn't worthless.
  But see the caveat: only slots 1-5 are merged here.

**Gotchas hit:** the reference `finish_and_decode` runs without a cache, so a mask that only applies
to answer-phase queries needs query-position awareness. `AttnMasker` now masks only rows with
absolute position >= `ans_start`. For CODI that is every row, so behaviour there is unchanged.
**Caveats:**
- merge_mean merges slots 1-5 only. Slot 6's K/V is produced inside the answer-phase pass, so it
  isn't in the cache yet at merge time; it is evicted with 2-5. So this isn't identical to CODI's
  6-slot merge.
- The additive mask renormalises the softmax onto the remaining keys (same caveat as CODI).
- Greedy only, one checkpoint; fp32/CPU.
**Next:** a value-zero variant for both methods; depth2 needs trained Coconut/CODI checkpoints
(none exist yet).
