## 2026-10-17 — pythia-160m-deduped (12 layers) few-shot no-CoT on depth2: L1 0.00, L2 0.01, reach 0 (baseline_fewshot_nocot, run_id: 20261017-230419_baseline_fewshot_nocot_depth2-fewshot-pythia-160m-deduped)

**Goal:** For depth2 (rule chain), does the number of rules a pretrained model can chain without CoT grow with its layer count? One model of the depth-vs-layers scan (Pythia, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Ouro loops).
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_fewshot_nocot`, EleutherAI/pythia-160m-deduped (released base weights, not fine-tuned), 12 layers, compute_steps=0.
**Data:** synthetic-depth2 test (generator 2.0.0), n=2400; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'n_shots': 6, 'shot_seed': 0, 'shot_source': 'train, same level', 'per_level': 200, 'cot_per_level': 50, 'max_new': 6, 'cot_max_new': 200, 'reach_floor': 0.08, 'loops': None, 'cot_loops': None, 'decoding': 'greedy', 'backend': 'vllm'}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh run` -> `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py --model EleutherAI/pythia-160m-deduped --max-len 2048 ...` on RunPod A100 SXM 80GB (secure).
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.008` (pooled over levels; not the useful number). no-CoT per level 1 -> 0.00, 2 -> 0.01, 3 -> 0.01, 4 -> 0.02, 5 -> 0.01, 6 -> 0.01, 7 -> 0.01, 8 -> 0.01, 9 -> 0.01, 10 -> 0.01, 11 -> 0.01, 12 -> 0.01; reach 0; 50% crossing None. CoT reference (overall 0.003): 1 -> 0.00, 2 -> 0.02, 3 -> 0.00, 4 -> 0.00, 5 -> 0.00, 6 -> 0.00, 7 -> 0.00, 8 -> 0.00, 9 -> 0.00, 10 -> 0.02, 11 -> 0.00, 12 -> 0.00.
**Interpretation:** Scan design (shared by all 20 runs of this scan, 2026-10-17/18): pretrained base models, no fine-tuning; 6-shot `Question: ...\nAnswer: N` prompts with shots drawn from depth2 train at the same level as the query (shot_seed 0); greedy, at most 6 new tokens, stop at newline; first 200 test items per level (levels 1-12; Ouro: levels 1-4 only, see gotchas). CoT reference: same shots with the applied arithmetic written out (`83-18=65. The answer is 65.`), first 50 items per level (Ouro: 20). Reach = largest L such that every level <= L has Wilson 95% lower bound above 0.08 (about 2x the shortcut floors: majority answer 0.03-0.04, first-/last-rule-only <= 0.05 for L >= 2). Summary table and plot: `scripts/depth_scaling_summary.py`. Across the scan: no model has reach above 1. Accuracy at 1 rule grows with scale (Qwen2.5 0.19 at 0.5B to 0.97 at 32B; Qwen3 0.14 to 0.92), but accuracy at 2 rules stays at or near floor in every model (max 0.10, Qwen2.5-32B, 64 layers), while the fine-tuned 12-layer GPT-2 no-CoT model gets 0.77 at 2 rules and 0.49 at 3 (`20261014-021704_filler_tokens_v2-depth2-nocot-25ep`). Same-depth pairs: Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (both 28 layers) 0.14 vs 0.28 at L1; Qwen3-4B vs 8B (both 36) 0.84 vs 0.84; Qwen2.5-7B (28 layers) beats Qwen2.5-3B (36 layers) at L1, 0.61 vs 0.39. Ouro-1.4B at fixed weights: loops 1-4 (24-96 effective layers) lift L1 0.16 -> 0.51 but leave L2 at floor (0.01-0.04); Ouro-2.6B, loops 1-4 (48-192 effective layers): L1 0.25 -> 0.90, L2 0.03-0.04, while its CoT reference is 0.90 at L2 and 0.65 at L3. At L2 the larger Qwen2.5 models mostly answer with a one-rule result (14B/32B: ~22% the rule-1 intermediate, ~20% rule 2 applied to the start). Reading: in-context, without CoT, these models do about one rule per forward pass regardless of layer count (24-64 layers, or up to 192 effective for Ouro), so the answer to 'does depth reach track layers' is no in this regime: the limit is not layer count but what the pretrained circuits do in one pass; fine-tuning a 12-layer model gets past it.
**Gotchas hit:** /workspace on this pod is MooseFS: huggingface_hub file locks hang forever there, so the HF `.locks` dir is symlinked to local disk (in depth_scan.sh). vLLM 0.10.2 needs transformers pinned to 4.56.2 (5.x breaks its tokenizer cache). The host rebooted once mid-scan (00:27 UTC); finished runs were on /workspace and survived, the remaining 7 were relaunched. vLLM runs log n_params=None (nominal size used in the summary). Ouro: HF bs=1 (batched decode is broken, see scripts/ouro_gate.py) made all 12 levels ~6 h for both models, so Ouro was rerun on levels 1-4 only (everything else is at floor from L2 on).
**Caveats:** One prompt format, one shot seed, no prompt search; base models only (no instruct). 200 items per level (95% CI about +-7 pt at 0.5). Layer count, width, params and training data co-vary within each family; the same-depth pairs and Ouro loops are the only controls, and they are few. Few-shot no-CoT is a lower bound on what the weights can do (the fine-tuned GPT-2 shows the task is learnable at 12 layers). Pythia <= 1.4B cannot execute one rule even with CoT (CoT L1 <= 0.20), so its no-CoT curve says nothing about depth. CoT reference n=50 per level. The pod had no .git, so `git.commit` is unknown; code = `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` + `scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Not run: (a) prompt variants (more shots, mixed-level shots, an instruct model) to test whether the one-rule ceiling is a prompting artifact; (b) fine-tune Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (same 28 layers) or GPT-2 small/medium/large no-CoT on depth2 to ask the layer question where models actually chain; (c) Ouro with a depth2 fine-tune, loops as the depth knob.

Reading: in-context, without CoT, these models do about one rule per forward pass regardless of layer count (24-64 layers, or up to 192 effective for Ouro), so the answer to 'does depth reach track layers' is no in this regime: the limit is not layer count but what the pretrained circuits do in one pass; fine-tuning a 12-layer model gets past it.
**Gotchas hit:** /workspace on this pod is MooseFS: huggingface_hub file locks hang forever there, so the HF `.locks` dir is symlinked to local disk (in depth_scan.sh). vLLM 0.10.2 needs transformers pinned to 4.56.2 (5.x breaks its tokenizer cache). The host rebooted once mid-scan (00:27 UTC); finished runs were on /workspace and survived, the remaining 7 were relaunched. vLLM runs log n_params=None (nominal size used in the summary). Ouro: HF bs=1 (batched decode is broken, see scripts/ouro_gate.py) made all 12 levels ~6 h for both models, so Ouro was rerun on levels 1-4 only (everything else is at floor from L2 on).
**Caveats:** One prompt format, one shot seed, no prompt search; base models only (no instruct). 200 items per level (95% CI about +-7 pt at 0.5). Layer count, width, params and training data co-vary within each family; the same-depth pairs and Ouro loops are the only controls, and they are few. Few-shot no-CoT is a lower bound on what the weights can do (the fine-tuned GPT-2 shows the task is learnable at 12 layers). Pythia <= 1.4B cannot execute one rule even with CoT (CoT L1 <= 0.20), so its no-CoT curve says nothing about depth. CoT reference n=50 per level. The pod had no .git, so `git.commit` is unknown; code = `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` + `scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Not run: (a) prompt variants (more shots, mixed-level shots, an instruct model) to test whether the one-rule ceiling is a prompting artifact; (b) fine-tune Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (same 28 layers) or GPT-2 small/medium/large no-CoT on depth2 to ask the layer question where models actually chain; (c) Ouro with a depth2 fine-tune, loops as the depth knob.

## 2026-10-17 — Qwen2.5-0.5B (24 layers) few-shot no-CoT on depth2: L1 0.19, L2 0.03, reach 1 (baseline_fewshot_nocot, run_id: 20261017-234329_baseline_fewshot_nocot_depth2-fewshot-qwen2.5-0.5b)

**Goal:** For depth2 (rule chain), does the number of rules a pretrained model can chain without CoT grow with its layer count? One model of the depth-vs-layers scan (Pythia, Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Ouro loops).
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_fewshot_nocot`, Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B (released base weights, not fine-tuned), 24 layers, compute_steps=0.
**Data:** synthetic-depth2 test (generator 2.0.0), n=2400; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'n_shots': 6, 'shot_seed': 0, 'shot_source': 'train, same level', 'per_level': 200, 'cot_per_level': 50, 'max_new': 6, 'cot_max_new': 200, 'reach_floor': 0.08, 'loops': None, 'cot_loops': None, 'decoding': 'greedy', 'backend': 'vllm'}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh run` -> `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B --max-len 4096 ...` on RunPod A100 SXM 80GB (secure).
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.032` (pooled over levels; not the useful number). no-CoT per level 1 -> 0.19, 2 -> 0.03, 3 -> 0.03, 4 -> 0.01, 5 -> 0.01, 6 -> 0.01, 7 -> 0.02, 8 -> 0.02, 9 -> 0.02, 10 -> 0.02, 11 -> 0.01, 12 -> 0.01; reach 1; 50% crossing None. CoT reference (overall 0.070): 1 -> 0.60, 2 -> 0.18, 3 -> 0.00, 4 -> 0.02, 5 -> 0.00, 6 -> 0.00, 7 -> 0.00, 8 -> 0.02, 9 -> 0.00, 10 -> 0.02, 11 -> 0.00, 12 -> 0.00.
**Interpretation:** Scan design (shared by all 20 runs of this scan, 2026-10-17/18): pretrained base models, no fine-tuning; 6-shot `Question: ...\nAnswer: N` prompts with shots drawn from depth2 train at the same level as the query (shot_seed 0); greedy, at most 6 new tokens, stop at newline; first 200 test items per level (levels 1-12; Ouro: levels 1-4 only, see gotchas). CoT reference: same shots with the applied arithmetic written out (`83-18=65. The answer is 65.`), first 50 items per level (Ouro: 20). Reach = largest L such that every level <= L has Wilson 95% lower bound above 0.08 (about 2x the shortcut floors: majority answer 0.03-0.04, first-/last-rule-only <= 0.05 for L >= 2). Summary table and plot: `scripts/depth_scaling_summary.py`. Across the scan: no model has reach above 1. Accuracy at 1 rule grows with scale (Qwen2.5 0.19 at 0.5B to 0.97 at 32B; Qwen3 0.14 to 0.92), but accuracy at 2 rules stays at or near floor in every model (max 0.10, Qwen2.5-32B, 64 layers), while the fine-tuned 12-layer GPT-2 no-CoT model gets 0.77 at 2 rules and 0.49 at 3 (`20261014-021704_filler_tokens_v2-depth2-nocot-25ep`). Same-depth pairs: Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (both 28 layers) 0.14 vs 0.28 at L1; Qwen3-4B vs 8B (both 36) 0.84 vs 0.84; Qwen2.5-7B (28 layers) beats Qwen2.5-3B (36 layers) at L1, 0.61 vs 0.39. Ouro-1.4B at fixed weights: loops 1-4 (24-96 effective layers) lift L1 0.16 -> 0.51 but leave L2 at floor (0.01-0.04); Ouro-2.6B, loops 1-4 (48-192 effective layers): L1 0.25 -> 0.90, L2 0.03-0.04, while its CoT reference is 0.90 at L2 and 0.65 at L3. At L2 the larger Qwen2.5 models mostly answer with a one-rule result (14B/32B: ~22% the rule-1 intermediate, ~20% rule 2 applied to the start). Reading: in-context, without CoT, these models do about one rule per forward pass regardless of layer count (24-64 layers, or up to 192 effective for Ouro), so the answer to 'does depth reach track layers' is no in this regime: the limit is not layer count but what the pretrained circuits do in one pass; fine-tuning a 12-layer model gets past it.
**Gotchas hit:** /workspace on this pod is MooseFS: huggingface_hub file locks hang forever there, so the HF `.locks` dir is symlinked to local disk (in depth_scan.sh). vLLM 0.10.2 needs transformers pinned to 4.56.2 (5.x breaks its tokenizer cache). The host rebooted once mid-scan (00:27 UTC); finished runs were on /workspace and survived, the remaining 7 were relaunched. vLLM runs log n_params=None (nominal size used in the summary). Ouro: HF bs=1 (batched decode is broken, see scripts/ouro_gate.py) made all 12 levels ~6 h for both models, so Ouro was rerun on levels 1-4 only (everything else is at floor from L2 on).
**Caveats:** One prompt format, one shot seed, no prompt search; base models only (no instruct). 200 items per level (95% CI about +-7 pt at 0.5). Layer count, width, params and training data co-vary within each family; the same-depth pairs and Ouro loops are the only controls, and they are few. Few-shot no-CoT is a lower bound on what the weights can do (the fine-tuned GPT-2 shows the task is learnable at 12 layers). Pythia <= 1.4B cannot execute one rule even with CoT (CoT L1 <= 0.20), so its no-CoT curve says nothing about depth. CoT reference n=50 per level. The pod had no .git, so `git.commit` is unknown; code = `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` + `scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Not run: (a) prompt variants (more shots, mixed-level shots, an instruct model) to test whether the one-rule ceiling is a prompting artifact; (b) fine-tune Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (same 28 layers) or GPT-2 small/medium/large no-CoT on depth2 to ask the layer question where models actually chain; (c) Ouro with a depth2 fine-tune, loops as the depth knob.

CoT reference: same shots with the applied arithmetic written out (`83-18=65. The answer is 65.`), first 50 items per level (Ouro: 20). Reach = largest L such that every level <= L has Wilson 95% lower bound above 0.08 (about 2x the shortcut floors: majority answer 0.03-0.04, first-/last-rule-only <= 0.05 for L >= 2). Summary table and plot: `scripts/depth_scaling_summary.py`. Across the scan: no model has reach above 1. Accuracy at 1 rule grows with scale (Qwen2.5 0.19 at 0.5B to 0.97 at 32B; Qwen3 0.14 to 0.92), but accuracy at 2 rules stays at or near floor in every model (max 0.10, Qwen2.5-32B, 64 layers), while the fine-tuned 12-layer GPT-2 no-CoT model gets 0.77 at 2 rules and 0.49 at 3 (`20261014-021704_filler_tokens_v2-depth2-nocot-25ep`). Same-depth pairs: Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (both 28 layers) 0.14 vs 0.28 at L1; Qwen3-4B vs 8B (both 36) 0.84 vs 0.84; Qwen2.5-7B (28 layers) beats Qwen2.5-3B (36 layers) at L1, 0.61 vs 0.39. Ouro-1.4B at fixed weights: loops 1-4 (24-96 effective layers) lift L1 0.16 -> 0.51 but leave L2 at floor (0.01-0.04); Ouro-2.6B, loops 1-4 (48-192 effective layers): L1 0.25 -> 0.90, L2 0.03-0.04, while its CoT reference is 0.90 at L2 and 0.65 at L3. At L2 the larger Qwen2.5 models mostly answer with a one-rule result (14B/32B: ~22% the rule-1 intermediate, ~20% rule 2 applied to the start). Reading: in-context, without CoT, these models do about one rule per forward pass regardless of layer count (24-64 layers, or up to 192 effective for Ouro), so the answer to 'does depth reach track layers' is no in this regime: the limit is not layer count but what the pretrained circuits do in one pass; fine-tuning a 12-layer model gets past it.
**Gotchas hit:** /workspace on this pod is MooseFS: huggingface_hub file locks hang forever there, so the HF `.locks` dir is symlinked to local disk (in depth_scan.sh). vLLM 0.10.2 needs transformers pinned to 4.56.2 (5.x breaks its tokenizer cache). The host rebooted once mid-scan (00:27 UTC); finished runs were on /workspace and survived, the remaining 7 were relaunched. vLLM runs log n_params=None (nominal size used in the summary). Ouro: HF bs=1 (batched decode is broken, see scripts/ouro_gate.py) made all 12 levels ~6 h for both models, so Ouro was rerun on levels 1-4 only (everything else is at floor from L2 on).
**Caveats:** One prompt format, one shot seed, no prompt search; base models only (no instruct). 200 items per level (95% CI about +-7 pt at 0.5). Layer count, width, params and training data co-vary within each family; the same-depth pairs and Ouro loops are the only controls, and they are few. Few-shot no-CoT is a lower bound on what the weights can do (the fine-tuned GPT-2 shows the task is learnable at 12 layers). Pythia <= 1.4B cannot execute one rule even with CoT (CoT L1 <= 0.20), so its no-CoT curve says nothing about depth. CoT reference n=50 per level. The pod had no .git, so `git.commit` is unknown; code = `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` + `scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Not run: (a) prompt variants (more shots, mixed-level shots, an instruct model) to test whether the one-rule ceiling is a prompting artifact; (b) fine-tune Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (same 28 layers) or GPT-2 small/medium/large no-CoT on depth2 to ask the layer question where models actually chain; (c) Ouro with a depth2 fine-tune, loops as the depth knob.

**Gotchas hit:** /workspace on this pod is MooseFS: huggingface_hub file locks hang forever there, so the HF `.locks` dir is symlinked to local disk (in depth_scan.sh). vLLM 0.10.2 needs transformers pinned to 4.56.2 (5.x breaks its tokenizer cache). The host rebooted once mid-scan (00:27 UTC); finished runs were on /workspace and survived, the remaining 7 were relaunched. vLLM runs log n_params=None (nominal size used in the summary). Ouro: HF bs=1 (batched decode is broken, see scripts/ouro_gate.py) made all 12 levels ~6 h for both models, so Ouro was rerun on levels 1-4 only (everything else is at floor from L2 on).
**Caveats:** One prompt format, one shot seed, no prompt search; base models only (no instruct). 200 items per level (95% CI about +-7 pt at 0.5). Layer count, width, params and training data co-vary within each family; the same-depth pairs and Ouro loops are the only controls, and they are few. Few-shot no-CoT is a lower bound on what the weights can do (the fine-tuned GPT-2 shows the task is learnable at 12 layers). Pythia <= 1.4B cannot execute one rule even with CoT (CoT L1 <= 0.20), so its no-CoT curve says nothing about depth. CoT reference n=50 per level. The pod had no .git, so `git.commit` is unknown; code = `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` + `scripts/pod/depth_scan.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Not run: (a) prompt variants (more shots, mixed-level shots, an instruct model) to test whether the one-rule ceiling is a prompting artifact; (b) fine-tune Qwen3-0.6B vs 1.7B (same 28 layers) or GPT-2 small/medium/large no-CoT on depth2 to ask the layer question where models actually chain; (c) Ouro with a depth2 fine-tune, loops as the depth knob.

## 2026-10-18 — Qwen2.5-7B 24shot no-CoT on depth2 L1-4: L1 0.69, L2 0.05 (baseline_fewshot_nocot, run_id: 20261018-031657_baseline_fewshot_nocot_depth2-fewshot-qwen2.5-7b-24shot)

**Goal:** Prompt check for the depth2 layer scan: is the one-rule no-CoT ceiling of pretrained models (every model, 24-64 layers, at floor from 2 rules) an artifact of an unclear 6-shot prompt? Conditions: base models with 24 shots instead of 6; instruct models with an explicit instruction, 0 and 6 shots.
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_fewshot_nocot`, Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B (released weights, not fine-tuned), 28 layers, compute_steps=0. Condition: 24-shot completion prompt (base model).
**Data:** synthetic-depth2 test, levels 1-4, first 100 items per level (n=400); run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'n_shots': 24, 'shot_seed': 0, 'shot_source': 'train, same level', 'per_level': 100, 'levels': [1, 2, 3, 4], 'cot_per_level': 0, 'max_new': 6, 'cot_max_new': 200, 'reach_floor': 0.08, 'loops': None, 'cot_loops': None, 'decoding': 'greedy', 'backend': 'vllm', 'chat': False, 'instruction': None, 'thinking': None, 'force_number': False}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/depth_prompt_check.sh run` -> `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` (see eval args in hyperparams) on RunPod A40 (secure).
**Headline results:** no-CoT per level 1 -> 0.69, 2 -> 0.05, 3 -> 0.02, 4 -> 0.02; bare-number rate 1.00. L2 answers: 0.06 = the rule-1 intermediate, 0.21 = rule 2 applied to the start. Reference: 6-shot base run 20261017-235730 (L1 0.61, L2 0.02).
**Interpretation:** Across the 6 conditions the 2-rule accuracy stays at or near floor (0.02-0.05; best 0.13 for Qwen3-8B-Base at 24 shots, 95% CI about 0.08-0.21, n=100) while 1-rule accuracy is 0.69-0.87. More shots and an explicit instruction move L1 a little and L2 not at all (the Qwen3 0-shot run is a forcing artifact, see headline). Unconstrained, the instruct models ignore 'answer only the number' from 2 rules on and start writing the steps (smoke test), i.e. they read the task correctly and reach for CoT. Together with the CoT references in the scan (Qwen3-8B-Base 0.66 at L2), this argues against 'the prompt is ambiguous': the models understand the task, do one rule per forward pass, and cannot compose a second one silently without training.
**Gotchas hit:** Qwen3's no-think chat template makes the reply open with a newline, so a newline stop gave empty outputs: chat mode has no newline stop and parses the first non-empty line. argparse reads `--slug-suffix -24shot` as a flag: use `--slug-suffix=-24shot`. Unconstrained instruct replies are CoT, hence `--force-number`.
**Caveats:** 100 items per level (95% CI about +-9 pt at 0.5, about 0.01-0.10 at 0.04). One instruction wording, one shot seed. Digit-constrained decoding forbids any tokens before the answer, which can hurt a model whose preferred first token is text (clearly so for Qwen3 0-shot). 7-8B models only; the scan's 32B is not re-tested here. Pod had no .git: `git.commit` unknown; code = `scripts/depth_scaling_fewshot.py` + `scripts/pod/depth_prompt_check.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** The open test is the tiny fine-tune (LoRA on Qwen3-1.7B with ~200 vs ~5k depth2 no-CoT examples): if a few hundred examples unlock 2 rules, the gap was task specification; if it needs tens of thousands (as GPT-2 did), it is a skill the weights lack.

## 2026-10-18 — Qwen3-1.7B-Base LoRA n=0 on depth2 no-CoT: L1 0.15, L2 0.01, L3 0.01 (baseline_no_cot, run_id: 20261018-033935_baseline_no_cot_depth2-lora-qwen3-1.7b-base-n0)

**Goal:** Does a small answer-only fine-tune unlock 2+ rule no-CoT chaining that prompting could not (layer scan: every pretrained model at floor from 2 rules; prompt check: 24 shots / explicit instruction give at most 0.13 at 2 rules)? A few hundred examples fixing it would mean the ceiling was task specification; needing thousands would mean a skill the weights have to learn. One point of a 0/200/1k/5k/20k curve.
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_no_cot` (fine-tuned no-CoT), Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-Base, 28 layers, frozen; untrained reference: the base model with the same zero-shot prompt (no shots), no adapter. compute_steps=0. Architecture diagram: claude.ai artifact "Depth2 LoRA Setup".
**Data:** train = nested prefix of one level-interleaved shuffle of depth2 train, levels 1-4 (0 test questions overlap with train). Test = first 200 items per level, levels 1-4 (n=800); seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'train_n': 0, 'train_levels': [1, 2, 3, 4], 'train_subset': 'nested prefix of one level-interleaved shuffle', 'data_seed': 0, 'lr': 0.0002, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 0, 'min_passes': 10000, 'min_epochs': 2, 'lora_rank': 16, 'lora_alpha': 32, 'lora_targets': 'all-linear', 'schedule': 'cosine, 3% warmup', 'per_level': 200, 'decoding': 'greedy, 6 tokens', 'prompt': "zero-shot 'Question: ...\\nAnswer:'"}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/lora_depth2.sh run` -> `scripts/lora_depth2.py` (one process, all sizes, fresh adapter per size) on RunPod A40 (secure).
**Headline results:** per level 1 -> 0.15, 2 -> 0.01, 3 -> 0.01, 4 -> 0.01; unparseable 0.000.
**Interpretation:** Whole curve: n=0: L1 0.15 / L2 0.01; 200: 0.90 / 0.12; 1k: 0.99 / 0.36; 5k: 1.00 / 0.57 (L3 0.10); 20k: 1.00 / 0.88 (L3 0.21, L4 0.07). 200 examples teach the format (L1 0.15 -> 0.90, above the best prompt's 0.87) but leave L2 at the prompting ceiling (0.12 vs 0.13); L2 then climbs steadily with data (0.36, 0.57, 0.88) and L3 starts to move only at 5k-20k. So the one-rule ceiling of the pretrained models is not a prompt / task-specification artifact: composing a second rule in one pass is a skill that takes thousands of examples to learn, and each extra rule takes more. A 1.7B pretrained model learns L2 from far less data than GPT-2 small (0.88 from 20k x 2 epochs on levels 1-4, vs GPT-2's 0.77 from 100k x 25 epochs on levels 1-12, `20261014-021704_filler_tokens_v2-depth2-nocot-25ep`), but GPT-2 is better at L3/L4 (0.49 / 0.27 vs 0.21 / 0.07), plausibly because it trained far longer.
**Gotchas hit:** The image's python is PEP 668-managed: install into a `--system-site-packages` venv. Training throughput about 37 examples/s on the A40 (bf16, batch 32).
**Caveats:** One seed, one LR, rank 16, no hyperparameter search; small sizes get many epochs (200 x 50) so passes are not equal across sizes (min 10k, 20k gets 40k). ## 2026-10-18 — Qwen3-1.7B-Base truncated to 7/28 layers, LoRA n=20000, depth2 no-CoT: L1 0.07, L2 0.05 (baseline_no_cot, run_id: 20261018-042915_baseline_no_cot_depth2-lora-qwen3-1.7b-base-keep7-n20000)

**Goal:** Layer-count comparison with everything else fixed: same width, tokenizer, pretraining and fine-tuning data, only the number of decoder blocks differs (first k of 28 kept). Does the number of rules a model can chain without CoT grow with k?
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_no_cot` (fine-tuned no-CoT), Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-Base with only its first 7 decoder blocks (final norm + tied LM head kept), frozen; LoRA r=16 on all linears; identical recipe to the full-depth n=20000 run (20k answer-only examples, levels 1-4, 2 epochs, 1250 steps, lr 2e-4, batch 32). compute_steps=0.
**Data:** same nested 20k training subset as the full-depth runs; test = first 200 items per level, levels 1-4 (n=800); seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'train_n': 20000, 'keep_layers': 7, 'train_levels': [1, 2, 3, 4], 'train_subset': 'nested prefix of one level-interleaved shuffle', 'data_seed': 0, 'lr': 0.0002, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 2, 'min_passes': 10000, 'min_epochs': 2, 'lora_rank': 16, 'lora_alpha': 32, 'lora_targets': 'all-linear', 'schedule': 'cosine, 3% warmup', 'per_level': 200, 'decoding': 'greedy, 6 tokens', 'prompt': "zero-shot 'Question: ...\\nAnswer:'"}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/lora_depth2.sh depth` -> `scripts/lora_depth2.py --sizes 20000 --keep-layers 7,14,21` on RunPod A40 (secure).
**Headline results:** per level 1 -> 0.07, 2 -> 0.05, 3 -> 0.03, 4 -> 0.02; final training loss 0.89.
**Interpretation:** Depth curve: k=7: L1 0.07 / L2 0.05 (final train loss 0.89); k=14: 0.14 / 0.07; k=21: 0.90 / 0.13 (loss 0.65); k=28 (full model, run 20261018-041131 n=20000): 1.00 / 0.88, L3 0.21 (loss 0.41). Read naively it is a staircase (7-14 layers: nothing, 21: one rule, 28: two rules and some of three), but the 7- and 14-layer models fail even one rule, which the full model learns from 1k examples, and their training loss stays high. One rule does not plausibly need 21 layers, so the shallow failures mostly measure that cutting late pretrained layers removes skills (arithmetic, mapping to output tokens) a rank-16 adapter cannot rebuild, not a serial-depth limit. The informative contrast is 21 vs 28 (both do one rule; only 28 does two), but even that is confounded by what the removed layers knew. Suggestive of depth mattering for composition, not a clean test.
**Gotchas hit:** none beyond the earlier LoRA runs (PEP 668 venv).
**Caveats:** One seed, one recipe tuned for nothing; LoRA rank 16 on a truncated model may be the bottleneck (full fine-tuning or higher rank might recover more); 2 epochs only; 200 test items per level. Truncation keeps the earliest layers, so 'depth' here also means 'which pretrained layers survive'. Pod had no .git: `git.commit` unknown; code = `scripts/lora_depth2.py` (`--keep-layers`) + `scripts/pod/lora_depth2.sh depth` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Cleaner depth tests: (a) full fine-tune (or high-rank LoRA) of the truncated models so capacity to repair is not the limit, checking that 1-rule accuracy recovers before reading 2+ rules; (b) Ouro fine-tuned and evaluated at 1-4 loops (depth varies, parameters fixed); (c) small fixed-width transformers trained from scratch at 2-16 layers.

**Interpretation:** Depth curve: k=7: L1 0.07 / L2 0.05 (final train loss 0.89); k=14: 0.14 / 0.07; k=21: 0.90 / 0.13 (loss 0.65); k=28 (full model, run 20261018-041131 n=20000): 1.00 / 0.88, L3 0.21 (loss 0.41). Read naively it is a staircase (7-14 layers: nothing, 21: one rule, 28: two rules and some of three), but the 7- and 14-layer models fail even one rule, which the full model learns from 1k examples, and their training loss stays high. One rule does not plausibly need 21 layers, so the shallow failures mostly measure that cutting late pretrained layers removes skills (arithmetic, mapping to output tokens) a rank-16 adapter cannot rebuild, not a serial-depth limit. The informative contrast is 21 vs 28 (both do one rule; only 28 does two), but even that is confounded by what the removed layers knew. Suggestive of depth mattering for composition, not a clean test.
**Gotchas hit:** none beyond the earlier LoRA runs (PEP 668 venv).
**Caveats:** One seed, one recipe tuned for nothing; LoRA rank 16 on a truncated model may be the bottleneck (full fine-tuning or higher rank might recover more); 2 epochs only; 200 test items per level. Truncation keeps the earliest layers, so 'depth' here also means 'which pretrained layers survive'. Pod had no .git: `git.commit` unknown; code = `scripts/lora_depth2.py` (`--keep-layers`) + `scripts/pod/lora_depth2.sh depth` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Cleaner depth tests: (a) full fine-tune (or high-rank LoRA) of the truncated models so capacity to repair is not the limit, checking that 1-rule accuracy recovers before reading 2+ rules; (b) Ouro fine-tuned and evaluated at 1-4 loops (depth varies, parameters fixed); (c) small fixed-width transformers trained from scratch at 2-16 layers.

## 2026-10-18 — T5-efficient-base nl2 (2+2 layers) full fine-tune, depth2 no-CoT: L1 0.10, L2 0.04 — below the 1-rule gate (null) (baseline_no_cot, run_id: 20261018-202745_baseline_no_cot_depth2-t5eff-base-nl2)

**Goal:** Layer-count comparison where nothing is cut away: google/t5-efficient-base-nl{2..48} share width (768), tokenizer, C4 pretraining and recipe and differ only in layer count, each pretrained at its own depth. Does the number of depth2 rules a model chains without CoT grow with depth? Follows the Qwen truncation runs, which were confounded by removing pretrained layers.
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_no_cot` (fine-tuned no-CoT), google/t5-efficient-base-nl2, 2 encoder + 2 decoder layers, 58M params, full fine-tune (no LoRA), compute_steps=0.
**Data:** train = first 30k of one level-interleaved shuffle of depth2 train, levels 1-6; test = first 200 items per level, levels 1-6 (n=1200); seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'train_n': 30000, 'train_levels': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 'train_subset': 'nested prefix of one level-interleaved shuffle', 'data_seed': 0, 'lr': 0.0003, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 3, 'optimizer': 'AdamW, wd 0, full fine-tune, bf16 autocast', 'schedule': 'cosine, 3% warmup', 'per_level': 200, 'decoding': 'greedy, 6 tokens', 'prompt': "encoder 'Question: ...', target = answer"}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/t5_depth2.sh run` -> `scripts/t5_depth2.py` (depths 2,4,8,12,16,24,32,48 planned) on RunPod A40 (secure).
**Headline results:** per level 1 -> 0.10, 2 -> 0.04, 3 -> 0.00, 4 -> 0.02, 5 -> 0.03, 6 -> 0.01; final train loss 1.93; train 143s.
**Interpretation:** Null at every depth run: nl2/4/8/12 all score 0.09-0.10 at 1 rule and floor beyond, and the answer-token loss plateaus at about 1.9 within the first ~15% of training at every depth (identical curves). The outputs are numbers close to the gold (65 -> 67, 40 -> 37): the models learned the answer's rough magnitude, not the arithmetic. No depth clears the ~0.9 1-rule gate, so this says nothing about depth vs composition. The scan was stopped after nl12 (the standard t5-efficient-base) rather than spending ~1 h more on nl16-48 with the same recipe. Likely causes: T5's 2021 C4 pretraining has little arithmetic, and its tokenizer treats 2-digit numbers as atomic and inconsistent tokens ('▁65' vs '▁' + '66' vs '▁' + '93'), so each rule is a lookup table to learn from scratch; GPT-2 (also atomic numbers) needed 100k x 25 epochs (~2.5M examples) where this recipe gives 90k.
**Gotchas hit:** First pod (EU-SE-1, 194.68.245.25:22019) accepted TCP on the direct SSH port but never sent an SSH banner although sshd was up; the proxy worked with a PTY only. Terminated and recreated; the second pod on the same host IP worked. Local env lacks peft, so t5_depth2.py does not import from lora_depth2.py.
**Caveats:** One recipe (AdamW 3e-4, batch 32, 3 epochs, bf16 autocast), no LR search; a plateau this flat may also mean the LR is wrong for T5 (Adafactor 1e-3 is T5's usual fine-tune recipe). nl16-nl48 not run. Pod had no .git: `git.commit` unknown; code = `scripts/t5_depth2.py` + `scripts/pod/t5_depth2.sh` as committed with these runs.
**Next:** Before any deeper T5 runs, get nl12 over the 1-rule gate on a short pilot: (a) digit-split numbers in the input/target (e.g. '6 5'), (b) Adafactor lr 1e-3, (c) ~10x more training. If nothing gets nl12 to L1 >= 0.9 cheaply, drop T5 and use Ouro loops (fine-tuned) as the depth test.

## 2026-10-19 — T5-efficient nl12 rescue recipe: digit-split + Adafactor lifts 1-rule 0.10 -> 0.55, still below the 0.9 gate (baseline_no_cot, run_id: 20261019-034448_baseline_no_cot_depth2-t5eff-base-nl12-digits-ada-50k6ep)

**Goal:** Was the T5-efficient layer scan's floor (nl2-12 all L1 ~0.10, loss plateau ~1.9) a recipe/tokenizer problem? Pilot on nl12 only before re-scanning depths.
**Mechanism / model:** `baseline_no_cot`, google/t5-efficient-base / google/t5-efficient-base + full fine-tune (not saved), compute_steps=0.
**Data:** synthetic-depth2 test n=1200 seed=None; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'train_n': 50000, 'train_levels': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 'train_subset': 'nested prefix of one level-interleaved shuffle', 'data_seed': 0, 'lr': 0.001, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 6, 'optimizer': 'Adafactor (no param scaling, no relative step), full fine-tune, bf16 autocast', 'digit_split_numbers': True, 'schedule': 'cosine, 3% warmup', 'per_level': 200, 'decoding': 'greedy, 6 tokens', 'prompt': "encoder 'Question: ...', target = answer"}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/t5_depth2.sh run --depths 12 --digits --optim adafactor --lr 1e-3 --train-n 50000 --epochs 6 --tag digits-ada-50k6ep` (A40, ran concurrently with the Ouro loop test on the same GPU)
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.167`, `unparseable_rate=0.000`, `compute_steps=0`
**Interpretation:** Per level 1-6: 0.55 / 0.24 / 0.07 / 0.06 / 0.06 / 0.04 (old recipe at nl12: 0.10 / 0.03 / ...). Loss fell 1.45 -> 1.09 and flattened in epochs 5-6 as the cosine schedule ended. Errors stay near misses (L1 median |error| 1, e.g. 40 -> '3 9'). By the 1-rule operation: halve 0.96, double 0.82, but add 0.48 and subtract 0.40 -- odd, since digit-wise add/subtract should be the easy case; the model has learned the rule-and-branch structure but not exact small-offset arithmetic. Splitting digits and switching optimizer was the main fix, but the model still fails the gate (L1 >= 0.9), so this still says nothing about depth vs composition.
**Gotchas hit:** Pod SSH proxy readiness loop never fired, pod idled ~1 h before launch; see the Ouro run notes.
**Caveats:** Single depth, single seed; 50k examples is still ~50x less than GPT-2's synthetic training. L2 0.24 at L1 0.55 is roughly what independent per-step errors would give, so no evidence about composition either way.
**Next:** Not re-scanning T5 depths: the Ouro loop test (same pod) answers the depth question cleanly. If T5 is revisited, train much longer (loss was still moving at epoch 4) or on 1-2 rule levels only to clear the gate first.

## 2026-10-19 — Ouro-1.4B loop-count test, 1 loop(s) of the same LoRA weights (L1-4: see table) (recurrent_depth, run_id: 20261019-042622_recurrent_depth_depth2-lora-ouro-1.4b-n20000-l1)

**Goal:** Does the number of depth2 rules a model chains without CoT grow with depth when parameters, tokenizer, pretraining and fine-tuning data are all fixed? Ouro repeats its 24-layer stack; one LoRA fine-tune (loss on every loop's exit), then the merged weights are scored at 1, 2, 3, 4 loops.
**Mechanism / model:** `recurrent_depth`, ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B / ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B + LoRA trained at 4 loops (not saved), compute_steps=1.
**Data:** synthetic-depth2 test n=800 seed=None; run seed=0.
**Hyperparams:** {'train_n': 20000, 'train_levels': [1, 2, 3, 4], 'train_loops': 4, 'loss': "mean over loops 1..train_loops of answer-token CE at that loop's exit", 'train_subset': 'nested prefix of one level-interleaved shuffle', 'data_seed': 0, 'lr': 0.0002, 'batch_size': 32, 'micro_batch_size': 8, 'epochs': 2, 'lora_rank': 16, 'lora_alpha': 32, 'lora_targets': 'q/k/v/o/gate/up/down proj', 'schedule': 'cosine, 3% warmup', 'per_level': 200, 'decoding': 'greedy, 6 tokens, HF bs=1, adapter merged', 'prompt': "zero-shot 'Question: ...\\nAnswer:'"}
**Command:** `bash scripts/pod/ouro_lora_depth2.sh run` (defaults: 20k answer-only examples over levels 1-4, 2 epochs, LoRA r16 q/k/v/o/gate/up/down, AdamW 2e-4, bs 32 as 4x8 micro, train at 4 loops; eval 200/level, greedy, HF bs=1)
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.484`, `unparseable_rate=0.000`, `compute_steps=1`
**Interpretation:** Same weights, per level 1/2/3/4: 1 loop (24 layer passes) 1.00/0.76/0.14/0.04; 2 loops (48) 1.00/0.93/0.41/0.18; 3 loops (72) 1.00/0.97/0.62/0.30; 4 loops (96) 1.00/0.97/0.68/0.35. Every level at 2+ rules improves monotonically with loops, with gains shrinking from 3 to 4 (trained loop count). Final train CE per exit 0.58/0.33/0.22/0.22 shows the same order. This is the first clean positive in the depth2 depth series: with everything else fixed, more serial depth means more rules chained without CoT. Matches the truncated-Qwen result (1 rule at 21 layers, 2 at 28) in direction, and Ouro at 1 loop (24 layers) already does 2 rules at 0.76.
**Gotchas hit:** The proxy (ssh.runpod.io) readiness loop never reported, so the pod idled ~1 h before launch; the completion monitor only watched the T5 job, so the pod idled ~1 h 50 min after Ouro finished (04:41 -> 06:30 UTC). Pod total ~4.7 h x $0.59 = ~$2.75 for this run plus the T5 pilot, about half of it idle. Use the direct SSH port for readiness checks and watch every job's terminal state.
**Caveats:** One seed, one model size, n=200 per level (95% CI about +-0.07 at 0.5). The 1-3 loop exits were trained directly (loss on every exit), so this is 'depth as a trained readout', not extrapolation; loops > 4 untested. Training ran at 4 loops, so the earlier exits saw gradients shaped by later loops. Levels 5+ not evaluated.
**Next:** Loops 5-8 at eval (does reach keep growing past the trained depth?), levels 5-6, and a second seed. Probe per-loop hidden states for the intermediate values (rule 1 result decodable at loop 1, rule 2 at loop 2?): a direct test of the serial-composition-per-loop story.

(1) The run was paused with SIGSTOP for ~13 h to stop it slowing Coconut; on SIGCONT the NCCL watchdog saw a 13.8 h all-reduce and aborted (SIGABRT). Relaunched under the same name: run.py resumed from checkpoint_1 (weights only, fresh AdamW state), losing ~22% of epoch 2. Do not SIGSTOP torchrun jobs. (2) The plateau watcher had no minimum epoch count; added `--min-epochs 12` (= KEEP_CKPT) so checkpoint_12 must exist. (3) `select no_cot` excludes checkpoint_12 from the last 3 (it assumes the plateau comes after 12); passed CKPTS="10 11 12" by hand.
**Caveats:** One seed. The plateau rule (0.5 pt on 360 monitor items = 2 items over 3 epochs) is noisy; it stopped at the earliest allowed epoch, and L1 0.76 suggests more training would still help. d50 2.35 is a lower bound on single-pass reach; the 25-epoch train_synthetic.py run (different stack, context only) gave 3.04. Optimizer state reset at epoch 2 (resume).
**Next:** Envelope + d50 bootstrap with no_thoughts, CODI-0 and student-only. Consider a longer no-CoT run (e.g. fixed 25+ epochs) as a sensitivity check on d50 if the envelope's L2-L4 matters for the onset prediction.

**Hyperparams:** {'recipe': 'TRAINING_PROTOCOL.md section 7.3 (CODI @2c23146 + codi_streaming/synthetic/model_fixes patches)', 'num_latent': 6, 'include_last_cot': False, 'fix_attn_mask': True, 'pad_invariant': True, 'lr': 0.003, 'scheduler': 'cosine', 'warmup_ratio': 0.03, 'epochs': 40, 'lora_r': 128, 'lora_alpha': 32, 'per_device_train_batch_size': 32, 'gradient_accumulation_steps': 4, 'effective_batch': 128, 'bf16': True, 'max_grad_norm': 2.0, 'weight_decay': 0.1, 'save_total_limit': 3}
**Command:** `env TASK=depth2 INCLUDE_LAST_COT=False EXP_NAME=gpt2_depth2_codi EXTRA_ARGS="--per_device_train_batch_size 32 --gradient_accumulation_steps 4" bash configs/synthetic/train_gpt2_depth_codi.sh` (env: lrm_work/env.sh). Smoke run passed first; padding check RESULT: OK.
**Headline results:** No eval: training diverged. Losses normal through epoch 6 (student CE ~0.6, distill ~0.18, teacher CE ~0.02). Grad norm at epoch 6.10: 22, then 1016 (6.11), 8.0e3, 2.9e7 (6.14), inf from 6.15; student CE to ~12, teacher CE to ~7; NaN in every loss from epoch 6.69. Ran on NaN until stopped by hand at step ~29,140 / 31,280 (~13 h of GPU time). train_log.json = trainer log_history.
**Interpretation:** A failed run of the protocol recipe, not a result about CODI's latents. Warning signs before the blow-up: teacher CE spikes at epoch 1.5 (to 3.6) and from epoch 5.95 (~1.6, sustained). At epoch 6 of 40 the cosine schedule is still near peak (lr 2.88e-3). The 32x4 micro-batch (protocol fallback, since 64x2 needs ~68 GB) is an unlikely cause: the only batch-dependent term is `distill_loss /= ref_selected.std()` (src/model.py:387), a std over micro-batch x 768 values, nearly identical at 32 and 64. The v1 CODI run (20261012-034825) used the same lr at 32x4 without diverging, but on a 10-epoch cosine (lr ~1e-3 by epoch 6).
**Gotchas hit:** (1) My log monitor filtered out loss lines, so the NaN went unnoticed for ~13 h; all CODI-stack runs now run with lrm_work/codi_guard.sh (stops on the first NaN loss or 3 inf grad norms). (2) `--save_total_limit 3` rotated away every pre-divergence checkpoint; reruns keep all epochs (`--save_total_limit 40`, selection rule unchanged). (3) First launch at the protocol's 64x2 took 68.6 GB next to the CoT job and was stopped after ~1 min (log gpt2_depth2_codi.bs64-aborted.log).
**Caveats:** Shared GPU 7 with the CoT run, the Coconut timing test and Coconut c1m6 during training (speed only).
**Next:** User decision 2026-11-01: rerun at the protocol's exact 64x2 (`gpt2_depth2_codi_bs64`, GPU 4, NaN guard, all epochs kept). If it diverges again near epoch 6, the recipe itself is unstable on RuleChain -> decide a recipe change (lower lr / tighter clipping) for CODI, CODI-0 and student-only together.

**Hyperparams:** {'recipe': 'TRAINING_PROTOCOL.md section 7.3, student-only: NUM_LATENT 0, ref_loss_factor 0, distill_loss_factor 0', 'lr': 0.003, 'scheduler': 'cosine', 'epochs': 40, 'lora_r': 128, 'lora_alpha': 32, 'per_device_train_batch_size': 64, 'gradient_accumulation_steps': 2, 'bf16': True, 'max_grad_norm': 2.0, 'save_total_limit': 40}
**Command:** `lrm_work/queue_gpu7_v7.sh` / `queue_gpu7_v8.sh` -> `env TASK=depth2 INCLUDE_LAST_COT=False EXP_NAME=gpt2_depth2_codi_student NUM_LATENT=0 REF_LOSS_FACTOR=0 DISTILL_LOSS_FACTOR=0 EXTRA_ARGS="--save_total_limit 40" bash configs/synthetic/train_gpt2_depth_codi.sh` (+ RESUME_FROM=checkpoint-5474 for the resume), NaN guard lrm_work/codi_guard.sh.
**Headline results:** No eval. Attempt 1 (18:08 PT) crashed at the first checkpoint save (upstream logging bug with zero-weighted losses; fixed by scripts/codi_zero_loss_log.patch, smoke-tested). Attempt 2 (20:24, fresh): stable to epoch 7.2 (student CE ~0.72, grad norm ~0.03), then CE 0.79 -> 7.4 -> 10.4 -> ~28 within 0.03 epochs, grad norm 250 -> 2e7 -> inf; the guard stopped it at step 5,900 (4 inf grad norms). Attempt 3 (21:36, user decision: resume from checkpoint-5474 = epoch 7, same recipe and seed): same spike at epoch 7.29-7.31 (restored RNG -> same batches), brief recovery to CE 2.9, then grad norm 4e10 and CE ~10; stopped by hand at epoch 7.63 (huge but finite grad norms do not trip the guard). Dropped. train_log.json = log_history to epoch 7.
**Interpretation:** With the teacher and distillation losses off, CODI's recipe (lr 3e-3, LoRA r128) diverges on RuleChain at the protocol's exact batch, so the instability is in the recipe (lr), not the micro-batch or the distillation terms. Across the CODI-stack runs: CODI 32x4 diverged (epoch 6.1), CODI 64x2 and CODI-0 64x2 completed, student-only 64x2 diverged twice (7.3). The protocol lists student-only as the first run to drop; CODI-0 remains CODI's matched reference and the envelope uses the other references.
**Gotchas hit:** (1) Zero-weighted-loss logging bug (above). (2) Resuming from the last good checkpoint restores the RNG and data order, so it replays the same batches; a different seed or data order would be needed to test whether the spike is batch-specific. (3) codi_guard.sh only stops on NaN loss or 3 inf grad norms; a finite blow-up (grad 1e8-1e10, CE 10-28) ran ~5 min past the spike before it went inf. Worth adding a CE/grad-norm ceiling to the guard.
**Caveats:** One seed; no eval of the pre-divergence epoch-7 checkpoint (not a protocol checkpoint).
**Next:** If a LoRA no-CoT health check is still wanted: rerun at a lower lr (e.g. 1e-3) and say it is not CODI-0's recipe; otherwise build the envelope without it (protocol section 2).

## 2026-11-02 — RuleChain CODI latent diagnostics: CODI needs 1-2 latents (k=0 drops 0.40 -> 0.22) but they rehost, not extend, CODI-0's computation; train-test gap 0.19-0.30 at L4-L8 (codi, run_id: 20261102-225018_codi_v2-depth2-codi-latent-diagnostics)

**Goal:** Debug round 1's null gain (CODI = CODI-0 on RuleChain, `RULECHAIN_RESULTS.md` on `kevin/lrm-training-1`). Three checks on the selected CODI checkpoint: (1) does it use its latents (latent-count sweep at inference, k = 0..12 on a model trained with 6); (2) where its answer-position state matches the teacher, per hidden-state layer and level (the distillation objective); (3) train vs test accuracy per level (memorisation). Paired with the same diagnostics on CODI-0: `20261102-225353_codi_v2-depth2-codi0-latent-diagnostics`.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, GPT-2 small + LoRA r128 + projection, `gpt2_depth2_codi_bs64/checkpoint-31280` (epoch 40, the checkpoint behind round-1 run 20261102-000204; downloaded copy in `rulechain-checkpoints/`, sha256-verified against Kevin's SHA256SUMS). Trained with 6 latents, `pad_invariant`, `include_last_cot False`.
**Data:** RuleChain (depth2, generator 2.0.0) test, all 6000 items (500/level), hashes verified; train check = 500 seeded-random items/level from `train.json`.
**Hyperparams:** see manifest. Teacher-forced: one forward through question, `<bot>`, k latents, `<eot>`, "The answer is:", argmax answer token at ":" (the distillation position). No generation: round-1 logged teacher-forced accuracy equals generated accuracy within +-0.004/level, and k=6 here reproduces round 1's teacher-forced numbers (L4 0.758 vs 0.756, L5 0.442 vs 0.436; MPS fp32 vs H100 bf16). Distillation loss as CODI's: SmoothL1(student, teacher) / teacher std per layer, mean over the 13 hidden-state layers; std over the whole set, not per batch of 128 as in training.
**Command:** `scripts/diagnose_codi_latents.py` from the CODI checkout (`../codi` @ 2c23146 + codi_streaming / codi_synthetic / codi_model_fixes / codi_zero_loss_log patches, own venv = upstream pins minus CUDA packages), see `eval_command.txt`. `--latent_counts 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,12 --train_per_level 500 --batch_size 32`, MPS, PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO 0.7.
**Headline results:** `final_answer_accuracy=0.402` (teacher-forced, k=6), `early_termination_necessity=0.177` (k=6 minus k=0). Teacher 1.000 at every level.

| k (latents at inference) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 6 (trained) | 8 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| overall | 0.225 | 0.389 | 0.398 | 0.401 | 0.401 | 0.402 | 0.401 | 0.401 |
| L3 | 0.334 | 0.988 | 0.990 | 0.992 | 0.992 | 0.992 | 0.992 | 0.992 |
| L4 | 0.100 | 0.716 | 0.754 | 0.756 | 0.754 | 0.758 | 0.758 | 0.752 |
| L5 | 0.064 | 0.382 | 0.422 | 0.428 | 0.432 | 0.442 | 0.452 | 0.444 |
| distill loss | 0.136 | 0.104 | 0.095 | 0.091 | 0.089 | 0.088 | 0.087 | 0.089 |

CODI-0 (no latents, its own run): overall 0.407, L3 0.964, L4 0.764, L5 0.498, distill 0.141.

Per-layer distillation loss (layer 0 = embeddings): CODI k=6 vs CODI-0 — L1-5 both ~0.002-0.006; **L6 0.004 vs 0.045, L7 0.054 vs 0.113, L8 0.058 vs 0.258**, L9 0.166 vs 0.305, L10 0.306 vs 0.407, L11 0.402 vs 0.457, L12 0.112 vs 0.214. CODI with k=0 is worse than CODI-0 at layers 1-5 (0.016-0.023).

Train vs test accuracy (k=6): L4 0.948 / 0.758, L5 0.728 / 0.442, L6 0.542 / 0.238, L7 0.332 / 0.110, L8 0.260 / 0.090, L9-12 train 0.15-0.23 vs test 0.04-0.05. L1-3 no gap.

**Interpretation:**
- **CODI depends on its latents, but only on the first one or two.** Removing all latents collapses L3 from 0.99 to 0.33 and L4 from 0.76 to 0.10 (overall 0.40 -> 0.22, well below CODI-0's 0.41: dependence, not added computation, per the protocol's rule). One latent restores almost everything (0.389), two saturate; latents 3-6 and extra ones at 8/12 change nothing. So CODI moved part of the computation CODI-0 does inside the answer pass into latent pass 1(-2), without adding reach: the same ~5-rule envelope, split over two forward passes instead of one. Six latents were available; the model behaves as if it had one.
- **The latents buy teacher-state similarity in the middle layers, not answer accuracy.** CODI's answer-position state is much closer to the teacher's at layers 6-9 than CODI-0's (L8 0.058 vs 0.258), and per level the gap is largest at L2-3 (0.013-0.017 vs 0.036-0.097) where both are already right. At L5-12 distill stays high (0.08-0.14) and accuracy is CODI-0's. The 30% lower training distillation loss (trainer_state) is this: closer imitation of the teacher's representation where the answer is computable anyway.
- **Both models memorise beyond their reach.** At L4-L8 train accuracy exceeds test by 0.17-0.30 (CODI-0: 0.21-0.43, see its run). 40 epochs over the same 100k items: at levels a single pass can't compute, the CE and distillation losses are lowered by fitting individual training items. That is a competing, easier route than learning to chain rules across latents, and it explains the training loss still falling at epoch 40 while test accuracy is flat.
- Together: there was pressure on the latents (teacher at 1.000, student far from it at k >= 5), but the losses were satisfied by (a) rehosting the in-reach computation into latent 1 and (b) memorising out-of-reach items, not by using latents 2-6 for later rules.

**Gotchas hit:** (1) The Mac slept during the first launch, then the run swapped (30 GB): CODI's eval helpers call the LM-head model on full sequences, building [B, T, 50k] logits (~5 GB/batch at L12) that are never used. `diagnose_codi_latents.py` runs the teacher and question passes through the transformer body (identical numbers on a smoke set, checked) and caps MPS memory; `scripts/eval_codi.encode_and_think` itself is unchanged. (2) Checkpoints were saved on CUDA: the script maps `torch.load` to CPU when CUDA is absent. (3) zsh does not word-split `$VAR` arguments: the runner is a bash script.
**Caveats:** One checkpoint, one seed (11). Truncating to k < 6 is off-distribution for CODI (never trained with fewer latents), so part of the k=0 drop may be distribution shift rather than lost computation; the resample-swap test (latents from another item of the same level) is the in-distribution version and is not run yet. Distillation losses of CODI and CODI-0 are each against their own teacher (same recipe, different weights; teacher stds differ, e.g. layer 11 8.6 vs 11.5), so the cross-model comparison is approximate; within-CODI comparisons across k are exact. Train sample 500/level (95% CI about +-0.04). Teacher-forced, not generated, accuracy.
**Next:** Resample swap and per-latent probes for v1, v2 (does latent 1 hold an intermediate value?). Retraining fixes this points to: fresh items every epoch (RuleChain is generated, so memorisation can be removed outright), and pressure to spread work over latents (step supervision per latent, or a curriculum that varies the latent count).

## 2026-11-02 — RuleChain CODI latent swap + probes: latent-1 input irrelevant, latents 2-6 essential (0.40 -> 0.11) but not transplantable (follows donor 0.04); intermediate values weakly and flatly decodable (codi, run_id: 20261102-232507_codi_v2-depth2-codi-swap-probes)

**Goal:** Follow-up to `20261102-225018_codi_v2-depth2-codi-latent-diagnostics` (CODI needs 1-2 latents, matches CODI-0). (1) The protocol's primary necessity test, in-distribution: resample swap of latents between items of the same level, plus mean/zero ablation, split by which latents are swapped. (2) Linear probes for the intermediate values v1..v6 and the answer at <bot>, each latent pass and the answer position: do latents hold the chain's values, one per rule? CODI-0 counterpart: `20261102-232815_codi_v2-depth2-codi0-swap-probes`.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, `gpt2_depth2_codi_bs64/checkpoint-31280` (epoch 40, behind round-1 run 20261102-000204), 6 latents, pad_invariant.
**Data:** RuleChain (depth2) test, all 6000 items; probes trained on 500 seeded-random train items per level (same sample as the diagnostics run).
**Hyperparams:** see manifest. z_1 = prj(h_<bot>), z_{j+1} = prj(h of latent pass j); latent pass j consumes z_j. Donor = random test item of the same level with a different answer (seed 5980). swap_all: all z_j from the donor, fixed. swap_z1: donor z_1, then the model's own passes. swap_rest: own z_1, donor z_2..z_6 fixed. mean_all: train-sample mean z_j. Readout: teacher-forced answer token at ":" (equals generation within +-0.004/level on these checkpoints). Probes: 100-class linear softmax on standardised features of one position and layer (0, 2, ..., 12), Adam 300 full-batch steps, weight decay 1e-3; target v_j only on items with >= j rules.
**Command:** `scripts/probe_swap_codi_latents.py` from `../codi` (CODI venv), see `eval_command.txt`; MPS, batch 32.
**Headline results:** clean teacher-forced accuracy 0.402. `intervention_accuracy` (swap_all, follows donor) = 0.045.

| condition | keeps own | follows donor | L2 own/donor | L3 own/donor | L4 own/donor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| clean | 0.402 | - | 1.00 | 0.99 | 0.76 |
| swap_z1 | **0.399** | 0.008 | 1.00 / 0.00 | 0.99 / 0.00 | 0.76 / 0.00 |
| swap_rest (z2-z6) | **0.113** | 0.042 | 0.06 / 0.13 | 0.01 / 0.12 | 0.04 / 0.07 |
| swap_all | 0.105 | 0.045 | 0.03 / 0.13 | 0.01 / 0.12 | 0.03 / 0.09 |
| mean_all | 0.181 | - | 0.62 | 0.17 | 0.08 |
| zero_all | 0.198 | - | 0.84 | 0.27 | 0.09 |

Probes, best test accuracy over layers (majority baseline): v1 (0.015): <bot> 0.167, z1-z6 0.152-0.156, ans 0.102. v2 (0.023): <bot> 0.096, z1-z6 0.113-0.117, ans 0.100. v3 (0.023): 0.049 / 0.080-0.087 / 0.083. v4-v6: <= 0.06. answer (0.020): <bot> 0.058, z1-z6 0.10, **ans 0.384** (model accuracy 0.402). CODI-0 (same probes, its run): v1 at <bot> **0.395**, v2 0.184, v3 0.104; answer at ans 0.375.

**Interpretation:**
- **What CODI uses is the computation of the later latent passes, not the latent-1 input.** Swapping z_1 changes nothing: latent pass 1 recomputes from the question. Replacing z_2..z_6 destroys accuracy down to 0.11 (below CODI-0's 0.41, and below CODI with no latents at all, 0.22). Mean and zero ablation also fall below CODI-0. By the protocol's rule this is dependence: the model routes its answer through the latent positions.
- **The latents are not transplantable.** Under a swap only 4% of answers become the donor's (12-13% at L2-L3), most become a third value. The donor's latents only make sense with the donor's question in context; what flows through them is not a self-contained "current value".
- **The latents do not hold a readable chain of values.** v_j is about as (in)decodable from z_1 as from z_6 (v2: 0.113 vs 0.117; v3: 0.080 vs 0.087): no progression one rule per latent. CODI-0's single <bot> position holds v1 and v2 more decodably (0.395, 0.184) than any CODI position (0.167, 0.117). The answer is readable only at the answer position (0.384, matching model accuracy, so the probe works when the information is linearly present).
- Combined with the diagnostics run: CODI's latents are a necessary but opaque channel. They neither add reach over CODI-0 nor carry per-rule intermediate values; the computation that matters seems to be spread over the positions in a way that only works with the item's own question.

**Gotchas hit:** none new (same memory settings as the diagnostics run).
**Caveats:** **Probes overfit heavily** (train 0.96 vs test 0.15 for v1 at z1; 6000 training items for a 768x100 probe, ~60 per class): absolute probe accuracies are lower bounds, and "not decodable" here means "not linearly decodable with this data". The CODI vs CODI-0 comparison uses identical probes, items and training, so the relative statement (CODI-0's <bot> holds v1/v2 better) is fairer than the absolute numbers. Probes are pooled over levels, not split per level. One checkpoint, one seed. One donor per item.
**Next:** Stronger probes (more train items, e.g. 2000/level; PCA or stronger L2; per-level splits; digit-wise targets). Activation patching of single latent positions (which position carries the answer-relevant signal). For retraining: fresh items per epoch (memorisation) and per-latent step supervision, since the unsupervised latents end up as an opaque channel.

## 2026-11-02 — RuleChain CODI logit lens: the 6 latents collapse to one repeated vector (within-item cos >= 0.987) that reads as "a number" and hits one of the item's intermediate values 30% of the time, with no per-rule order (codi, run_id: 20261102-233815_codi_v2-depth2-codi-logit-lens)

**Goal:** Training-free counterpart to the linear probes of `20261102-232507_codi_v2-depth2-codi-swap-probes` (which overfit): project hidden states at <bot>, latent passes 1-6 and the answer position (":") through GPT-2's final LayerNorm + tied unembedding, at layers 0, 2, ..., 12, and check whether the top tokens are the item's intermediate values v_1..v_k. CODI's paper reads GSM8K latents the same way. CODI-0 counterpart: `20261102-233932_codi_v2-depth2-codi0-logit-lens`.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, `gpt2_depth2_codi_bs64/checkpoint-31280` (epoch 40, round-1 run 20261102-000204), 6 latents, pad_invariant.
**Data:** RuleChain (depth2) test, all 6000.
**Hyperparams:** see manifest. Layer 0 at a latent position = the fed vector z_j (+ position embedding); layer 12 is post-ln_f in HF GPT-2, other layers get ln_f applied. A token "counts" as value v if it spells v with or without a leading space (all 0..99 are single tokens). "any_intermediate" = top-1 equals any of the item's v_1..v_{k-1}.
**Command:** `scripts/logit_lens_codi_latents.py` from `../codi`, see `eval_command.txt`. Collapse check (ad hoc, same checkpoint, 50 test items/level = 600, `probe_swap_codi_latents.run`): cosines and norms of the fed vectors z_1..z_6.
**Headline results:**
- **Latent positions, layer 0 (the fed vectors):** top-1 is a number token 84% of the time; it equals one of the item's intermediate values 30-32% (chance ~ 0.84 x 5.5 distinct intermediates / 100 values ~ 0.05); v1 0.070, v2 0.081, v3 0.067-0.070, v4 0.044-0.047 (top-5: v1 0.13, v2 0.15). **Identical for z1 through z6** (any_intermediate 0.301 / 0.312 / 0.315 / 0.315 / 0.317 / 0.315). Layers 2-12 at latent positions: falls to ~0 (layer 12 top tokens are '-', ',', '.').
- **Answer position, layer 12:** answer top-1 0.402 (= model accuracy); v1-v4 0.10-0.12 (mostly items where v_j is the answer or equal to it). Layers 0-8: no numbers.
- **<bot>:** nothing (top tokens 'The', ' of').
- **Collapse check:** within an item, cos(z_i, z_j) = 0.987-0.989 between z1 and the rest, 0.997-1.000 among z2..z6. Across items, cos 0.73-0.76 at every position. Norm ~44 for every z_j vs 3.96 for token embeddings (11x).

**Interpretation:**
- **CODI's six latents are one vector repeated.** After the first latent pass the recurrence sits at a fixed point (z2..z6 cos >= 0.997 with each other). That explains the earlier results directly: one latent recovers almost all accuracy (`20261102-225018`), extra latents at 8/12 change nothing, swapping z1 does nothing (pass 1 recomputes the fixed point from the question), and swapping z2..z6 breaks the model (the answer attends to five copies of another item's vector). This is the "homogeneous latents" failure SIM-CoT (Wei et al., ICLR 2026) reports for Coconut/CODI without step-level supervision.
- **The vector does carry item content, in token-embedding space:** read through the unembedding it is a number ~84% of the time and one of the item's own intermediate values ~30% (about 6x chance), but with no order: v1, v2, v3 are equally likely at every latent position. It looks like one blended "intermediate-number" embedding per item, not a chain v1 -> v2 -> v3.
- Latent hidden states inside the passes (layers 2-12) do not decode to numbers; the answer appears in the vocabulary basis only at the answer position's last layer.

**Gotchas hit:** none.
**Caveats:** Logit lens only sees what is aligned with the unembedding; information in other directions is invisible to it (the probes are the complement, with their own overfitting caveat). Layer-0 readout of z_j is a reading of the projection output, a vector 11x larger than any token embedding, so "decodes to a number" is about its direction only. The collapse check is on 600 items and was not saved as its own run; numbers above are from the session log. Chance baseline is approximate (assumes uniform numbers). One checkpoint, one seed.
**Next:** Same lens and collapse check on the released GSM8K CODI (`zen-E/CODI-gpt2`): if its latents are not collapsed and decode in order there (as CODI's paper and the LessWrong analysis suggest), the RuleChain collapse is task/training-specific. For retraining on RuleChain: per-latent step supervision (SIM-CoT style) directly targets the collapse; fresh items per epoch target the memorisation found in `20261102-225018`.

**Addendum (2026-11-02, same session): the collapse holds at every layer, not just the fed vectors.** Same 600 items,
hidden states of latent passes 1-6 at all 13 layers. Raw cosine within an item: z1 vs z2..z6 0.978-0.997, among z2..z6
0.995-0.999 at every layer (raw cosines in GPT-2's middle layers are inflated by its outlier dimensions: different items
also reach 0.68-0.86 there; at layer 12, after ln_f, different items are 0.11 while one item's latents stay 0.978/0.995).
After subtracting the per-layer mean over items and positions: z1 vs z2..z6 0.944-0.975, among z2..z6 0.993-0.996,
different items ~0.00; only 0.9-1.7% of the variance at any layer is between the latent positions of an item, the rest
is between items. So each latent pass computes nearly the same state as the previous one at every depth: a fixed point
of the whole pass, not just of the projection.

## 2026-11-02 — Released GSM8K CODI: latents NOT collapsed (only 1-2% vs 58-77% of variance between positions on RuleChain vs GSM8K); odd latents decode to operators, even latents to the item's intermediate values (47-56%) (codi, run_id: 20261102-235641_codi_gsm8k-released-lens-collapse)

**Goal:** Is the latent collapse found on RuleChain (`20261102-233815_codi_v2-depth2-codi-logit-lens` + addendum: six latents = one repeated vector, within-item centred cos >= 0.94 at every layer) a general CODI property, which would undercut prior CODI results, or specific to RuleChain / our training? Same logit lens and collapse statistics on the authors' released GSM8K GPT-2 CODI.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, `zen-E/CODI-gpt2` @ fd641b3 (local HF cache; 43.7% paper / 41.9% our eval in `20260918-021217_codi_released-weights-6lat`), 6 latents, trained with upstream masking (no pad_invariant).
**Data:** GSM8K-Aug test, all 1319, file order. Intermediate values from `Example.intermediate_values` (the `<<...=x>>` results); a top-1 token counts as v if it is the first token of v (with or without a leading space).
**Hyperparams:** batch size 1 (no padding, so upstream masking is exact), fp32, MPS. Lens = final LayerNorm + tied unembedding (layer 12 already normed). Collapse statistics as in the RuleChain addendum (raw / centred within-item cosine across latent positions, share of variance between positions).
**Command:** `scripts/gsm8k_codi_lens_collapse.py --ckpt_dir <HF snapshot>`, see `eval_command.txt`.
**Headline results:** teacher-forced first-token accuracy 0.434 (sanity, matches 41.9-43.7%).
- **Logit lens, layer 12 of each latent pass:** latents 1/3/5 decode to operator / bracket tokens ('-', '/', ' <<', '>>', '*'; number 0.2-0.7%); latents 2/4/6 decode to numbers 89-92% of the time and to one of the item's intermediate values **56% / 48% / 47%**. By step: latent 2 = step 1 0.24, **step 2 0.30**, step 3 0.09; latent 4 = 0.22 / 0.18 / **0.12** / 0.07; latent 6 = 0.21 / 0.18 / 0.12 / 0.07.
- **Collapse statistics:** centred within-item cosine 0.08-0.33 across layers (RuleChain 0.94-0.98); **share of variance between latent positions 0.56-0.77** (RuleChain 0.009-0.017). Centred cosine at layer 12: odd latents resemble each other (1-3 0.49, 3-5 0.80), even latents too (2-4 0.69, **4-6 0.94**), odd vs even ~0.02-0.14.
**Interpretation:**
- **The collapse is not a general CODI property.** On GSM8K the latents are distinct states with a period-2 structure: an "operator" latent then a "number" latent, which is what CODI's paper reports from decoding its latents. The number latents hold the item's own intermediate results about half the time, at the last layer (the state that becomes the next latent input). On RuleChain the same method gives one repeated vector whose readable content sits only at the projection output and has no order.
- Ordering on GSM8K is partial: latent 2 favours steps 1-2, latents 4/6 shift weight toward step 3, and latents 4 and 6 are nearly the same (0.94): the chain does not keep advancing to step 4+ (mean GSM8K-Aug rationale ~3 steps, so 6 latents = 3 operator/number pairs cover most items).
- Together with the GSM8K necessity results (41.9% -> 23.8% with latents truncated, `20260918-*`), this argues against "CODI's latents never mattered in prior work". The RuleChain null is specific: a task where one pass already reaches ~5 rules and values are single tokens, plus 40 epochs over 100k items (memorisation). Whether the latents account for all of CODI's gain over No-CoT on GSM8K still needs the CODI-0 GSM8K control.
**Gotchas hit:** CODI's resized vocabulary has ids past the tokenizer (added tokens) that `decode` cannot render: number detection limited to `len(tokenizer)`.
**Caveats:** Logit lens sees only unembedding-aligned content; "first token of v" over-counts multi-token values that share a first token (e.g. '1' for 12, 150). Teacher-forced first token, not the paper metric. One released checkpoint (seed 11). Different training conditions from our RuleChain checkpoint (upstream masking, include_last_cot False on GSM8K too, 385k items x 40 epochs), so "task vs training" is not separated by this run alone.
**Next:** CODI-0 on GSM8K (cost estimate in session: ~$18-25 for a 20-epoch RunPod run, or free on cci-p124). On RuleChain: retrain with fresh items per epoch and/or per-latent step supervision to see whether the collapse lifts.

## 2026-11-03 — Released GSM8K CODI: seen train items 0.796 vs test 0.425 (+0.21 to +0.47 within every step count); memorisation (or an easier train distribution) is present on GSM8K too, where the latents do not collapse (codi, run_id: 20261103-001945_codi_gsm8k-released-train-vs-test)

**Goal:** Free test of the memorisation hypothesis for the RuleChain CODI null. On RuleChain both CODI and CODI-0 fit training items they cannot compute (train-test gaps 0.17-0.43 at L4-L8, `20261102-225018`, `20261102-225353`) and CODI's latents collapse (`20261102-233815`). GSM8K CODI's latents do not collapse (`20261102-235641`). If GSM8K CODI shows no comparable train-test gap, memorisation is a candidate for what differs; if it shows one, memorisation alone does not cause the collapse.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, `zen-E/CODI-gpt2` @ fd641b3 (released; trained on all 385,620 GSM8K-Aug train rows, 40 epochs), 6 latents.
**Data:** "seen" = the repo's fixed 1000-item `split="validation"` carve-out of GSM8K-Aug train (all in CODI's training data); test = GSM8K-Aug test, all 1319.
**Hyperparams:** batch size 1 (no padding, upstream masking exact), greedy, `eval_codi.generate_batches`; paper metric (last number) for prediction and gold (a few train golds carry units, e.g. "$165"); shared `score_outputs` agrees. Stratified by the number of `<<...>>` steps (6 = 6+).
**Command:** `scripts/gsm8k_codi_train_vs_test.py`, see `eval_command.txt`. ~8 min on MPS.
**Headline results:** test 0.425 (matches the 41.9-43.7% on record), seen train **0.796**, gap **+0.371**. By step count, seen vs test: 1 step 0.87 / 0.40 (n=142/65), 2 steps 0.87 / 0.66 (404/357), 3 steps 0.80 / 0.49 (267/364), 4 steps 0.70 / 0.31 (122/290), 5 steps 0.37 / 0.14 (41/138), 6+ 0.25 / 0.07 (24/87). Gap +0.18 to +0.47 at every step count.
**Interpretation:**
- GSM8K CODI is far better on items it trained on than on test, by about as much as RuleChain CODI at its middle levels (RuleChain L5: 0.73 vs 0.44, L6: 0.54 vs 0.24). Within each step count the gap stays 0.2-0.5, so it is not just that train items are shorter.
- Yet GSM8K CODI's latents are distinct and structured (56-77% of variance between positions, operator/number alternation). So **fitting training items does not by itself produce the latent collapse**: memorisation (H3 in the team list) is weakened as the sole explanation for RuleChain. It may still matter in combination (e.g. on RuleChain memorisation is the alternative to latents for exactly the out-of-reach items, while on GSM8K latents are needed even for short items: no-latent accuracy is 24%).
- Remaining top candidates for the RuleChain collapse: the single-pass shortcut (H4: one pass reaches ~5 rules on RuleChain vs ~24% no-latent accuracy on GSM8K), budget mismatch (H2: up to 11 steps for 6 latents vs ~3 steps on GSM8K), and the learning rate / instability (H1).
**Gotchas hit:** First full run crashed after the seen split on a gold answer "$165" (float parse); gold now parsed with the same last-number rule as predictions.
**Caveats:** **Distribution shift is not controlled:** GSM8K-Aug train is model-generated augmentation of GSM8K train, test is the original GSM8K test, so part of the gap may be that train items are easier, not memorised. Step-count stratification controls only length. No held-out item from the train distribution exists for this model (it trained on all of train). One released checkpoint.
**Next:** To separate memorisation from shift on GSM8K, a CODI(-0) trained with the 1000-item carve-out held out would give a same-distribution unseen set (the GSM8K CODI-0 run could do this for free by training on `split="train"`). For RuleChain: the collapse-over-epochs check (needs Kevin's 40 epoch checkpoints) and the combined retrain (lr 1e-3, fresh data, levels 1-6).

## 2026-11-03 — Released ProsQA CODI: latents are one constant vector for every item and position (98.7-99.9% of energy shared, raw cross-item cos >= 0.995); 0 latents = 6 latents (0.820 vs 0.816) (codi, run_id: 20261103-021023_codi_prosqa-released-lens-collapse)

**Goal:** Kevin's question after the RuleChain collapse finding: do CODI latents also collapse on ProsQA/ProntoQA, where our Zhang swap (`20261011-062104`) showed the latents are ignored? Hypothesis: unneeded latents -> the recurrently fed state barely changes. Same collapse statistics as the GSM8K (`20261102-235641`, not collapsed) and RuleChain (`20261102-233815` + addendum, collapsed within item) runs, plus a variance decomposition and 0-latent truncation. ProntoQA counterpart: `20261103-021408_codi_prontoqa-released-lens-collapse`.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, `connordilgren/gpt2-prosqa-codi` (Dilgren & Wiegreffe grid, GPT-2, 6 latents, projection + LN, LoRA r128), loaded with the grid's `CODIInference`.
**Data:** Dilgren & Wiegreffe `prosqa_test.json`, all 500, file order.
**Hyperparams:** batch 1 (no padding), fp32, CPU, greedy, max 48 new tokens; answer = text after "The answer is:", exact match (same as `swap_random_codi.py`). 0-latent condition = question + <bot> + <eot> (off-distribution). Lens = ln_f + tied unembedding. New: decomposition of the uncentred energy ||X||^2 at each layer into constant (grand mean) / position / item / item x position.
**Command:** `scripts/logic_codi_lens_collapse.py --dataset prosqa`, see `eval_command.txt` (codi venv: torch 2.7.1, transformers 4.52.4, peft 0.15.2).
**Headline results:** accuracy 0.816 (matches our Oct 11 run and D&W's 80.0); **0 latents 0.820**. Raw within-item cos 0.999-1.000 and **raw cross-item cos 0.995-1.000** at every layer. Energy share, layer 12: constant **0.987**, item 0.012, position 0.001, item x position 0.0001 (layer 6: constant 0.9985). Logit lens: top-1 is ' truth' (layer 0) / '.' (layer 12) for every item; step-word and question-word hits 0.000 at every layer and position.
**Interpretation:** The collapse here is stronger than on RuleChain: not one vector per item but **one vector for all items**, i.e. a learned constant "thinking" embedding that carries (almost) no input information. Together with 0 latents = 6 latents and the 0% swap effect, the latents are inert padding on ProsQA, consistent with D&W's latent = no-CoT parity. Supports Kevin's hypothesis that unneeded latents stop changing. Three regimes now: GSM8K (latents needed, distinct, stepwise content), RuleChain (needed but collapsed to one item-specific vector, opaque), ProsQA/ProntoQA (not needed, collapsed to a global constant). The cheap diagnostic should report both within-item and cross-item similarity (or the decomposition) to tell the last two apart.
**Gotchas hit:** The centred statistics (centred within-item cos 0.48-0.94, "share of variance between positions" 0.03-0.40) look moderate but describe a residual that is ~1% of the energy; read them with the decomposition. The centred position drift is smooth (cos decays with distance), shared by all items.
**Caveats:** One released checkpoint per task. Lens-based word matching only sees unembedding-aligned content (and ProsQA concept names are multi-token; first-token match). The 1.2% item energy at layer 12 may still carry something a probe could read; not probed. 0-latent condition is off-distribution.
**Next:** Same check on the grid Coconut ProsQA/ProntoQA checkpoints and on Kevin's RuleChain Coconut pilots; add the decomposition to the RuleChain/GSM8K numbers for one comparable table.

## 2026-11-03 — RuleChain k<=8 pilot: Coconut published GSM8K recipe (2x3 = 6 latents), test L1-8 0.180, d50 1.71; null vs no_thoughts_m3 (G -0.004) (coconut, run_id: 20261103-033009_coconut_v2-depth2-pilot_k8_coconut_c2m3)
