## 2026-11-06 — Start-last position and donor tests: CODI's gain now reaches two rules before the last, not just the last rule; everything before the last rule still passes through the latents (codi, run_id: 20261106-105634_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-position-donor)

**Goal:** TRAINING_PROTOCOL section 11.3 position test, donor patch, mediation and same-value donors on the selected pair: does CODI's gain spread to earlier rules once prefill is closed?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2. Start-last CODI (6 latents) and CODI-0, checkpoint-17820, fp32, MPS.
**Data:** 200 test items per level, L3-L7 (position) and L2-L7 (donor). 15,129 threshold edits, 3,764 small edits, 10,000 constructed chains (in `predictions.jsonl`, with both models' answers). 424 different-value and 338 same-value donor pairs answered exactly right. Edited and constructed items are new questions.
**Command:** `scripts/codi_null_audit/`: `FORMAT=startlast b13_resolution`, `a25_position`, `FORMAT=startlast b16_donor`, `a21_donor`. The freeze test was skipped because rule tokens hold no running value here.
**Headline results:**
- **Position.** Right branch, CODI vs CODI-0, on items both answered within 2, by rules left after the edited rule. Margin 1: last rule .550 / .225, 1 left .234 / .138 (p .007), 2 left .455 / .359 (p .013), 3+ left .466 / .414 (p .23). Margin 2: .674 / .322, .323 / .195 (p .0003), .507 / .408 (p .024), .480 / .450 (p .35). Margin 3+: .854 / .508, .508 / .348 (p 3e-5), .600 / .501 (p .001), .561 / .533 (p .41). With the start first, round-1 CODI gained at the last rule only (.81 / .59, then .47 / .51, .59 / .61, .58 / .65).
- **Natural items** with exactly one tight decision, exact wins/losses: last rule 16/2 (p .001), 1 left 5/3, 2 left 6/6, 3+ left 16/10. These do not show a gain before the last rule.
- **Constructed chains**, exact CODI / CODI-0. Wide: L3 .51 / .25, L4 .36 / .17, L5 .20 / .11, L6 .13 / .08, L7 .10 / .06. Tight: L3 .16 / .07, L4 .06 / .03, then both near floor.
- **Mediation.** Share following the donor, through latents / direct route. Edit at the last rule 0.00 / .97. 1 rule left .97 / 0.00. 2 left .68 / 0.00. 3+ left .70 / .04. Own-latent control 1.0.
- **Same-value donors** keep the answer 1.00 / .94 / .94 / .86 at L2-L5. Single latents follow the donor .00-.01; replacing from z_1, z_2, z_3 on gives .88, .76, .49.

**Interpretation:** Section 11.3 stays "latents help", because reach difference is +0.23. But "gain at the last rule only" does not describe this model: on edited items the gain reaches one and two rules before the last and stops by three, which fits about two passes of real work (20261106-101740). The route split is the same as the working start-first models: latents carry everything before the last rule, the answer tokens apply it, and latents act through the value.
**Gotchas hit:** `a20_lasthop.py` is written for the start-first runs, so `a25_position.py` repeats its first two tables for this pair.
**Caveats:** One seed. The position split comes from the earlier post-hoc analysis, though it was pre-registered here. Edited items are conditioned on both models being within 2. Natural items do not confirm the earlier-rule gain, with few items and small counts (5/3, 6/6). Deep edits land on neither answer .26-.32 of the time through latents, unexplained.
**Next:** See 20261106-101740.

## 2026-11-07 — Start-last readability: the value before the last rule reads .63 / .31 / .21 on right answers at L3-L5, beats the no-latent control, and tracks the model's own errors; earlier steps do not beat the control (codi, run_id: 20261107-084635_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-readability-right-wrong)

**Goal:** RQ2 of the paper draft. Pooled reads sat near accuracy (L3 .46 against .52), so were values clear on right answers and absent on wrong ones? Do reads beat the matched no-latent model, and do they reflect what the model actually computed?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2. Start-last CODI (6 latents) and CODI-0, checkpoint-17820; lr-3e-3 CODI as the known relay. fp32, MPS.
**Data:** Valid only, L3-L5, 286 items per level. Probes fit on 8,000 train items of one level; a 4,000 fit reproduces `b20` (L3 h4 layer 2: .46). Right items: 149 / 94 / 39 at L3-L5. `predictions.jsonl` holds start-last CODI's answers and decoded values at h4 layer 2.
**Command:** `codi_audit_artifacts/b23_right_wrong.py`, tables from `a26_right_wrong.py`, under `run_guarded.sh`. Cells fixed in advance (t1, h2, h4, h6, colon at layers 0, 2, 4, 8, 12), and h4 layer 2 is the headline cell, so nothing is picked on scored items.
**Headline results:**
- **Value before the last rule, exact, h4 layer 2, L3 / L4 / L5.** All items .49 / .21 / .12. Right answers .63 / .31 / .21. Wrong answers .33 / .16 / .11. Shuffled labels .01 / .02 / .02.
- **No-latent control.** CODI-0 at the last question token .16 / .04 / .03, at the answer token .19 / .06 / .04.
- **Relay, right answers.** 1.00 / .93 / .79.
- **Raw latent input (h4 layer 0).** .22 / .14 / .09, against .98 / .74 / .44 for the relay. In start-last the value needs one transformer block to read.
- **Own errors.** Applying the last rule to the decoded value gives the model's exact answer on .23 / .21 / .16 of its wrong answers. Using another item's decoded value gives .02 / .02 / .03, and CODI-0's last-token read gives .07 / .05 / .05. A wrong answer can only match if the decoded value is itself wrong, so these are reads of the model's own mistaken value. Relay: .41 at L4, .39 at L5.
- **Earlier steps.** v_1 at h4 layer 12 reads .45 / .28 / .19, against .42 / .26 / .20 for CODI-0 at the last question token, so it does not beat the control. L4 v_2 reads .12 against .08.

**Interpretation:**
- RQ2 profile is late-only, and partial. One value is readable above control and the earlier steps are not, so there is no full rollout.
- Readability is not a null. The read is selective, beats the control, is better on right answers, and follows the model's own wrong values, which is what a monitor needs. It is weak in size: even on right answers it misses 37% at L3 and 69% at L4.
- The hoped-for pattern, clear on right answers and absent on wrong ones, is only partly there: .63 against .33 at L3.
- Used and readable agree only for the group of latents. Single latents are near copies and follow the donor .00-.01 (20261106-105634), so the draft's per-latent cells will read "readable but unused" while replacing the group moves the answer.
- Corrects my earlier statement that the results "already fit the draft's framework". Gain follows the prediction: 0 at k=1, +.02 at k=2, +.24 at k=3 = d50. Reliance does not: all latents ablated takes k=1 from 1.00 to .09 and k=2 from 1.00 to .05 (20261106-105537), though CODI-0 scores 1.00 and .98 with none. The draft's claim table lists "high already at k=1" as refuted.

**Gotchas hit:** None in this run.
**Caveats:** One seed per model. Valid only. Right items are few at L5 (39) and selected for being easy. Linear probes are lower bounds; 4,000 to 8,000 fit items added about .03 at L3. The own-errors test is correlational. The relay has no matched CODI-0.
**Next:** Update the draft's Prediction and claim table to separate need (gain) from reliance (ablation). Run the same analysis on any new start-last arm.

## 2026-11-07 — Round-1 plain Coconut ignores its latents: all six mean-ablated .158 against .155 intact on L2-4, another item's real latents leave 95-98% of answers unchanged, answers follow the donor .019 (coconut, run_id: 20261107-092430_coconut_v2-depth2-coconut-c1m6-latent-ablation)

**Goal:** First necessity test on any plain Coconut model on RuleChain. Does its poor accuracy come with latents it uses badly, or latents it does not use? Protocol section 3's primary test (resample swap within level) had never been run on this stack.
**Mechanism / model:** `coconut`, GPT-2 small, `gpt2_depth2_coconut_c1m6/checkpoint_10` (test record 20261102-022150), 6 latents, CPU fp32.
**Data:** Canonical depth2 test, first 200 items per level, L1-L4 (n=800). Mean latents from 500 train items, one mean per pass, pooled over levels.
**Command:** `scripts/ablate_synthetic_coconut.py --levels 1-4 --window 2-4 --per_level_n 200 --mean_n 500 --device cpu`; full argv in the manifest.
**Headline results:**
- Pooled L2-4 (n=600), exact: intact .155; mean-ablated .158 (p .63); swap same level .152 (p .63), follows donor .019, keeps gold .153; swap other level .157; truncated to 2 latents .155, to 1 .143, to 0 .137 (p .11). Zero .108 and noise .127 cost more.
- Same answer as intact, L2 / L3 / L4: mean-ablated .96 / .96 / .975; swap same level .98 / .95 / .975; truncated to 2 latents .88 / .90 / .95; truncated to 0 .585 / .755 / .905.
- L1: intact .99, mean-ablated .99, swap .99 with every answer unchanged. Zero .425, noise .90.
- Within 2 of gold, intact vs mean-ablated: L2 .635 / .640, L3 .415 / .395, L4 .265 / .255.

**Interpretation:**
- Plain Coconut does not use latent content at any level tested. This is the opposite of the lr-3e-3 and round-1 CODI models, which follow donors .91-1.00 at L2-3 on edits before the last rule.
- The rough value (within 2 far above chance, about .08) survives ablation and donor swaps, so it is computed outside the latents, in the ordinary pass.
- Latent positions matter a little and their content does not: removing positions moves answers (.585 same at L2) with no significant accuracy cost, while replacing content with the mean or a donor's does almost nothing.
- Zero and noise costs are off-distribution damage, not evidence of use: a real donor latent, and the mean, do nothing.
- So "Coconut null" is not a failed chain. There is no latent route at all, even though the single pass fails from L2 on, so a bypass cannot explain it. Why stage-1 training leaves the latents idle is inferred, not tested here: one rule fits in a single pass, so nothing forces latent 1 to hold v_1.

**Gotchas hit:** `scripts/ablate_synthetic_coconut.py` and `latentreasoning/tasks/twins_v2.py` were untracked in the working tree at run time, so this record's script is not yet in git. The mean is pooled over levels, not per depth as the paper draft specifies; the same applies to the CODI ablations.
**Caveats:** One checkpoint, one seed, final checkpoint only, so stage-1 behaviour is not observed. 200 items per level, and correct items are few at L3-4 (30, 12). L1-4 only. Swap "keeps gold" is capped by intact accuracy, so answer stability is the more useful measure.
**Next:** The same battery on the SIM-Coconut checkpoint (cci-p124), which is the open test of whether step supervision routes the work through the latents. If stage checkpoints survive, run it on the stage-1 checkpoint too.

## 2026-11-07 — Attention across latent passes: GSM8K walks forward through the problem, more on longer chains, and stops by the last passes; start-last and the relay freeze after the first latent (codi, run_id: 20261107-093340_codi_attention-across-passes-gsm8k-vs-startlast)

**Goal:** Why does start-last CODI not roll out? One candidate is that nothing tells a pass which rule comes next. GSM8K CODI's harder items settle at later passes, so does its attention move through the problem pass by pass, while start-last's does not?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2, 6 latents. Released GSM8K CODI (`zen-E/CODI-gpt2`), start-last CODI checkpoint-17820, lr-3e-3 CODI as the relay. fp32, MPS, batch 1, so no padding.
**Data:** GSM8K test items with at least 2 steps whose numbers appear in the question: 580 / 236 / 57 / 6 items with 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 mapped steps (5 not reported). RuleChain valid L3-L6 (relay L4-L5), about 286 per level.
**Command:** `codi_audit_artifacts/b24_pointer.py`, tables from `a27_pointer.py` and `a28_pointer_passes.py`. Rows: `<bot>` then passes p0-p5. RuleChain sets are rule tokens; GSM8K sets are question numbers first used in step j. Position 0 is never counted. Centre of mass (COM) runs 0 (first step) to 1 (last).
**Headline results:**
- **Move in COM, p1 to p3, all heads.** GSM8K +.009 / +.028 / +.066 at 2 / 3 / 4 mapped steps. Start-last +.006 / +.005 / +.003 / +.001 at L3-L6. Relay -.003 / -.004.
- **Same, 20 held-out heads.** GSM8K +.036 / +.069 / +.170. Start-last +.022 / +.023 / +.019 / +.015. Relay +.006 / +.005.
- **p3 to p5.** GSM8K +.002 / +.002 / -.005, so the walk has stopped.
- **Mean change in a head's COM, p1 to p3.** GSM8K .10-.12, start-last .01, relay .01.
- **Alternation.** Attention on step tokens at `<bot>`, p1, p3, p5 over p0, p2, p4: GSM8K 2.3-2.6x, start-last .94-1.06x, relay .96-.97x. Those GSM8K passes produce z_0, z_2, z_4 and z_6; z_0, z_2 and z_4 are the sites that carry values under aligned patching.
- **Shares by step, GSM8K 3 steps.** `<bot>` .51 / .25 / .23, p1 .38 / .34 / .27, p3 .38 / .29 / .32, p5 .37 / .30 / .32. **Start-last L4 by rule:** `<bot>` .28 / .23 / .19 / .30, p0 .14 / .12 / .23 / .51, p5 .11 / .11 / .22 / .55. The relay's latents look the same as start-last's.

**Related re-analyses, no new model runs:**
- **Pass sweep by step count**, truncation logged in 20260927-005051, script `codi_audit_artifacts/gsm8k_pass_sweep_by_steps.py`. Accuracy after k = 1-6 latents: 2 steps .37 / .50 / .63 / .63 / .64 / .65; 3 steps .25 / .15 / .43 / .45 / .48 / .49; 4 steps .20 / .11 / .19 / .19 / .29 / .31; 5 steps .10 / .06 / .07 / .05 / .14 / .14. Mean pass where right answers settle: 1.8 / 2.9 / 3.7 / 4.3. Join on `idx`: `load_gsm8k_aug(split="test")` shuffles by default.
- **Twin patches by edited step**, from 20260927-004340, chains of 3+ steps, 61 first-step and 136 later edits. Single z_0 follows the twin .49 against .18 (recipient-bootstrap difference +.21 to +.41), z_2 .15 against .29, z_4 .41 against .46. Post hoc, one checkpoint.

**Interpretation:**
- GSM8K CODI has pointer-like behaviour that start-last lacks. It grows with chain length and stops where accuracy stops rising.
- This does not show that a missing pointer causes the fixed point. Near-copy latents must give near-identical attention, so start-last's freeze follows from the fixed point either way. Only an intervention can separate them.
- GSM8K's three reading passes, the sites that carry values and the jumps in accuracy line up, from three separate measurements.

**Gotchas hit:** My first summary, a slope over all rows, was dominated by the jump from `<bot>` to the first latent, which even the relay has, so it was dropped for same-parity moves between latent passes. The tokenizer here has no offsets, so they come from token bytes, checked against question length. The pass sweep first ran on a misaligned join (1,303 gold mismatches); it was discarded and rerun, with 0 mismatches.
**Caveats:** Attention is not use. GSM8K sets cover digits in the question only, and questions often give numbers in solving order, so position and step are confounded. RuleChain sets are whole rules, so the two tasks are compared on shape, not size. Released model only; 57 items at 4 mapped steps.
**Next:** Rule-gated latents test the cause directly. Kevin could repeat this on his GSM8K checkpoint.

## 2026-11-07 — Rule-gated start-last CODI: test L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.982; pooled L5-L6 gain over ungated CODI +0.861 [+0.840, +0.882], 861/0, pre-registered ROLLOUT (codi, run_id: 20261107-204814_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-gated-depth2-codi)

**Goal:** Pre-registered test (TRAINING_PROTOCOL section 12). Ungated start-last CODI stops after about two passes and fails at L5-L7 with passes unused. If each latent pass is shown one rule, so it is told which rule comes next, does the model carry a value through the latents, one rule per pass? No values or step labels are given.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2, num_latent 6, `--rule_gate True` (`scripts/codi_rule_gate.patch`, class `RuleGate`) in training and every eval. Otherwise the start-last CODI arm (20261106-083843): section 10.2 recipe (lr 2e-3 cosine, adam_beta2 0.98, adam_epsilon 1e-6, max_grad_norm 1.0, LoRA r128/a32, 64 x 2, bf16, seed 11), 12 epochs, RunPod A40 (pod y545w15vxjl80p, $0.59/h, about 11 pod-hours).
**Data:** `synthetic_data_v2_l1to7w_startlast`, the same files as 20261106-083843. Test = canonical L1-L7, 500/level, paired item by item with that run (3,500 ids, 0 question or gold mismatches).
**Command:** `scripts/pod/codi_stab_arm.sh` via `scripts/pod/launch_stab_arm.sh` with the section 12.1 flags (`ARM_EXTRA="--rule_gate True" ARM_NAME=gpt2_l1to7w_startlast_gated ARM_SLUG=v2-l1to7w-startlast-gated-depth2`), `scripts/pod/pair_watcher.py` on the laptop under `caffeinate -is`; `eval_command.txt`. Leak check before launch: `scripts/check_rule_gate.py`.
**Headline results:**
- **Test, exact:** L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.982 (9 wrong). Ungated: 1.000 / 0.998 / 0.476 / 0.308 / 0.158 / 0.120 / 0.072.
- **Primary, pooled L5-L6 paired gain, gated minus ungated:** +0.861, 95% CI [+0.840, +0.882], discordant 861/0, exact McNemar p 1.3e-259.
- **By level:** L2 +0.002 (1/0), L3 +0.524 (262/0), L4 +0.692 (346/0), L5 +0.842 (421/0), L6 +0.880 (440/0), L7 +0.910 (455/0). The ungated model is right on no item that the gated model gets wrong.
- **Selection:** checkpoint-17820, best of the last 3 on valid (0.993 / 0.996 / 0.997 mean over levels).
- **Valid by epoch, L1-L7:** epoch 5 .96 / .80 / .57 / .32 / .20 / .16 / .09; epoch 6 .97 / .91 / .92 / .86 / .82 / .79 / .19; epoch 8 1.00 / .99 / .99 / .98 / .98 / .97 / .89; from epoch 9 at least .99 on L1-L6.
- **Mid-run checks on valid (laptop, teacher-forced answer token, not rerun on the selected checkpoint):** at epoch 6, one pass short of a level's last pass gives .01 / .00 / .02 / .01 / .06 at L2-L6 against .90 / .92 / .86 / .82 / .80 with it. At epoch 10 (checkpoint-14850), one pass short gives L5 .07 and L6 .08 against .99 and 1.00; gate off at eval gives L5 .02; on edited items (two rules swapped, or a new start value) the answer follows the new chain .99-1.00 of the time and never keeps the old answer under a rule swap. None of the 2,000 valid questions appear in train.
- **Out of range:** see the canonical record (L8-L12): the model outputs the answer of exactly the rules the gate shows it.

**Interpretation:**
- By section 12.3 this is **Rollout**: gain at least 0.05 with p < 0.05, by a wide margin. With the same model, data, recipe and 12-epoch budget, the gated model solves L5-L7 where ungated CODI scores .07-.16. So this budget is enough to run a rollout through 6 latents; ungated training does not find one.
- Through L3 and beyond, any accuracy above floor must pass through the latents, because the gate leaves no other route to the early rules (a solver missing one rule scores about 6%). The latents therefore carry a running value across at least five passes.
- The protocol's correction at epoch 6 said six passes cover only L6 and L7 can get through only the upper layers of the last pass. L7 reaches .982, so that route works almost fully.
- Section 12.3 also asks whether the shortfall at L2-L4 is the price of the gate: at the selected checkpoint there is none (L1-L2 1.000 against 1.000 / 0.998).
- This does not show that rollouts emerge on their own. The gate supplies the schedule and also removes every other route, so routing and blocking are bundled.

**Gotchas hit:** None in training: the watchdog never fired, the max gradient norm was 37.7 (step 10430), and the loss fell from 1.19 (epoch 1 mean) to 0.11 (epoch 12). First LR check passed (3.36e-5 at step 10). The pod could not get a self-terminate limit (runpodctl has no flag here, and self-deletion from the pod was blocked), so the laptop watcher was the only shutdown path.
**Caveats:** One seed. No CODI-0 arm, by design: under this gate it can apply only the last rule. The reference is ungated CODI, which differs only in the gate. The mid-run checks are on valid at earlier checkpoints and use the teacher-forced answer token. A forced rollout is a diagnostic, not a natural result. GPT-2 small and CODI only.
**Next:** Pre-registered: the shuffled-gate control, then the decoder control (probes as `b23` at every latent site, L3-L6), which is reported either way and is free on the laptop. Under discussion as an alternative to the shuffled gate: a partial gate that keeps per-pass routing but leaves the other routes open, to separate routing from blocking.

## 2026-11-07 — Rule-gated start-last CODI on the canonical L1-L12 test: L1-L7 as the main record, L8-L12 at floor because the gate hides their middle rules, and the output is the answer of the visible rules on 97-99% of items (codi, run_id: 20261107-204918_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-gated-depth2-codi-canonical)

**Goal:** Secondary check on L8-L12 (TRAINING_PROTOCOL sections 10.3 and 12). Under the gate these levels cannot be solved by construction: six passes see rules 1-6, the answer tokens see the last rule, and rules 7 to L-1 are seen by nothing.
**Mechanism / model:** As 20261107-204814 (rule-gated start-last CODI, checkpoint-17820).
**Data:** `synthetic_data_v2_startlast`: canonical L1-L12 test, 500/level, start value after the rules. L1-L7 items are the main record's, item for item.
**Command:** `scripts/pod/codi_stab_arm.sh`; `eval_command.txt`. The visible-rules check ran on the laptop from `predictions.jsonl`: simulate each chain from the question text (0 gold mismatches), applying only rules 1-6 and the last rule.
**Headline results:**
- **Test, exact:** L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.982, L8 0.006, L9 0.104, L10 0.014, L11 0.032, L12 0.014; overall 0.596. Ungated CODI on L8-L12: .054 / .038 / .036 / .010 / .018.
- **Visible-rules answer:** applying rules 1-6 and then the last rule gives the gold answer on .004 / .104 / .014 / .032 / .014 of L8-L12 items, matching accuracy at every level. The model outputs that visible-rules answer on .988 / .986 / .982 / .968 / .982 of items.
- **Teacher (written CoT, same weights):** L8-L12 .652 / .236 / .116 / .046 / .036.

**Interpretation:**
- L9's .104 is not a leak: on about 10% of L9 items the two hidden rules (7 and 8) cancel, for example halve then double, so the visible rules give the gold answer.
- The model computes exactly the chain the gate shows it, even on levels it never trained on, extended past 6 rules only by the answer tokens' last rule. This is out-of-distribution evidence that its latents run the gated chain rule by rule.

**Gotchas hit:** None.
**Caveats:** One seed. Out of range by construction, so accuracy here says nothing about reach. The visible-rules check is behavioural, not a probe of the latents.
**Next:** None for this record.

## 2026-11-07 — Decoder control on rule-gated CODI: every intermediate value reads 1.00 from its own latent, by linear probe and by an untrained logit lens, in a two-site staircase; ungated CODI reads at control except the value before the last rule (codi, run_id: 20261107-211610_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-gated-decoder-control)

**Goal:** RQ2 decoder control, pre-registered in TRAINING_PROTOCOL section 12.3 and reported either way. The gated model carries a known rollout (20261107-204814). Can the decoders used on ungated CODI read it? If they can, ungated CODI's late-only profile (20261107-084635) is an absence of a rollout, not a decoder failure.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2, 6 latents. Rule-gated start-last CODI checkpoint-17820 with the gate on, as in training; ungated start-last CODI checkpoint-17820 as the comparison. fp32, MPS.
**Data:** Valid only, L3-L6, 286 / 286 / 286 / 285 items. Probes fit on 8,000 train items of one level (seed 20), plus a 4,000 fit and a shuffled-label fit. `predictions.jsonl` holds, per model and item, the step values, the answer, and the probe and logit-lens reads of v_j from z_j.
**Command:** `codi_audit_artifacts/b27_gated_decoder.py`, tables from `a29_gated_decoder.py`, under `run_guarded.sh` and `caffeinate -dims`; record from `record6.py`. Sites: t1 (`<bot>`), h1-h6 (pass s = h{s+1}, input z_s), colon; layers 0, 2, 4, 8, 12. Probes as `b23`. Logit lens: final LayerNorm, then the LM head on the 100 number tokens, all 13 layers. Headline cells, fixed in the script before any read: v_j at z_j (h{j+1} layer 0) and at h{j} layer 12, j = 1 to L-1.
**Headline results:**
- **Checks.** The collector matches `eval_codi.encode_and_think` exactly (max latent difference 0, same answers, gate on and off). Answers: gated 1.000 at L3-L6; ungated .521 / .329 / .136 / .123, with right counts 149 / 94 / 39 as in `b23`. Calibration: ungated value before the last rule at h4 layer 2 reads .49 / .21 / .12 at L3-L5, as `b23`.
- **Gated, headline cells.** Every v_j at every level reads 1.00 from z_j, by probe and by logit lens, and 1.00 at h{j} layer 12. Shuffled labels .00-.05. The 4,000 fit already reads 1.00.
- **Gated, logit-lens grid.** Each v_j reads about 1.00 at exactly two sites, h{j} (the pass that read rule j) and h{j+1} (whose input is z_j), and .01-.14 at every other latent site. The answer reads 1.00 at the colon. At intermediate layers the colon also reads the value before the last rule (.33-.38).
- **Gated, probe grid.** Same staircase, but later sites keep earlier values in part (L6: v_1 .18-.43 at h5-h6). v_0 reads 1.00 almost everywhere, since every pass sees the start value.
- **Negative control.** One step ahead of its rule, v_j reads .18-.34, at or below a guess from the exact previous value (.22-.38): halving an even value, for example, needs no constant. Two or more steps ahead, at most .05 (mean .02-.03).
- **Ungated.** Probe reads of v_1 to v_{L-2} at z_j are .03-.22, near shuffled (.01-.04), and saturation is not the limit. The logit lens reads intermediates at .01-.07, except the value before the last rule (.06-.15). The colon reads the answer at about accuracy (.52 / .33 / .14 / .12).

**Interpretation:**
- The decoders are not blind. When a rollout exists, a linear probe reads every step perfectly from its own latent, and so does the untrained logit lens. So ungated CODI's late-only profile is an absence of a rollout, not something these decoders missed.
- In the gated model each latent is in effect a number token: v_j decodes from z_j through the unembedding with no training. A monitor would need no probe here.
- This latent is used as well as readable. Under the gate, z_j is the only route from rules 1 to j to the answer, and edited items follow the new chain (20261107-204814). So readable and used coincide at every site. That is the "readable and used" cell of the draft's grid, though forced by design.
- Paper framing (link 2, use to readable): when computation is forced through the latents one step per pass, it is fully readable. The open question is link 1: plain training does not route computation this way.

**Gotchas hit:** None. My pre-set negative control included one-step-ahead cells, which a value-only guess can partly solve. They are split out above, with a baseline that knows the previous value.
**Caveats:** One seed per model, valid only. The state is one integer from 0 to 99, so a perfect read is weak evidence that richer latent computation would be readable. The gate forces the bottleneck, so this does not show what a naturally emerging rollout would look like. The headline cells are fixed, but the grids report the best layer per site, which leans slightly high. No per-latent patching yet: use is argued from the gate's construction and the edited-item test, not from swapping single z_j.
**Next:** A per-latent causal test on the gated model: swap z_j from a donor with a different v_j and check that the answer follows the donor's chain from rule j+1. This is cheap on the Mac. The paid control (shuffled or partial gate) awaits the team's decision.

## 2026-11-07 — Per-latent swap on rule-gated CODI: every latent z_1..z_{L-1} decides the answer alone (follows the donor .98-1.00, mean ablation to chance); latents after z_{L-1} are idle, though a probe reads the value in them (codi, run_id: 20261107-214950_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-gated-latent-swap)

**Goal:** The decoder control (20261107-211610) found every step readable from its own latent. Is each latent also used, tested one latent at a time rather than argued from the gate? And which latents are idle?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2, 6 latents. Rule-gated start-last CODI checkpoint-17820, gate on. fp32, MPS.
**Data:** Valid L3-L7, 286 / 286 / 286 / 285 / 285 items; scored pairs use recipients answered right, n = 279-286 per cell. Mean latents from 2,000 train items per level (seed 21).
**Command:** `codi_audit_artifacts/b28_gated_swap.py` under `run_guarded.sh` and `caffeinate -dims`; record from `record7.py`. Swap: replace the input latent z_j (j = 1-5) with a same-level donor's z_j. k = min(j, L-1) is the step z_j carries. Donor: first in a seeded shuffle with a different v_k whose predicted answer (the recipient's rules k+1 to L applied to the donor's v_k) is in 0-99 and differs from the recipient's gold. Mean ablation: z_j set to its train mean, which is the draft's necessity measure.
**Headline results:**
- **Checks.** Patching an item's own z_j back in leaves every answer unchanged (smoke run). Clean accuracy 1.000 at L3-L6, .979 at L7.
- **z_1 to z_{L-1}, the latents that carry the chain:** follows donor 1.000 at every position at L3-L6, and .982-.993 at L7. Keeps own .000 everywhere. Mean ablation leaves .024-.063 (chance).
- **z_L to z_5, after the chain (L3: z_3-z_5; L4: z_4, z_5; L5: z_5):** follows donor .000, keeps own 1.000, mean-ablated accuracy 1.000.
- **"Donor answer"** (.00-.15) only counts items where the predicted answer happens to equal the donor's own answer, so it is not a separate route.
- **Route.** The answer reads v_{L-1} from the pass whose input is z_{L-1}, the first pass after the last rule-reading pass. At L6 and L7 that is the last pass, so all of z_1-z_5 are used.

**Interpretation:**
- In the gated model, readable and used coincide one latent at a time for z_1 to z_{L-1}: each latent alone decides the answer from its step onward, and no other route to its value exists.
- Latents after z_{L-1} are idle. Swapping or ablating them changes nothing, yet the linear probe reads v_{L-1} from them at 1.00 (20261107-211610). The logit lens reads values only at the sites in use. So in this model a probe-based monitor would report values the model does not use, while the logit lens tracks use.
- Against ungated start-last CODI, single latents follow the donor .00-.01 there (20261106-105634), because its latents are near copies. Single-latent tests therefore cannot show reliance in that model, but here they can.

**Gotchas hit:** The Mac went to sleep on battery mid-run (pmset: sleep at 13:36 and 13:38), so the run took about 30 minutes instead of about 5. It saves after each level, and results are unaffected.
**Caveats:** One seed, valid only. The swap moves the whole latent, not a value direction, so this does not show which features in z_j carry the value. Pairs are restricted to items the model got right with an in-range predicted answer.
**Next:** On ungated start-last CODI below reach, swap all latents from a different-value donor against mean ablation, to separate content reliance from format damage at L1-L2. On this model, block the route in use and test whether the idle latents can stand in as a backup.

## 2026-11-07 — Ungated start-last CODI, content reliance: at L1 latents are ignored (donor latents keep 1.000, same-level mean keeps 1.000); from L2, below reach, the answer follows the latents' content (.994); the earlier ".09 at k=1" was a pooled-mean artefact (codi, run_id: 20261107-220408_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-content-reliance)

**Goal:** Separate reliance on latent content from damage done by an off-distribution latent. 20261106-105537 found all latents mean-ablated take k=1 from 1.00 to .09, though CODI-0 needs no latents there, which contradicts the draft's prediction that reliance starts at d50 = 3.
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2. Start-last CODI checkpoint-17820 (20261106-083843), ungated, 6 latents. fp32, MPS.
**Data:** Canonical test L1-L7, 500/level. Recipients: items the model answers right. Means come from train: 2,000 per level for the same-level mean, 500 per level over L1-L7 for the pooled mean (seed 21).
**Command:** `codi_audit_artifacts/b29_ungated_resample.py` and `b29b_pooled_mean.py` under `run_guarded.sh` and `caffeinate -dims`; record from `record8.py`. All six latent inputs are replaced at once, because single latents are near copies. Different-value donor: same level, a different v_{L-1}, predicted answer = the recipient's last rule applied to the donor's v_{L-1} (in 0-99 and != gold). Same-value donor: same level, same v_{L-1}. Identity patch keeps every answer (smoke).
**Headline results:**

| Level | Clean | Diff donor: follows / keeps own (n) | Same-value donor keeps own | Same-level mean | Pooled mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | 1.000 | .000 / 1.000 (500) | 1.000 | 1.000 | .092 |
| L2 | .998 | .994 / .002 (499) | 1.000 | .042 | .056 |
| L3 | .476 | .374 / .017 (238) | .616 | .026 | .036 |
| L4 | .306 | .275 / .033 (153) | .423 | .038 | – |
| L5 | .160 | .150 / .025 (80) | .325 | .040 | – |
| L6 | .116 | .034 / .017 (58) | .193 | .020 | – |
| L7 | .076 | .105 / .079 (38) | .105 | .034 | – |

Mean columns give accuracy on all items. At L1, z_0's same-level mean has cosine .39 with the pooled mean; at L2-L3 the cosine is .96-.97.

**Interpretation:**
- **L1: latents not relied on.** The answer keeps its own value whatever the latents hold, and the depth-matched mean (the draft's own N_j definition) changes nothing. The .09 in 20261106-105537 came from its pooled mean: L1 latents differ from those of longer chains, and a mean dominated by L4-L7 breaks the model. That is format damage, not reliance.
- **L2: relied on, though not needed.** Donor latents move 99.4% of answers to the donor's value, and the same-value control keeps 1.000. Yet CODI-0 scores .98 at L2 with no latents. Reliance starts at k = 2, the first level with an intermediate value to carry, one level below d50 = 3. The latent gain starts at k = 3 (+.02 at k = 2, +.24 at k = 3; 20261106-083843).
- **L3 and up: relied on, and not a clean carrier.** Donor latents change almost every answer (keeps own .02-.08), but only .37 / .28 / .15 follow the donor's v_{L-1}, and same-value donors keep only .62 / .42 / .33. The latents carry more than v_{L-1}, or carry it imprecisely, which fits the partial reads in 20261107-084635.
- **For the draft:** "reliance near zero below d50" holds at k = 1 and fails at k = 2. Need and use separate by one level, and only content tests show it: mean ablation pooled over depth wrongly puts reliance at k = 1.

**Gotchas hit:** The pooled mean in 20261106-105537 did not follow the draft's per-depth definition (its gotcha line flagged this for the Coconut record and said the CODI ablations shared it). A correction is appended to that record.
**Caveats:** One seed, one checkpoint. Few right recipients at L5-L7 (80 / 58 / 38). Target "follows donor" assumes the latents carry v_{L-1}; at L3 and up they carry something less clean. Recipients are items answered right, which are easier.
**Next:** Run the same test on any new arm, including a latent-only gate (prefill ungated, each latent pass shown one rule), to see whether reliance still starts at k = 2.

## 2026-11-07 — Rule-gated CODI, idle latents are not a backup: hiding the pass the answer reads leaves .08-.21, hiding everything but the idle passes leaves chance, though a probe reads v_{L-1} from them at 1.00 (codi, run_id: 20261107-220408_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-gated-idle-backup)

**Goal:** Idle latents (after z_{L-1}) are ignored under swap and mean ablation (20261107-214950), yet a linear probe reads v_{L-1} from them at 1.00 (20261107-211610). Are they a working backup the model can fall back on, or inert?
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2. Rule-gated start-last CODI checkpoint-17820, gate on. fp32, MPS.
**Data:** Valid L3-L5 (levels with idle passes), 286 per level.
**Command:** `codi_audit_artifacts/b30_gated_backup.py` under `run_guarded.sh` and `caffeinate -dims`; record from `record8.py`. Only the answer tokens' attention to latent passes changes.
**Headline results (exact, L3 / L4 / L5):**
- Clean: 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000.
- Hide the pass the answer reads (input z_{L-1}): .206 / .108 / .084.
- Hide passes 0 to L-1, leaving only the idle passes: .038 / .042 / .028.
- Hide only the idle passes (control): 1.000 / 1.000 / 1.000.
- Hide every latent pass (floor): .028 / .021 / .010.

**Interpretation:**
- The idle passes are inert. With every other route hidden, the answer cannot use them, so a probe's 1.00 read there is a value the model neither uses nor can fall back on. For a monitor this is a pure false alarm. The logit lens does not read these sites.
- The residual .08-.21 after hiding the pass in use most likely comes from the pass before it, which computed v_{L-1} in its upper layers (inferred, not tested).

**Gotchas hit:** None.
**Caveats:** One seed, valid only. Blocking attention removes the route entirely; this does not test whether brief retraining would make the idle latents usable.
**Next:** None for this model.

## 2026-11-07 — SIM-CODI on start-last RuleChain: test L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.998; pooled L2-L7 gain over start-last CODI +0.644 (1933/0), over CODI-0 +0.743; primary passed, latent use not yet tested (codi, run_id: 20261107-225603_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-sim-depth2-codi)

**Goal:** Pre-registered test (TRAINING_PROTOCOL section 13): with the start value after the rules, does a step decoder on each latent (SIM-CoT on CODI) give a readable, used trace and more depth than start-last CODI? Primary: pooled L2-L7 paired gain over start-last CODI (20261106-083843).
**Mechanism / model:** `codi`, gpt2, num_latent 6, RunPod A40, 12 epochs, section 10.2 recipe unchanged (lr 2e-3 cosine, adam_beta2 0.98, adam_epsilon 1e-6, max_grad_norm 1.0, LoRA r128/a32, 64 x 2, bf16, seed 11), plus `--step_decoder True`: a separate fp32 GPT-2 reads latent z_j as a one-position prefix and writes teacher step j+1 (`<<a op b=c>>` + EOS), teacher-forced, decoder lr 1e-4, loss factor 1.0, training only (patch `scripts/codi_step_decoder.patch`). `n_params` 268,939,008 counts the decoder; the answer path has 144,499,200 as before.
**Data:** `synthetic_data_v2_l1to7w_startlast`, as the start-last pair. Test = canonical L1-L7, 500/level, paired item by item with start-last CODI and CODI-0. No valid or test question appears in train (exact-match check, 0/2000 and 0/3500).

Paired tests from the three `predictions.jsonl` files.
**Headline results:**
- **Test, exact:** L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.998; overall 0.9997. Teacher-forced identical. d50 beyond range (no level below 50%).
- **Primary, against start-last CODI (exact McNemar):** pooled L2-L7 **+0.644, 1933/0, p < 1e-300**. By level: L2 +0.002 (1/0), L3 +0.524 (262/0), L4 +0.692 (346/0), L5 +0.842 (421/0), L6 +0.880 (440/0), L7 +0.926 (463/0). No item that CODI solved is lost.
- **Secondary, against start-last CODI-0:** pooled L2-L7 +0.743 (2230/0); L2 +0.020 (10/0, p 0.002), L3 +0.768, L4 +0.864, L5 +0.920, L6 +0.944, L7 +0.944.
- **Selection:** checkpoint-16335 (valid 0.999, tied with 17820). Valid by epoch: 0.216, 0.340, 0.503, 0.596, 0.674, 0.824, 0.966, 0.984, 0.994, 0.997, 0.999, 0.999. Start-last CODI ended at 0.456.
- **Training:** student CE by epoch .68, .50, .42, .36, .31, .25, .12, .06, .03, .010, .005 (start-last CODI .69 to .42); explain loss 8.8 at step 0, median .48 in epoch 1, about 1e-4 per latent by epoch 11.

**Interpretation:** Primary passed by a wide margin: the step decoder turns start-last CODI's L3-L7 .48-.07 into .998-1.000 with the answer path, data and recipe unchanged. This matches rule-gated start-last CODI (20261107-204814, L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.982) without a gate. It is not yet an outcome-table row: "Trace used, steps, gain" needs the ablation, donor, pass-sweep and probe checks of section 13.3, and "readable trace, answers ignore latents" is not ruled out by accuracy alone, although start-last CODI already depends on its latents. A low explain loss shows the latents carry each step's operands, since the decoder cannot see the question; it does not show they carry the result, which the decoder could compute from `<<a op b=`.
**Gotchas hit:** Pod smoke gate passed (explain loss 7.81 to 1.89 in 20 steps, optimizer groups [(98, .002), (4, .002), (50, 1e-4), (98, 1e-4)], peak 42.5 GB). First LR check passed (3.36e-5 at step 10). Gradient norm 71.7 at the first logged step, in warmup; median 1.26 in epoch 0 with 84% of logged steps above the 1.0 clip, then medians .83, .69, .64, .60, .60, .74, .60, .51, .31, .06 with 3-19% above 1. So clipping was active mostly in epoch 0 and partly in epochs 6-8. The norm includes the decoder, so it is not comparable with start-last CODI's .07-.22. Watchdog never fired (`GRAD_MAX` 500). The laptop slept about 21:13-21:46 UTC on battery; training on the pod was unaffected.
**Caveats:** One seed. Not bit-matched to start-last CODI: LoRA, `prj` and new token rows are built before `set_seed`, and the dropout stream diverges; data order matches. At this size the gain cannot be a seed effect (1933/0), but a second seed is still needed before quoting per-level numbers as stable. The step loss could also improve the ordinary pass, so a gain alone does not show that the latents do the work (section 13.3 table, last row).
**Next:** Section 13.3 secondaries on checkpoint-16335: `ablate_latents_rulechain_codi.py`, donor and same-value donor patches, the pass sweep (`b22_passes.py`), `b19_trend.py`, `b23`-style frozen linear probes for every step at every latent, and decoded value plus last rule against the model's own errors (few errors exist: 1 on test). Then the table's next step.

## 2026-11-07 — SIM-CODI start-last on the canonical L1-L12 test: L1-L7 as the main record, L8 0.006; out of range it mostly applies rules 1-6 plus the last rule (65% at L8, falling to 16% at L12) (codi, run_id: 20261107-225709_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-sim-depth2-codi-canonical)

**Goal:** Secondary check on L8-L12, levels this model never trained on (TRAINING_PROTOCOL sections 11.2 and 13).
**Mechanism / model:** As 20261107-225603 (SIM-CODI, start-last, checkpoint-16335).
**Data:** `synthetic_data_v2_startlast`: canonical L1-L12 test, 500/level, start value after the rules. L1-L7 items are the main record's, item for item.
**Command:** `scripts/pod/codi_stab_arm.sh`; `eval_command.txt`. The rule-subset check ran on the laptop from `predictions.jsonl`: parse each chain from the question (`parse_chain_question`, 0 gold mismatches), then for every split "first k rules + last m rules" ask whether the prediction equals that subset's final value.
**Headline results:**
- **Test, exact:** L1-L6 1.000, L7 0.998, L8 0.006, L9 0.070, L10 0.014, L11 0.014, L12 0.030; overall 0.594, d50 7.22, AUC 0.602. Start-last CODI on L8-L12: .054, .038, .036, .010, .018. The CoT teacher in the same model: L8 .622, L9 .356, L10 .186, L11 .082, L12 .086.

Unlike the gated model it does this less cleanly and less often as chains grow, and a third of L8 answers instead stop after rule 7. Behavioural evidence only; the latent ablation, donor and probe checks on the main record test it directly.

## 2026-11-07 — SIM-CODI start-last uses its latents one step per pass: swapping z_1..z_{L-2} makes the answer follow the donor's next value (.993-1.000), mean ablation to chance, pass sweep needs L-1 passes, probes show a staircase. Smokes: identity patch keeps every answer (s1); collector latents equal `encode_and_think` (max diff 0, s2).
**Headline results:**
- **Swap, one latent at a time** (recipients answered right; donor same level, different v_{j+1}; predicted answer = the recipient's remaining rules on the donor's v_{j+1}). z_1..z_{L-2}: follows donor .993-1.000 at every level, keeps own .000. z_0: follows .82 (L2), .66, .66, .61, .62, .56 (L7), keeps own .01-.03; the rest match neither the donor's start value run through the recipient's rules (about .10, chance) nor any other simple alternative tried.

- **Pass sweep** (answer after k passes, trained with 6): with k = L-1 passes (one per trained step) L2 .56, L3 .80, L4 .97, L5 .96, L6 .98, L7 1.00; with k = L every level L2-L6 is 1.000; with fewer than L-1, chance (L7 .00 at k = 5). Start-last CODI plateaus after k = 2 at every level (b22). Extra passes keep L1-L6 at 1.000; L7 drops to .02-.06 at k >= 7.
- **Probes, exact (shuffled-label control .00-.05, mode share .03-.05).** Pre-registered cells: v_k at its trained latent z_{k-1} .78-.86 at L3-L6; at the state it is projected from (t1 or h{k-1}, layer 12) .50-.82. Not pre-registered, same grid: v_k at the next latent z_k .97-1.00 at every k and level. Logit lens at the latents .02-.07 (gated CODI 1.00, ungated .00-.15): the values are linear but not number-token embeddings. The answer v_L reads .30-.55 at the latents and 1.00 at the answer colon.
- **Not run:** `b19_trend.py` (epoch trend); the model's own wrong answers (1 error on test, 2 on valid: nothing to test).

**Interpretation:** By the section 13.3 table this is **trace used, steps, gain over start-last CODI** ("forced rollout adds real depth"). Each latent decides the answer alone, different latents hold different steps, and level L needs L-1 passes (one per trained step, plus one more for full accuracy below L7), which start-last CODI never showed. What a latent holds matches the decoder's step text: z_j carries the operand v_j almost perfectly (.97-1.00) and the result v_{j+1} at about .8 by a linear probe, while the swap shows v_{j+1} is fully set by z_j. So the latent holds the step `<<v_j op b =`, the next pass computes the result, and the next latent carries it as its operand. Readings of the decoded trace are faithful in the causal sense used here: change what the latent says and the answer changes as the trace predicts. The untrained latent after the last step carries v_{L-1} (probe 1.00 at L6) and the answer tokens apply the last rule, as the out-of-range pattern in 20261107-225709 showed. z_0 is only partly a clean carrier: it is computed from the question, and a third of its swaps end elsewhere.
**Gotchas hit:** The checkpoint includes decoder weights; `load_state_dict(strict=False)` drops them because the local CODI has no `step_decoder` field, and the clean run confirms the answer path is unchanged.
**Caveats:** One seed, valid only (test is reserved for the main record). The "next latent" probe cell was read after the pre-registered cells, so it is post hoc, though it sits in the pre-registered grid. Teacher-forced decoding is not used here; probes are frozen and linear. Mean ablation is the draft's necessity measure, and the swap is the stronger test. The step loss could also have improved the ordinary single pass, but the pass sweep rules that out as the source of the gain: with fewer passes than steps accuracy is at chance.
**Next:** As the table says: start-first SIM-CODI, then a step-supervision control with no latents. Optional: swap the untrained z_{L-1} to see whether it holds v_{L-1} or the answer; trace why L7 fails at k >= 7 (a guess, not tested: the extra pass applies rule 7 and the answer tokens apply it again).

## 2026-11-08 — Readable is not used, with ground truth: probes read idle latents at 1.00 in gated and SIM (13 of 48 cells readable but unused), the logit lens misses 14 of 18 used SIM cells, and plain CODI has no single latent that is readable or used (24 of 24 neither) though all six together are needed (codi, run_id: 20261108-012524_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-readable-vs-used)

**Goal:** HANDOFF_2026-11-07 step 1 (paper F5, draft Figure 4). For every model x level x latent, is the value the latent carries readable by a decoder, is the latent used by the answer, and where do the two disagree? Use comes from swaps and ablations, so this measures decoder faithfulness against ground truth.
**Mechanism / model:** three start-last GPT-2 CODI models, 6 latents, same data / recipe / seed 11: plain CODI (`20261106-083843`), rule-gated CODI with the gate on in every forward (`20261107-204814`), SIM-CODI checkpoint-16335 loaded without its step decoder (`20261107-225603`).
**Data:** `synthetic_data_v2_l1to7w_startlast` **valid** L3-L6 (286/286/286/285), all three models, 3,429 rows (model x item). Means from 2,000 train items of the same level (seed 21), never pooled. The plain all-six comparison (b29) is on **test**.
**Command:** On the laptop (MPS, float32, `run_guarded.sh`, `caffeinate`), in `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/codi_audit_artifacts`: `MODEL={plain,gated,sim} t1_single_use.py` (one script for handoff 1a/1b/1c: single-latent swap and same-level mean ablation of every z_0..z_5, plus b30's hide conditions at L3-L5 for all three models), `t1_table.py` (joins with the read side: `b27_gated_decoder.json` for gated / plain, `s2_sim_probe.json` for SIM; output `t1_table.md`, `t1_table.json`), `record9.py`. Smokes (L4, 40 items): identity patch keeps every answer, all three models. Reproduction: every overlapping answer array equals b28 (44 arrays), s1 (42) and b30 (gated hide, 12): 0 differ.
**Definitions (fixed before compiling, `t_predictions.md`):** value read kr: gated and SIM min(j, L-1) (SIM z_j holds the operand v_j); plain L-1. Swap moves ks: gated min(j, L-1), with j = 0 the start value; SIM min(j+1, L-1); plain L-1. Donor: same level, seeded shuffle `Random(1000 L + j)` as b28 / s1, differs at v_ks, predicted answer (recipient's rules after ks on the donor's v_ks) in 0..99 and != gold; recipients answered right.
*Readable* = probe exact >= .5 at site h{j+1}, best of layers 0/2/4/8/12 (selected on the scored items, slightly high), with the shuffled-label probe at that layer <= .06. *Used* = swap follows the donor >= .5, or <= .5 of the clean-right items stay right under mean ablation.
**One deviation, made before compiling, after seeing the plain L3-L5 log lines:** the handoff's "mean ablation leaves accuracy <= .5" marks every plain latent used, because plain's clean accuracy is .52 / .33 / .14 / .12 at L3-L6. It is now relative to the items answered right. Nothing changes where clean is ~1 (gated, SIM).

**Headline results** (24 cells per model, L3-L6 x z_0..z_5):

| Model | Decoder | Readable + used | Readable, not used | Used, not readable | Neither |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain | probe (best-of or layer 0) / lens | 0 | 0 | 0 | 24 |
| gated | probe, best-of or layer 0 | 17 | **7** | 0 | 0 |
| gated | logit lens | 17 | 1 | 0 | 6 |
| SIM | probe, best-of or layer 0 | 17 (+1 edge) | **6** | 1 (edge) | 0 |
| SIM | logit lens | 4 | 0 | **14** | 6 |

L3 (at plain CODI-0's d50 = 3) and L4-L6 (past it) have the same pattern. The table has no below-reach level.
- **Probes read unused latents perfectly.** Gated idle latents z_L..z_5 (6 cells) and SIM idle latents z_L..z_5 (6 cells): probe 1.00 (layer 0 .62-1.00), single swap keeps own 1.000 and follows .000, mean ablation 1.000. Hiding every pass except the idle ones leaves chance: gated .03-.04, SIM .01-.04. The latents carry the right value, and nothing reads it.
- **The logit lens fails both ways.** In gated it is the more faithful decoder: 1.00 on every used step latent and .04-.10 on idle ones, so it does not read the decorative cells. Its only "readable, not used" cell is gated z_0 at L3. In SIM it reads the operand latents at .16-.29 although they are used at .99-1.00 (14 "used, not readable" cells). It reads z_{L-1} at .85-.88.
- **Plain CODI: no single latent is readable or used.** Single swaps follow .00-.08 and keep own .49-.96 (the rest end elsewhere). After single mean ablations .74-.97 of right items stay right. The probe reads v_{L-1} at <= .49 at L3, falling to <= .10 at L6, and the lens at <= .15. Yet all six together are needed: on test, same-level mean ablation of all six drops accuracy to .02-.04, and all-six donors are followed .37 / .28 / .15 / .03 at L3-L6 (b29). Hiding all passes but the "idle" ones leaves clean accuracy (.54 / .32 / .15): in plain the later passes are copies that substitute for each other, not idle.
- **1a, SIM after the last trained step.** The first untrained latent z_{L-1} is **fully used** on swap: follows .997-1.000 at L3-L6, although mean ablation leaves .08 / .19 / .37 / .72. It holds v_{L-1}, not the answer: the donor's own answer comes out only .09-.15, and the probe reads v_{L-1} at 1.00. So the answer tokens apply the last rule, which also settles handoff step 5's first check. z_L..z_5 are inert, as in gated. Hiding only the pass whose input is z_{L-1} leaves .77 / .97 / .96 in SIM, against .21 / .11 / .08 in gated. When that pass is hidden, SIM finds v_{L-1} in the passes before it; idle passes alone give chance.
- **1c, gated z_0 (start value).** Swap follows .49 / .57 / .64 / .60 and keeps own .15-.23. Mean ablation leaves .99-1.00. Probe 1.00, lens .97-.98. A donor's z_0 redirects the answer most of the time, while an uninformative z_0 costs nothing: the passes fall back on the start value in the question tail. It is "used" by the swap rule at L4-L6 and just below at L3 (.486).
- **Swap and mean ablation disagree in exactly two places.** Gated z_0 (swap .49-.64, ablation harmless) and SIM z_{L-1} (swap 1.00, ablation .08-.72). In both, a second copy of the value exists (question tail, earlier passes), so mean ablation underestimates use.

**Predictions (written 16:00 PST before any output, `t_predictions.md`):**
- *Idle latents inert, as in gated:* right.
- *z_{L-1} "partly used":* wrong for the swap (fully used). Right that mean ablation is partial.
- *Plain single swaps follow <= .05:* .00-.08, one cell above .05 (L5 z_1, .077, n = 39). Single ablations cheap: right.
- *Gated z_0 may be ignored:* half right. Ablation is harmless, but a donor's z_0 is followed about .6 of the time.
- *SIM lens misses used latents:* right.

**Interpretation:** This makes F5 a complete ground-truth table. A linear probe reading a value at ~1.00 says nothing about whether the model uses that latent: 13 of the 48 gated and SIM cells are readable and unused, with use measured by swaps rather than inferred. A latent monitor built on probes would report a faithful trace at positions the answer ignores (Lanham-style unfaithfulness, the "decorative" kind). The untrained logit lens has the opposite failure. It is faithful in gated, where values sit in number-token directions, and blind to most used SIM latents, where they do not. So no single decoder is faithful across methods without a causal check. Plain CODI is the third case: use is spread over near-copies, and no decoder reads the value from any one of them. A per-latent table there would call every latent "neither" although the model depends on the set. Group-level tests (b29) are the right unit for CODI.
**Gotchas hit:** (1) The absolute mean-ablation threshold breaks on a model with clean accuracy below .5; changed before compiling, see above. (2) SIM L5 z_4 is a threshold edge. The probe reads 1.00 at every layer, and the shuffled control is 18/286 = .063 at layer 0, the first of the tied best layers, against .049-.052 at layers 2 and 4. By the fixed rule it is "used, not readable". Under section 14's readable rule (>= .30 above shuffled) it is readable + used, and no other cell in the table changes under section 14's definitions. (3) In the first wait loop a zsh glob with no match ended the loop, not the run.
**Caveats:** One seed per model; valid only, except the b29 comparison (test). Best-of over layers is selected on the scored items, but layer 0 alone gives the same counts. Plain cells at L5-L6 rest on 35-39 recipients. The swap is a single-site intervention: "not used" means this latent alone does not carry the value to the answer, which for plain is redundancy, not absence. The probes are frozen linear ridge probes from b27 / s2 (8,000-item fit); a non-linear decoder could read more in plain, but that would only add cells to "readable", not "used".
**Next:** Handoff step 2 (SIM all-latent donors, test L1-L7) and step 3 (dynamics figure) are running in the same session. Optional: hide passes L-1..5 in SIM to confirm that pass L-2 supplies v_{L-1} when pass L-1 is hidden (not run).

## 2026-11-08 — Content reliance in SIM-CODI matches plain CODI's split: latents ignored at L1 (all-six donors followed .000, mean ablation 1.000), relied on from L2 (follows .998-1.000, mean ablation to .01-.02), so reliance does not track need in either method (codi, run_id: 20261108-013131_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-sim-content-reliance)

**Goal:** HANDOFF_2026-11-07 step 2 (paper F2, "reliance does not track need", across methods). Does SIM-CODI, like plain start-last CODI (`20261107-220408_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-content-reliance`), ignore its latents at L1 and rely on their content from L2, below reach? Start-last CODI-0 solves L2 at .98 with no latents.
**Mechanism / model:** SIM-CODI start-last, checkpoint-16335 (`20261107-225603`), loaded without its step decoder (answer path unchanged; clean test L1-L6 1.000, L7 .998 as the pod eval).
**Data:** canonical **test** L1-L7, 500 per level (499 recipients at L7), to match the plain record row by row. Means: 2,000 train items of the same level (seed 21).
**Command:** On the laptop (MPS, float32, `run_guarded.sh`, `caffeinate`): `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/codi_audit_artifacts/t2_sim_resample.py`, a copy of `b29_ungated_resample.py` with only the checkpoint and output names changed (diff checked); record `record10.py`. Smoke (L2, 40 items): identity (patching an item's own six latents back) keeps every answer.
**Design (b29's):** all six latent inputs replaced at once. Different-value donor: same level, differs at v_{L-1}, predicted answer = the recipient's last rule on the donor's v_{L-1}, in 0..99 and != gold. Same-value donor: same v_{L-1}, a different start value where possible (format control). Mean: each z_s set to its same-level train mean. Recipients: answered right.

**Headline results** (SIM-CODI vs plain CODI from b29, same test items and donor seeds):

| L | SIM clean | SIM diff donor: follows / keeps / donor's answer | SIM same-value donor keeps (different start share) | SIM mean acc | plain clean | plain follows / keeps | plain same keeps | plain mean acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.000 | .000 / 1.000 / .012 | 1.000 (0.00; at L1 v_{L-1} is the start value) | 1.000 | 1.000 | .000 / 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| 2 | 1.000 | **.998** / .000 / .142 | .998 (1.00) | .022 | .998 | .994 / .002 | 1.000 | .044 |
| 3 | 1.000 | 1.000 / .000 / .118 | 1.000 (1.00) | .020 | .476 | .374 / .017 | .616 | .032 |
| 4 | 1.000 | 1.000 / .000 / .120 | 1.000 (1.00) | .016 | .306 | .275 / .033 | .423 | .038 |
| 5 | 1.000 | 1.000 / .000 / .108 | 1.000 (1.00) | .024 | .160 | .150 / .025 | .325 | .040 |
| 6 | 1.000 | 1.000 / .000 / .130 | 1.000 (1.00) | .022 | .116 | .034 / .017 | .193 | .020 |
| 7 | .998 | 1.000 / .000 / .120 | 1.000 (1.00) | .012 | .076 | .105 / .079 | .105 | .034 |

- **L1: latents ignored, in both methods.** A donor's six latents (different start value) never move the answer (.000 follows, 1.000 keeps own), and all-six mean ablation leaves 1.000. The answer tokens apply the single rule to the start value in the question.
- **L2 and up: content reliance, in both methods.** SIM follows the donor .998-1.000 at every level L2-L7. A same-value donor with a different start value keeps the answer (.998-1.000), so what the latents pass on is the value v_{L-1}, not format or the start value. Mean ablation drops to chance (.012-.024). The donor's own answer comes out only .11-.14: the answer tokens apply the recipient's last rule to the donor's value.
- At L3+ plain CODI's clean accuracy is low, and its "follows" is bounded by it. SIM shows the same reliance at full accuracy.

**Predictions (`t_predictions.md`, written before any output):** "L2+ follows near 1.0, same-value donor keeps ~1.0, mean ablation to chance from L2": right. "L1 the open cell, guess follows partly (.3-.9)": **wrong**, L1 ignores the latents completely.
**Interpretation:** F2 now holds across two methods. Both models depend on latent content at L2, where the same backbone without latents (CODI-0) already scores .98, and both ignore the latents at L1. So reliance follows the training setup, not the depth the task needs. The boundary sits at the same place despite very different training signals (no step labels vs a step decoder on every latent). For SIM, reliance from L2 is partly imposed: the step loss trains z_0 to carry v_1 at L2. But L1 has no trained step, and there SIM, like plain, lets the answer tokens do the one rule themselves. This connects to step 1 (`20261108-012524`): at L3+ SIM's first untrained latent z_{L-1} is fully used on swap, but at L1 the same position (z_0 = z_{L-1}) is not. The answer reads a carried value only when a pass before it had a rule to apply.
**Gotchas hit:** none. At L1 the same-value control is trivial (same v_0 = same start value, share 0.00 different), as in b29.
**Caveats:** One seed; test split (as the plain row), so this record is not on valid like steps 1 and 3. All-six swaps cannot tell which latent carries the value (step 1 does that per latent on valid). Plain's L3+ rows rest on 38-238 recipients.
**Next:** Handoff step 3 (dynamics) is logged with this; step 4 (formation over epochs) and step 5's second check (L7 with 7+ passes) remain.

## 2026-11-08 — Latent dynamics: plain CODI reaches a fixed point after two passes (relative step .01-.03 from t = 2, consecutive latents centred cos .98-1.00), while gated and SIM take large near-orthogonal steps through the pass the answer reads, then stop (gated at once, SIM over 2-3 passes) (codi, run_id: 20261108-013131_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-latent-dynamics)

**Goal:** HANDOFF_2026-11-07 step 3. Show plain CODI's attractor (2607.09698 calls CODI "a stable attractor" from geometry alone) next to the gated and SIM staircases, in geometric terms, for the three models whose latent use is known from swaps (`20261108-012524`).
**Mechanism / model:** plain start-last CODI checkpoint-17820 (`20261106-083843`), rule-gated with the gate on (`20261107-204814`), SIM-CODI checkpoint-16335 without its decoder (`20261107-225603`).
**Data:** `synthetic_data_v2_l1to7w_startlast` **valid** L3-L6 (286/286/286/285) per model, the items of step 1. Clean accuracy here equals step 1's answers item by item (checked in the collector): plain .52 / .33 / .14 / .12, gated 1.00, SIM 1.00 / 1.00 / 1.00 / .996.
**Command:** On the laptop (MPS, float32, `run_guarded.sh`, `caffeinate`), in `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/codi_audit_artifacts`: `t3_dynamics.py` (collector, CODI venv; per-item metrics in `t3_dynamics.json`), `t3_plot.py` (figure, repo env: `t3_dynamics_z.{png,pdf}`, `t3_dynamics_h.{png,pdf}`; medians in `t3_medians_{z,h}.md`), `record11.py`. Smoke: plain L4, 40 items, answers match t1.
**Metrics:** two trajectories per item, t = 0..6: z_t = prj(h_t), the latent inputs (z_0 from `<bot>`; z_6 is computed but never read), and h_t, the last-layer states before prj. D_t = x_{t+1} - x_t, the output of pass t minus its input. Per item: step size ||D_t||; relative step ||D_t|| / ||x_t||; turning cos(D_t, D_{t-1}); centred consecutive cosine cos(x_t - mu, x_{t+1} - mu), with mu the mean over the level's items and positions 0..5; sensitivity surrogate log(||D_t|| / ||D_{t-1}||). These are the quantities the handoff lists for 2607.09698's Eqs. 1-3; I did not check them against the paper's text.

**Headline results** (z trajectory, medians over items; relative step at t = 0..5):

| L | plain | gated | SIM |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | .70 .11 .03 .01 .01 .01 | .82 .87 **1.07** .09 .01 .01 | 1.32 1.30 **1.01** .49 .10 .02 |
| 4 | .63 .09 .02 .01 .01 .01 | .85 .88 .87 **1.07** .09 .01 | 1.34 1.32 1.28 **.93** .51 .14 |
| 5 | .57 .10 .02 .01 .01 .01 | .85 .87 .85 .89 **1.06** .10 | 1.33 1.32 1.32 1.27 **.88** .49 |
| 6 | .54 .09 .02 .01 .01 .01 | .82 .85 .88 .85 .85 **1.05** | 1.27 1.33 1.26 1.31 1.23 **.68** |

(bold: t = L-1, the output of the pass whose input z_{L-1} the answer uses.)
- **Plain: a fixed point after two passes, at every level.** The relative step falls from .54-.70 to about .10 at t = 1 and .02-.03 at t = 2, then .01. Consecutive latents have centred cos .98-.99 at t = 1 and .999-1.000 from t = 2. Turning goes to .9-1.0 as the steps shrink along one direction. Accuracy plateaus after 2 passes too (`20261106-101740`).
- **Gated: equal large steps while rules are read, one larger step out of the used pass, then stop.** Relative step .82-.89 for t <= L-2, 1.05-1.07 at t = L-1, then .09-.10 and .01. During the rollout consecutive latents are near orthogonal (centred cos -.04 to .36) and turning sits at -.5. That is the value expected for steps between roughly independent states of equal norm. The idle latents after the used pass are near copies (centred cos .98-1.00): the probe-readable but unused cells of step 1.
- **SIM: the same staircase with larger steps and a slower stop.** Relative step 1.23-1.34 for t <= L-2, .68-1.01 at t = L-1, then decaying over 2-3 passes (L3: .49, .10, .02). Centred cos -.10 to .17 during the rollout, rising to .56-.99 after it.
- **h (last-layer states before prj):** the same picture. Plain's step falls over t = 0..2 (relative .84-.87, .37-.50, .08-.10), gated and SIM stay at 1.1-1.5 until t = L-1, then drop. The sensitivity surrogate dips for plain at t = 2 (log ratio -1.4 to -1.8) and stays near 0 for gated and SIM during the rollout.

**Predictions (`t_predictions.md`, written before any output):**
- *Plain contracts to near-zero step size after pass 2:* right.
- *Gated and SIM keep large steps through the last rule-reading pass (t = L-2), then drop:* off by one. Large steps continue through t = L-1, the output of the pass the answer reads. Gated drops at once after it; SIM decays over 2-3 passes.
- *Turning low during the rollout, high for plain after the fixed point:* right (-.5 vs .9-1.0).

The figure's reference line marks t = L-1. It was moved there after seeing the data; the pre-registered reference was t = L-2. Said in the plot script's docstring.
**Interpretation:** The geometry separates the two regimes as the swaps do. Plain CODI's latents converge after two passes to a point and stay there, which is 2607.09698's attractor description. Step 1 shows what that means causally: the six latents become near copies that no single swap moves, and only the set matters. Gated and SIM move far each pass, to nearly unrelated states, for exactly as many passes as there are rules to read plus the pass the answer reads. Each of those states is used (step 1). After that both settle into a fixed point too, but a different one: idle latents, readable and unused. So "a fixed point" in the latent geometry does not mean the latents are unused or used. Plain's fixed point is used as a set, gated's and SIM's idle fixed points are not used at all, and the geometry alone does not tell them apart.
**Gotchas hit:** Calibration against the earlier collapse statistic (`20261106-101740`, plain, test: consecutive centred cos .58, .97, .99, .996): ours from t = 1 matches (.98, .999, 1.000). At t = 0 ours is .07-.29 against .58; the earlier centring set (levels, positions, split) is not the same as here, and I did not reconcile the two.
**Caveats:** One seed per model; valid only. Plain's medians include its many wrong items (clean .12-.52); restricting to right items was not done. The step size depends on the norm, which differs by model (SIM's latents move about 1.5x more in relative terms), so compare the shapes across models, not the levels. Descriptive geometry; the causal claims come from step 1.
**Next:** Optional handoff step 4 (does the staircase form before, with, or after the epoch 5-7 accuracy jump?) and step 5's second check (L7 with 7+ passes). Figures for the draft: `codi_audit_artifacts/t3_dynamics_z.pdf` (main), `t3_dynamics_h.pdf` (appendix).

**Candidates (fixed before the full run):** gold; last rule twice r7(r7(v_6)); three times; r7(r_j(v_6)) for j = 1..6 (the extra pass applies rule j, then the answer applies rule 7); v_6. Share = fraction of items matching; unique = matching only that candidate.

**Headline results (L7):**

| k | gold | r7(r6(v_6)) | r7(r7(v_6)) (handoff guess) | other r7(r_j(v_6)) | none | post hoc: r7(r6^(k-6)(v_6)) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | **.996** | .004 | .000 | .000-.004 | .004 | - |
| 7 | .021 | **.877** (unique .565) | .091 | .074-.091 | .084 | .877 |
| 8 | .056 | .133 | .032 | .014-.021 | .698 | **.495** |
| 9 | .025 | .109 | .025 | .021-.046 | .733 | **.305** |

- **The 7th pass applies rule 6 again.** At k = 7 the answer is rule 7 applied to rule 6 applied to v_6 on .877 of items. The handoff's guess (rule 7 twice) matches .091, at the level of the other wrong-rule candidates, which share values with the correct one by coincidence. Unique matches: r7(r6(v_6)) .565, gold .018, every other candidate <= .007.
- **Post hoc (chosen after seeing k = 7):** each further pass applies rule 6 once more. Rule 6 twice then rule 7 matches .495 at k = 8; three times, .305 at k = 9. The share falls as errors compound.
- **L6 control:** gold .996 at every k = 6..9, answers identical across k. At L6 the 7th and later passes come after the last trained step, are idle (step 1: inert), and change nothing.

**Predictions (`t_predictions.md`):** "rule 7 twice, the majority at k = 7": **wrong** (.091). "L6 stays at gold": right.
**Interpretation:** SIM-CODI's passes map to rules by position, and the map saturates at the last position seen in training. Pass s applies rule s+1 for s = 0..5; an untrained pass 6 applies rule 6 again, the rule of the last trained pass position. At L7 the step chain has no room left: z_6 carries v_6, the extra pass applies rule 6 to it, and the answer tokens apply rule 7 to the result. At L6 and below, the pass after the last step is idle (no rule to read), so extra passes are harmless. So the rollout is a position-indexed program, not a "find the next unread rule" procedure, and its length is bounded by training. This fits the out-of-range pattern in `20261107-225709` (out of range it mostly applies rules 1-6 plus the last rule).
**Gotchas hit:** The smoke floor of .98 failed on 39/40 (a known single error); relaxed to .95 after checking the error equals s1's.
**Caveats:** One seed; valid only. The k = 8 and 9 test is post hoc. Candidates can coincide on an item, which is why unique shares are given. Only rule 6's repetition was tested, not what an extra pass does at L <= 5 (idle there by step 1).
**Next:** Handoff step 4 (rollout formation over epochs) is the only one left, optional.

## 2026-11-08 — Start-last CODI's latent passes are parallel noisy copies that the answer averages: donor swaps follow the number of donor passes, not their position (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 of passes 1-5: follows .01 / .05 / .45 / .75 / .88), mixed swaps give in-between answers (.78-.86, chance .2), later passes overwrite a donor's early latents, and any single pass alone gives .61-.76 exact but .84-.95 within 2 (codi, run_id: 20261108-032531_codi_v2-l1to7w-startlast-prefix-suffix-pooling)

**Goal:** Understand how start-last CODI (`20261106-083843`, the one unforced model with a matched gain past reach) uses its latents. Earlier records established two working passes, then a fixed point (`20261106-101740`), a look-back to earlier passes that a relay lacks, and that single latents never move the answer. Open: do later passes build on earlier latents (a chain), and how does the answer combine six near-copies?
**Mechanism / model:** start-last CODI checkpoint-17820, 6 latents, ungated.
**Data:** the b16 pairs on canonical **test** (`FORMAT=startlast`, seeds 61/16, 200 items per level L2-L7). A diff pair is an item plus a copy with one taken constant changed (gold moves >= 6). Kept: both answered right, 424 diff pairs (249 with the edit 1+ rules before the last).
**Command:** On the laptop (MPS, float32, `run_guarded.sh`, `caffeinate`): `~/Documents/Penn/CIS5980/codi_audit_artifacts/t6_prefix_hide.py`, a copy of `scripts/codi_null_audit/b16_donor.py` with new conditions; tables `t6_table.py` (`t6_table.md`); record `record13.py`. The own-latent control left every answer unchanged. The `all` and `suffix_s` rows reproduce `b16_raw_startlast.json` (`20261106-105634`): .97 / .88 / .56 / .03 for suffix from z_1..z_4, one rule left.
**Conditions:** prefix_s puts the donor's z_0..z_{s-1} in and recomputes the later latents from them (a chaining test). suffix_s puts the donor's z_s..z_5 in. hide_ge_s / only_s cut the answer tokens' attention to latent passes >= s, or to all but pass s, with clean latents (which passes the answer reads). Pass t is the pass whose input is z_t.

**Headline results:**
- **Later passes overwrite a donor's early latents.** One rule left (n = 178): prefix_1, _2, _3 follow .00 / .00 / .02 and keep the recipient's answer .99 / .92 / .63. Only with four or five donor latents does the donor win (.46, .85). A chain would carry an early change forward; here each pass's output is re-derived mostly from the question.
- **The answer follows the number of donor passes, not their position.** Edits 1+ rules before the last (n = 249), donor-input passes among passes 1-5:

| Donor passes | Condition | Follows donor | Keeps own | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (pass 1) | prefix_2 | .01 | .83 | .16 |
| 2 (passes 4-5) / (1-2) | suffix_4 / prefix_3 | .06 / .04 | .44 / .53 | .51 / .43 |
| 3 (3-5) / (1-3) | suffix_3 / prefix_4 | .49 / .41 | .04 / .08 | .47 / .51 |
| 4 (2-5) / (1-4) | suffix_2 / prefix_5 | .76 / .73 | .02 / .02 | .21 / .24 |
| 5 (1-5) | suffix_1 | .88 | .01 | .11 |

  Early and late passes count the same: prefix and suffix swaps with the same count agree within .08.
- **Mixed swaps give in-between answers.** When the answer is neither the donor's nor the recipient's, it lies strictly between the two .78-.86 of the time, against .18-.22 for a uniform guess. The answer averages the values the passes hold.
- **Pass 0 (input z_0 from `<bot>`) is not read; any one later pass carries most of it.** With only pass 0 visible, accuracy is .05-.11 (chance). With one pass s = 1..5 alone, recipients stay right .61-.76 at L3-L5, and within 2 .84-.95. Seeing passes 0-4 gives .95-1.00 (hide_ge_5). Each pass holds a noisy copy, and pooling makes it exact.
- **No-model re-analysis of saved runs (same session, before t6):**
  - b29's all-six donors (test, `20261107-220408`): the answer follows the donor's v_{L-1} exactly .37 / .27 / .15 at L3-L5, but within 2 .82 / .59 / .44. With donors the model gets right: exact .47 / .43, within 2 .91 / .86 at L3-L4.
  - b21's look-back block (`20261106-101740`) by level: answers changed .30 / .31 / .23 / .21 / .20 at L2-L6, accuracy .997 to .699 at L2, then net -.07, -.03, -.01, .00. Blocking only the previous latent changes .00-.11 with no accuracy cost.

**Predictions (`t_predictions.md`, written before t6 output):**
- *Prefix follows near the 'all' rate by s = 2-3:* **wrong**. Prefixes are overwritten until four or five passes are swapped.
- *hide_ge_3 near clean:* right at L2 (1.00), partly at L3-L5 (.74-.84).
- *One pass alone keeps much of the accuracy:* right (.61-.76).
- *only_0 worse:* right (chance).

**Interpretation:** Start-last CODI does not chain. Its passes 1-5 each compute a noisy estimate of the value before the last rule, mostly from the question; the look-back to earlier passes feeds into that estimate. The answer pools the passes, close to an average: swapped-in donor passes pull the answer by their number, and a split gives a value in between. This explains:
- why single swaps never move the answer (one vote in five);
- why mean-ablating all six is fatal while ablating one is not;
- why the model stops improving after two or three passes (more copies only reduce noise);
- why its errors are mostly near-misses (`20261105-074801`).

The latents add precision by averaging, on top of the one or two hops the look-back carries. For monitoring, the value is in no single latent; it is a population code across passes.
**Gotchas hit:** None in the script. hide rows count recipients once per item (diff pairs share recipients).
**Caveats:**
- One seed. Test split (the b16 pairs).
- Edits 2+ rules before the last rest on 44 and 16 pairs.
- "Averages" is a description of in-between answers and count dependence, not a fitted model of the readout.
- In prefix swaps the donor passes still attend to the clean question, so "overwritten" means the question dominates a pass's output, not that the input is ignored.
**Next:** Partial-information probes in the same session (`20261108-032531_..._partial-probes`): is the value held as a magnitude with a noisy ones digit?
